title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. Across all three benchmarks, we found that increasing the thinking effort does not increase decision quality in a statistically meaningful way. The same change in thinking effort raises stated confidence at a statistically significant level, so extra thinking buys confidence rather than correctness. We also measure the calibration of these models (how well their reported confidence percentage matches their true correctness percentage) in these tasks and show that most models are not well-calibrated at every effort level. We also find that errors are strongly shared: when one model errs in a task, several others tend to err on that same task. Furthermore, on tasks where several models all err, a large number of them pick the same wrong product.

title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
abstract: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.

title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
abstract: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence. Our key insight is that a bias obscured in one feature space may be clearer in another. In this work, we propose CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus. CHORD aggregates aggregates within-class partitions in each view, which is a proxy for specifying candidate biases, to debias the target representation and classifier without bias supervision. Experiments on seven benchmarks across vision, language, speech, and medical imaging show consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/davelee-uestc/chord_debiasing_public .

title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
abstract: High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. We formulate this setting as Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a task that jointly refines spatial and temporal resolution while predicting future high-resolution trajectories. To this end, we propose a framework that decomposes prediction into spatial and temporal stages using a shared pretrained backbone, fixed numerical scaffolds, and lightweight residual heads. For backbone adaptation, we introduce PROLA (PRincipal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation), which allocates a fixed low-rank budget between pretrained weights' principal directions and their orthogonal complement. PROLA further rescales rank-1 optimizer updates using gradient signals, improving adaptation without increasing trainable rank. Experiments in the PSWD setting show that PROLA outperforms representative low-rank adaptation baselines. Further experiments across diverse datasets and tasks support the broader applicability of PROLA, showing that its benefits extend beyond the primary weather downscaling setting.

title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
abstract: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful candidate artifacts exist, but selection is no better than random at telling them from harmful ones, so errors accumulate across rounds. At the method level (ranking methods), typical margins of a few percentage points are smaller than the difference between two independent runs of the same method, so published rankings often rest on luck. Together, these findings indicate that agent evolution is often bottlenecked by reliably identifying improvements. This calls for a shift in how we develop and evaluate self-improving agents, from designing ever more candidate improvement systems to making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
abstract: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. We construct ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K for two-stage training. Contrastive supervised fine-tuning teaches when and how to respond, while reinforcement learning with Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment (BACA) combines trajectory-level and local advantages to refine decisions, responses, and silence across multi-turn interactions. We also introduce FSI-Bench to evaluate feedback seeking and subsequent task completion. ALIVE achieves the highest overall scores among the compared models on four public benchmarks and FSI-Bench, demonstrating strong streaming understanding and interactive capabilities.

title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
abstract: Flow-based generative models are trained on a hand-chosen prediction target, such as the velocity, the noise, or the clean data. This choice strongly affects training and sample quality. We introduce Anisotropic Flow Models (AnisoFlow), which replaces a fixed prediction target with a fully learnable one. AnisoFlow learns to scale the noise component of the target anisotropically, assigning a separate nonnegative weight to each direction in a jointly learned basis. A closed-form map recovers the velocity from the network's prediction, leaving the architecture, flow-matching loss, and sampler unchanged. Since recovery is exact, training optimizes the target purely to make it easier for the network to predict. We theoretically analyze the resulting prediction error and predict that the preferred noise weight in each direction scales near-linearly with data variance, in agreement with the weights learned empirically in pixel space. AnisoFlow improves FID from 1.90 to 1.55 over the JiT baseline on ImageNet 256times256, by learning only the prediction target, without representation alignment or architectural changes. In pixel-space text-to-image generation, AnisoFlow improves image quality and, through better-conditioned velocity recovery, largely removes patch-seam artifacts under reduced-precision inference.

title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head. Unlike previous methods, where the denoising output leads to final pixels, DWD separates the two roles: the original denoising head continues to drive sampling, then the new DWD head predicts the pixels at the final step. We extend pretrained latent models with DWD efficiently by finetuning only the last few transformer blocks, training the DWD head with pixel quality losses while anchoring the denoising head to the pretrained model to preserve the sample trajectory. Across latent image and video generators, DWD removes the decoder and reduces inference cost while maintaining or even improving pixel quality. On Wan video generation, it visibly reduces detail distortion and flickering, lowering warping error by 23%. Remarkably, the same separation also improves pixel diffusion models that do not even use a decoder: a final-step DWD head produces substantially better texture detail in text-to-image generation, and improves ImageNet FID from 1.55 to 1.43, a new state of the art among pixel flow models.

title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
abstract: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide strong representations for downstream classification tasks. Yet adapting a TSFM under changing operating conditions remains challenging. A model must improve on each newly observed condition without sacrificing conditions it has already learned, often from only a small labeled calibration set and without knowing the operating condition at inference time. We find that this difficulty has an important geometric structure. Under an operating-condition shift, the embedding space of a TSFM does not move uniformly: some local regions change substantially, while others remain nearly unchanged. Consequently, a global adaptation can unnecessarily move embeddings that were already correctly classified. To address this, we propose the novel PACT (Piecewise Adaptation via Chart Transport). PACT partitions the frozen source embedding space into local charts and learns lightweight residual transports for the regions affected by each new condition. An explicit identity path is always retained, and a learned gate softly selects among the identity and accumulated transports for each input. The pretrained TSFM encoder, classifier head, and previously learned transports remain fixed. With only 5% labeled calibration data per arriving condition and no condition identity at test time, PACT maintains an average macro-F1 above 0.95 across a four-condition bearing-fault stream. Under homogeneous tasks and label spaces, similar retention-adaptation behavior is observed across public benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Sachithx/PACT.

title: Rotatiridoid, a rare iridoid from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen and its anti-inflammatory activity
abstract: A rare iridoid featuring an unusual 3-O-8 bridged ether bond, named rotatiridoid (1), was obtained from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen, along with five known analogues. Its structure was established by means of HRESIMS, 1D and 2D NMR experiments, and ECD calculations. When evaluated in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, compound 1 displayed anti-inflammatory activity, suppressing the production of pro-inflammatory mediators such as NO and ROS at 7.5 μM.

title: Phenolic profile and biological activities of ultrasound-assisted aqueous-ethanolic extracts of Tamarix hispida Willd
abstract: Tamarix hispida Willd. (Tamarisk; locally known as “zhyngyl” in Kazakh) is a halophyte traditionally used for dysentery, rheumatism, and ulcers, with reported antioxidant and prolyl endopeptidase-inhibitory activities. This study investigated the phenolic profiles and biological activities of 10%, 50%, and 70% aqueous-ethanolic extracts (THU-10, THU-50, and THU-70) obtained by ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE). Phenolic constituents were analyzed by HPLC-DAD, and antioxidant, enzyme inhibitory, anti-inflammatory, and cytotoxic activities were evaluated. Eleven phenolic compounds, including rutin, gallic acid, epicatechin, fisetin, and p-hydroxybenzaldehyde were identified, where rutin was the predominant quantified phenolic compound, reaching 2.78, 3.88, and 4.42 mg/g in THU-10, THU-50, and THU-70, respectively. THU-10 showed the strongest antioxidant activity in the ABTS and DPPH assays (IC50 = 2.13 ± 0.75 and 6.01 ± 0.30 µg/mL, respectively) and the strongest AChE and BChE inhibition (IC50 = 21.90 ± 0.70 and 38.71 ± 0.19 µg/mL, respectively). The extracts also inhibited α-amylase, α-glucosidase, and pancreatic lipase. THU-70 exhibited the strongest anti-inflammatory activity (IC50 = 18.4 ± 0.2 µg/mL). In the BSLA, the tested extracts showed no activity and were considered non-cytotoxic. UAE reduced extraction time from 48 h to 25 min and increased extract yield 3–4-fold. Overall, solvent composition significantly influenced the phenolic profiles and biological activities of T. hispida extracts.

title: Short-form video and microlearning in English language education: A bibliometric and science mapping review
abstract: Short-form video platforms, particularly TikTok, have altered how second language learners encounter and process linguistic input. Individual studies have examined specific aspects of microlearning in second language contexts, yet, to the authors' knowledge, no bibliometric analysis has mapped the intellectual structure of this emerging subfield. This study maps the publication landscape, thematic clusters, and research gaps characterizing microlearning research in English language education through short-form video platforms. We conducted a hybrid bibliometric analysis of 80 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2004 and 2026. Performance analysis was performed using Biblioshiny (R), and science mapping was executed through VOSviewer. The bibliometric outputs were then interpreted through a qualitative synthesis using the Theory, Context, Characteristics, and Methodology framework. Three principal patterns emerged. First, scholars from developing Asian economies, including Malaysia, Hong Kong, China, and Indonesia, contributed the largest share of publications, whereas traditional Western academic centers produced comparatively fewer studies. Second, the thematic clusters concentrated on phonological production and vocabulary acquisition, with limited attention to academic writing or reading comprehension. Third, qualitative and experimental designs together accounted for approximately two-thirds of the corpus, while computational learning analytics appeared only peripherally in the keyword co-occurrence network. This bibliometric review maps the knowledge structure of a rapidly expanding subfield at the intersection of educational technology and applied linguistics. The findings point to a need for longitudinal experimental designs, methodological diversification toward learning analytics, and empirical investigation of how algorithmic recommendation systems mediate L2 input delivery.

title: Extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, and product development of oridonin: a review
abstract: Isodon rubescens (I. rubescens), a plant of the family Lamiaceae, is the dried aerial part of I. rubescens (Hemsl.) Hara. It has the effects of clearing heat and detoxifying, relieving pain, promoting blood circulation, and reducing swelling. As a highly valued traditional Chinese medicine, it contains a variety of chemical components. Among them, oridonin (ORI) exhibits antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties, garnering significant attention in pharmacological research. Furthermore, ORI serves as a crucial quality control marker for I. rubescens. It can exert biological effects on the nervous, cardiovascular, and visceral organ systems via multiple signaling pathways, thereby conferring potential therapeutic value for related diseases. To improve the efficacy and safety of its applications and ensure that the isolated monomer compounds exhibit high purity and favorable stability, the extraction and purification processes have been optimized. Synthetic ORI-derived products exhibit anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activities, which are widely used as dietary supplements and functional beverages in daily life. Therefore, this paper reviews the source, extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, derivatives, content determination, toxicity and product applications of ORI. This has updated and deepened the understanding of ORI, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for its further research.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

title: Adaptive Gyroscopic Leadership Model: Integrating Planned and Generative Orientations in Principal Leadership Preparation
abstract: School principal leadership increasingly operates within contexts characterized by ambiguity, uncertainty, disruption, accountability pressures, and rapid social and technological change. Traditional approaches to principal leadership often struggle to prepare aspiring leaders for the interpretive, relational, and adaptive demands of contemporary practice. This theoretical paper examines the reconceptualization of principal leadership preparation through the integration of planned and generative orientations in organizational development. Drawing on these perspectives, this paper introduces the Adaptive Gyroscopic Leadership Model (AGLM) as a conceptual framework for understanding how leadership preparation programs can cultivate the capacity to maintain purposeful direction while responding to changing environments. The AGLM conceptualizes leadership preparation through five interdependent components: core commitments, sustained learning momentum, planned learning structures, generative learning structures, and contextual forces. Their continuous interaction provides a framework for creating learning conditions intended to support candidates’ professional judgment and adaptive capacity. This paper presents the redesign of a public university’s Educational Leadership program as an illustrative application of the AGLM. Specifically, program elements related to coursework and clinical practice, assessment, and learning support are mapped onto the framework. The paper contributes to educational leadership scholarship by offering a theoretically grounded framework for designing principal leadership programs that develop adaptive and reflective leaders.

title: The Translation of Humour using AI tools for subtitling and dubbing: case study of Egyptian movie “Foul El-Seen Al-Azeem”
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated subtitling and dubbing in translating humour from Egyptian Arabic into English using the comedy film Foul El-Seen Al-Azeem as a case study. It employed a mixed-methods design combining qualitative analysis based on Martínez-Sierra’s humour taxonomy and Anstey and Bull’s multimodality theory with a quantitative evaluation using a modified Translation Quality Assessment (TQA) rubric and audience-based surveys. The study examined two Humorous scenes containing multilingual code-switching, including Egyptian Arabic, Chinese, French, English and Lebanese Arabic, to assess how AI tools manage linguistic complexity and cultural humour. title: A new acylated quercetin triglycoside with anti-inflammatory activity from the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida
abstract: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida led to the isolation of a previously undescribed acylated quercetin triglycoside (1), together with three known constituents (2–4). Their structures were established by HR-ESI-MS with 1D and 2D NMR analyses and, for the known compounds, by comparison with reported spectroscopic data. Compound 1 was elucidated as quercetin 3-O-[β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→3)]-[α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)]-[2-O-(E)-p-coumaroyl]-β-D-glucopyranoside. Compounds 1–3 inhibited lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 14.9 ± 1.7, 13.4 ± 2.6, and 37.7 ± 2.9 μM, respectively, while their CC50 values were >64 μM. 4 was cytotoxic (CC50 10.9 ± 0.7 μM) and was therefore not evaluated for nitric oxide inhibition. These findings expand the known chemical diversity of C. flavida var. flavida and identify 1 and 2 as moderate inhibitors of nitric oxide production.

abstract: A chemical investigation of the endophytic fungus Peroneutypa scoparia RJHH-3 led to the isolation of a new highly oxygenated pimarane diterpenoid, peroneutone A (1), together with three known analogues, scopararane C (2), libertellenone A (3), and 9α-hydroxyisopimara-8(14),15-dien-7-one (4). These findings expand the chemical and biological diversity of pimarane diterpenoids from P. scoparia.

title: Gastroprotective potential of Bixa orellana: A critical review of extract-specific phytochemistry and preclinical evidence
abstract: Peptic ulcer disease remains clinically important despite effective Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication and acid-suppressive therapy. Gastric injury reflects an imbalance between aggressive factors, including acid-pepsin activity, H. pylori, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), ethanol, oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and microvascular disturbance and protective mechanisms such as mucus-bicarbonate secretion, prostaglandin signaling, nitric oxide-regulated blood flow, epithelial restitution, and endogenous antioxidant defenses. Bixa orellana L. (annatto or achiote) is a tropical medicinal plant whose seed arils are rich in the apocarotenoids bixin and norbixin, whereas its leaves contain variable phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, terpenoids, alkaloids, and other constituents depending on geography, maturity, and extraction method. This critical narrative review uses a structured search and qualitative evidence-appraisal framework to evaluate extract-specific phytochemistry, direct gastric evidence, indirectly relevant gastrointestinal and vascular evidence, mechanistic plausibility, safety, quality control, and translational readiness. The available literature supports B. orellana as a biologically plausible preclinical mucosal-protective candidate, particularly for prevention of acute chemical injury; however, it does not establish clinical efficacy or chronic ulcer-healing activity. Confidence is limited by the small number of direct gastric studies, incomplete chemical characterization, inconsistent separation of leaf and seed evidence, limited dose-response testing, narrow model selection, and insufficient mechanistic and histological endpoints. Future studies should use authenticated plant material, voucher specimens, chromatographic fingerprints, quantitative markers, complementary prevention and healing models, acute and repeated-dose toxicology, mucus and prostaglandin measurements, oxidative and inflammatory biomarkers, and blinded histological scoring before human investigation is justified.

title: Cytotoxic isoprenoid flavonoids isolated from Sophora davidii
abstract: Five isoprenoid flavonoids (1–5) were isolated from Sophora davidii. Notably, the absolute configuration of compound 1 and the 13C NMR data of compound 4 are presented herein for the first time. The structures of all compounds were established by spectroscopic data analysis, including HR-ESI-MS, 1D NMR, and 2D NMR. Their absolute configurations were determined via theoretical calculations, including ECD and NMR chemical shift calculations. The cytotoxic effects of the isolated compounds on human HCT-116, MDA-MB-231, and BCPAP cells were evaluated using the MTT assay. Compounds 2, 3, and 5 exhibited cytotoxicity against all three cell lines, with IC50 values ranging from 10.28 μM to 19.34 μM.

title: New phenylpropanoids with antifungal and antioxidant activities from the essential oil of Ocimum gratissimum L.
abstract: One new lignan, ocigralignan A (1), and one new phenylpropanoid, 3-amino-1-(4-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl)propane-1, 2-diol (2), together with six known compounds (3–8) were isolated from the essential oil of Ocimum gratissimum L. The structures and absolute configurations of 1 and 2 were elucidated by spectroscopic methods, including 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy as well as ECD analysis. Most of the isolated compounds exhibited significant antifungal activities against Alternaria arborescens and Aspergillus flavus, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranging from 1 to 8 μg/mL. Notably, compound 8 displayed potent antifungal activity comparable to the positive control nystatin, with an MIC value of 1 μg/mL. Additionally, compounds 1 and 5 demonstrated considerable antioxidant activity, achieving DPPH radical scavenging rates of 85.17% and 96.51%, respectively, at a concentration of 1 mg/mL.

title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food innovation, biotechnology, functional foods, nutrigenomics, sustainability, food safety, culinary heritage

title: Future VLSI Architectures for Neuromorphic Computing, Edge AI and Sustainable Systems
abstract: The future of Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) architectures is being fundamentally reshaped by the intersecting demands of Neuromorphic computing, edge artificial intelligence (AI), and sustainable electronic systems. As traditional CMOS scaling nears its physical limitations, researchers are exploring bio-inspired Neuromorphic designs that mimic the brain's energy-efficient computing mechanisms using spiking neural networks (SNNs), as demonstrated by platforms like Intel’s Loihi and IBM’s True North (Davies et al., 2018; Merolla et al., 2014). In parallel, edge AI is driving the need for VLSI systems capable of performing high-speed, low-latency inference directly on-device, thus reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. Hardware accelerators such as Eyeriss and Google’s EdgeTPU offer promising solutions through energy-aware architecture and domain-specific design (Chen et al., 2019; Jouppi et al., 2017). These innovations are increasingly evaluated not just on performance, but also on ecological impact. Emerging sustainable VLSI solutions include non-volatile memory technologies like ReRAM and PCM, in memory computing approaches that reduce data movement, and eco-friendly materials like carbon nanotubes and organic semiconductors (Sebastian et al., 2020; Rajendran et al., 2020). However, despite significant advancements, challenges persist in fabrication scalability, algorithm-hardware co-design, and lifecycle sustainability assessment. This paper explores the synergetic evolution of these domains and highlights the critical need for interdisciplinary collaboration to develop future VLSI architectures that are intelligent, efficient, and environmentally responsible. The convergence of Neuromorphic computing, edge AI, and green hardware marks a paradigm shift, positioning VLSI not only as a medium for computation but as a cornerstone of sustainable technological progress.

title: Rreth disa sinonimeve në terminologjinë islame në gjuhën shqipe
abstract: Terminologjia islame si një nga fushat që është mishëruar në mendësinë shqiptare, e që filloi të depërtonte qysh herët në gjuhën shqipe, akoma nuk ka arritur të standardizohet. Sot gjejmë në përdorim forma të dysorëve e të tresorëve për nocione të njëjta, si: profet- pejgamber-i dërguar, Zot-Allah-Perëndi, engjëll-melaqe, xhenet-parajsë, xhehenem-skëterrë-ferr etj. Për shumë nocione islame përdoren fjalë e terma me prejardhje neolatine, të cilat kanë depërtuar me ardhjen e krishterimit. Çështja për diskutim është se sa nga termat e kësaj fushe mund të gjejnë barasvlerësit e tyre shqip, pa ua humbur kuptimin? Në këtë punim do të vështrojmë disa probleme që lidhen me sinonimin dhe me shqipërimin e disa nocioneve islame në gjuhën shqipe.

title: Modification of the Proximity Indexed Value Method Based on Distance-Based Normalization to Improve the Stability of Alternative Rankings
abstract: The Proximity Indexed Value (PIV) method provides a proximity-based mechanism for ranking alternatives in multi-criteria decision-making; however, its ranking results can be affected by the normalization process and the relative characteristics of criterion values. This study proposes a Distance-Based Proximity Indexed Value (D-PIV) method by incorporating distance-based normalization into the PIV framework to represent the proximity of alternatives to criterion-specific ideal conditions more explicitly. The proposed method was evaluated using an alternative location selection dataset comprising eight alternatives and six criteria, including one cost criterion and five benefit criteria. The evaluation included comparative ranking analysis using 36 systematic criterion-weight perturbation scenarios with changes of ±0.05, ±0.10, and ±0.15. The results show that D-PIV changes the ordering of Loc 3 and Loc 8 compared with conventional PIV, resulting in a ranking that fully corresponds to the reference ranking. The Spearman correlation increased from 0.9762 for PIV to 1.0000 for D-PIV. However, the sensitivity analysis indicates that the distance-based modification does not uniformly improve ranking stability across all alternatives. D-PIV increases the stability of Loc 8 from 69.44% to 72.22%, while lower stability is observed for Loc 3 and Loc 6 compared with PIV. These findings demonstrate that D-PIV contributes a reference-oriented normalization mechanism that improves baseline ranking consistency while redistributing, rather than uniformly eliminating, sensitivity to criterion-weight variations. The study therefore provides both a methodological contribution through the integration of distance-based normalization into PIV and an empirical contribution through systematic evidence of its effects on ranking agreement and stability.

title: HIVE Weighting: A Novel Heterogeneity-Aware Approach for Criteria Weighting in Multi-Criteria Decision Making
abstract: Objective criterion weighting plays an important role in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), particularly when decision outcomes depend on how differences among criteria are represented. However, conventional objective weighting approaches may emphasize specific statistical characteristics of the decision matrix without explicitly considering criterion heterogeneity as an integrated concept. This study proposes Heterogeneity-Informed Value Emphasis (HIVE) Weighting, a Heterogeneity-Informed Value Emphasis approach, for objective criterion weighting in MCDM. The method incorporates the mean, standard deviation, and relative variability of normalized criterion values to construct a heterogeneity-based measure of criterion importance. The resulting weights are then integrated with established MCDM methods to examine their applicability in alternative evaluation. A comparative analysis is conducted against Entropy, WENSLO, LOGSTA, CRITIC, and MEREC, followed by evaluations using the SAW and MOORA methods. Sensitivity analysis is further performed by varying criterion weights across multiple perturbation scenarios to examine the stability of the resulting rankings. The findings indicate that HIVE generates a more balanced representation of criterion importance than several comparative weighting approaches while preserving compatibility with different MCDM aggregation procedures. The ranking results obtained through SAW and MOORA show consistent patterns, while the sensitivity analysis indicates that the overall ranking structure is relatively stable under changes in criterion weights. These results demonstrate that HIVE provides an interpretable and flexible framework for incorporating criterion heterogeneity into objective weighting. The proposed approach offers a basis for further research on heterogeneity-aware weighting across diverse MCDM datasets and decision-making contexts, supporting more reliable and transparent weighting practices in complex decision environments.

title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.

title: CIVIL AND CRIMINAL LIABILITY OF DEEPFAKE AI PLATFORM PROVIDERS IN VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHT TO REPUTATION
abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced deepfake technology, which is capable of manipulating audiovisual data with high realism. While this technology offers creative utility, its misuse for synthesizing non-consensual pornography, political disinformation, and character assassination severely violates an individual’s right to reputation. This study examines the civil and criminal liabilities of AI deepfake platform providers under the Indonesian legal framework, specifically Law No. 1/2024 (Second Amendment to the ITE Law) and Law No. 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection (UU PDP). Using a socio-legal research method, this study analyzes how textual legal norms interact with the digital behavior of platform providers and the psychological and social vulnerabilities of victims. The results indicate a significant normative gap: current regulations primarily target the individual creators or distributors of deepfake content, while platform providers escape liability by hiding behind the "safe harbor" doctrine. Sociologically, this legal vacuum fosters a culture of impunity and exacerbates digital gender-based violence. This paper argues for a paradigm shift from passive moderation to active algorithmic accountability. Platform providers must be held civilly liable under Article 1365 of the Indonesian Civil Code for systemic negligence, and criminally liable under the corporate fault doctrine for failing to implement mandatory digital watermarking and proactive content filtration systems.

title: Reconstructing the Legal Enforcement Framework for Digital Activism in an Era of Technological Disruption
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed civic engagement by enabling digital activism as a powerful medium for public participation, social advocacy, and democratic expression. While these developments strengthen citizen engagement, they also create significant legal challenges in balancing freedom of expression with the need to maintain public order and prevent digital misconduct. This study reconstructs the legal enforcement framework governing digital activism in the era of technological disruption by identifying regulatory deficiencies, evaluating current enforcement practices, and proposing a more adaptive and rights-based legal model. The research employs a qualitative normative legal methodology complemented by a socio-legal perspective. It analyzes statutory regulations, legal doctrines, judicial decisions, and policy frameworks concerning digital expression and online activism. Data were collected through a systematic review of legal documents, scholarly literature, and policy reports, then examined using conceptual and comparative legal analysis to identify structural weaknesses within existing enforcement mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that current enforcement remains largely rooted in conventional regulatory paradigms that inadequately address the complexity of digital activism. Ambiguous legal provisions, overlapping institutional authorities, and inconsistent enforcement practices generate legal uncertainty and increase the risk of over-criminalizing legitimate civic expression. Furthermore, the absence of clear legal standards governing digital advocacy, online mobilization, and algorithm-driven information dissemination complicates effective enforcement and weakens legal certainty. This study proposes a reconstructed enforcement framework grounded in the principles of proportionality, transparency, accountability, and digital rights protection. The framework emphasizes adaptive regulation, integrated digital governance, institutional capacity building, and clearer legal standards for technology-mediated civic participation. By bridging technological realities with constitutional safeguards, the proposed model contributes to contemporary legal scholarship on digital governance while offering practical policy recommendations for developing a more balanced, accountable, and responsive legal system capable of addressing the evolving challenges of the digital era.

title: Evaluating Digital Technologies’ Economic and Environmental Effects on Compliance, Governance, and Privacy in Sustainable Environmental Management
abstract: The purpose of the study was to analyze new technologies impact on environment. The prospective benefits and challenges of new technologies on the use of technologies within environmental governance and compliance were uncovered in this study. Utilizing a convergence approach of qualitative and quantitative studies, the researchers sent out a survey to 9407 stakeholders within the environment, which included civil society, the private sector, and government. The study found out that the enforcement and reporting of compliance with environmental legislation would be greatly assisted by the streamlining of governance and compliance in the adoption of new technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT), The study also acknowledged the presence of other challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, expensive technologies, and poor technical capacity. The gaps and challenges on the governance of the environment, compliance, and sustainability would be solved by the introduced new technologies, which in turn would create a sustainable environment. This would lead to the development of Nigeria in an economically sustainable manner, while also providing overall environmental sustainability. The paper recommend that Nigeria's should increase her investment in the construction of training facilities within the administrative regulatory systems of new technological systems in environmental sustainability, collaborative Joint ventures should be encouraged so as to achieve economies and environmental sustainability.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Scenario-Based Validation for Agentic Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Validating agentic artificial intelligence systems that operate through long-horizon interaction with complex environments remains a fundamental and unresolved challenge. Contemporary validation practice relies heavily on scenario-based testing, benchmarking, and large-scale simulation, implicitly assuming that sufficient scenario coverage can approximate the system’s operational behavior. This paper challenges that assumption by framing validation as an inference problem under bounded information and analyzing its limits from an information-theoretic perspective. We formalize deployment behavior as a random variable over an expansive scenario space and characterize validation as the acquisition of finite information through observed interaction trajectories. Under minimal and realistic assumptions, we show that the entropy of the scenario space grows rapidly with interaction horizon, while the information obtainable through finite validation is strictly bounded. As a consequence, exhaustive scenario coverage and complete validation guarantees are, in general, information-theoretically impossible for agentic AI systems. We further demonstrate that empirical coverage metrics may diverge from epistemic certainty, leading to increasing apparent validation confidence without proportional reduction in residual uncertainty. To address these limits constructively, we identify conditions under which scope-limited, conditional guarantees remain attainable when validation is restricted to explicitly defined scenario classes. Theory-confirming empirical illustrations are provided to demonstrate the saturation of validation capacity and the persistence of uncertainty under increasing validation effort. The results delineate principled boundaries on certifiable claims for agentic AI systems, while also clarifying the conditions under which validation evidence remains epistemically interpretable, evaluation, and governance practices.

title: Integración de un chatbot educativo basado en inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación superior
abstract: This study examines the integration of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based educational chatbot in undergraduate higher education, aiming to analyze students' perceptions, usability, and its pedagogical value as an academic support tool. A quantitative approach was adopted, employing a non-experimental, cross-sectional design with a descriptive-correlational scope. The sample consisted of 98 students enrolled in the International Business program at a private university in Mexico during the January–July 2025 academic term. Data were collected through a validated questionnaire assessing dimensions related to user experience, problem management, and the chatbot's operational performance. The results indicate no statistically significant differences in the overall evaluation of the system based on prior AI proficiency levels, suggesting high accessibility and inclusive usability. Additionally, strong correlations were identified between response quality, relevance, objectivity, and perceived usefulness, highlighting the potential of educational chatbots as complementary digital tutors that support self-regulated learning and enrich student experiences in higher education.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Knowledge Diversity, and Sociopreneurship on Hospital Performance: Moderating Role of Service Quality in Central Java
abstract: Objective: Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) Theory, this study examines how technological interventions and medical staff capabilities interact to influence healthcare service performance in hospitals. Specifically, the study seeks to understand the relationships among these key resources within the context of healthcare service delivery. Method: A quantitative survey was conducted using descriptive statistics from Likert-scale questionnaires (1-5) distributed online to 102 respondents, including medical staff, managers, and administrators at type B hospitals in Central Java. Given the research objectives of prediction, exploration, or structural theory development, data were processed using SmartPLS 4.0. The independent variables in this study were Implementing Artificial Intelligence (AI), Knowledge Diversity, and Sociopreneur, while the dependent variable was Organizational Performance, with Service Quality as a moderating variable. Results: The findings indicate that each variable has a good level of validity (LF ≥ 0.70) and significance; the evaluation of discriminant validity using the Fornell-Larcker criterion, cross-loadings, and HTMT met the requirements; the f-test result of 0.037 (high) indicates the significant moderating effect of service quality on the relationship between AI implementation and organizational performance. Based on the model fit assessment, the influence of AI implementation has an R² of 0.787% (strong); the SRMR is 0.093, which is < 0.10, indicating that the model fits the empirical data well. Novelty: The implementation of AI can improve operational efficiency, diagnostic accuracy, and data management, thereby enhancing quality and service in hospitals. The follow-up to this research is the need to consider the infrastructure and medical staff expertise when implementing AI in type B hospitals in Central Java to improve healthcare services.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis and Literature Review of Sustainable Business Practices: Sustainability Disclosure in Indonesia’s Cement Industry
abstract: Objective: The purpose of this study is to analyze data mapping from cement companies and disclosures in sustainability reports. Diagrams will be incorporated to facilitate a comprehensive understanding. Method: This research uses sustainability reports from 17 cement companies in Indonesia, with disclosure years 2017-2020, using the GRI standards approach. This study reviews sustainability reports using Textual Analysis with a word-count approach developed by Loughran and McDonald. This approach counts how many words describe the context of the sustainability report and its disclosures, followed by the presentation of the Bibliometric Analysis developed by Hesford. Furthermore, the researcher will conduct a complete descriptive and thematic analysis. Results: This study shows that Semen Jawa had the best overall sustainability disclosures across the observed years. The most general aspect was disclosed by Semen Jawa in 2017, Semen Tonasa in 2018, and Semen Baturaja in 2019 and 2020. The most economical aspect was Semen Jawa throughout 2017-2019, and Semen Baturaja in 2020. Disclosing the most environmental aspect was PT. Indocement Tunggal Perkasa for the entirety of the observed years. The most social aspect was Semen Jawa from 2017-2020. With this mapping, you will be able to see the cement industry's concern for sustainability. Novelty: Through sustainability reports, it is hoped to demonstrate the sustainability of Indonesia's cement industry, which is expected to help protect it from the negative impacts of its production operations. Therefore, it is hoped that the cement industry's role in the country's economy will eventually be strengthened.

title: SparseDVFS: Sparsity-aware DVFS for Energy-Efficient Edge Inference
abstract: We present SparseDVFS, a sparsity-aware DVFS technique operating at fine-grain for energy-efficient edge inference. Our key insight is that operator sparsity is a primary metric for hardware frequency modulation. Traditional model-level DVFS, on the other hand, is often too coarse-grained to capture intra-inference variations in sparsity and computational intensity, whereas fine-grained operator-level scaling suffers from prohibitive performance degradation due to significant hardware switching latency. By distinguishing between compute-bound dense operators and memory-bound sparse operators, SparseDVFS applies specialized frequency configurations to maximize energy efficiency. We achieve this with a combination of three techniques: (1) an offline modeler that establishes a mapping between operator sparsity and optimal frequency configurations via white-box timeline analysis; (2) a runtime graph partitioner that aggregates operators into super-blocks, balancing scaling granularity and DVFS switching latency through a latency amortization constraint; and (3) a co-governor that employs a scaling engine to jointly synchronize CPU, GPU, and memory clock frequencies and a look-ahead instruction queue to eliminate antagonistic effects between independent component governors and hide hardware switching latencies. Extensive evaluations show that SparseDVFS improves energy efficiency by 78.17% with only a 12.8% latency penalty and reduces DVFS switching overhead by 8.5×, while ensuring thermal stability.

title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
abstract: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

title: ApproxHDC: Approximation Tuning for Hyperdimensional Computing
abstract: As Moore's law reaches its physical and economic limits, domain-specific approaches are increasingly employed to accelerate machine learning workloads. Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) represents one such emerging paradigm, offering an alternative to conventional deep learning techniques. Rooted in cognitive models of computation, HDC is designed bottom-up with hardware efficiency as a first-class objective. Consequently, HDC workloads map naturally to heterogeneous hardware platforms, including CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, as well as emerging in-memory computing technologies such as Resistive RAM (ReRAM) and Phase-Change Memory (PCM). The intrinsic tolerance of HDC algorithms to noise and approximation enables substantial performance gains with minimal loss in inference quality. In this work, we introduce ApproxHDC, a framework for automated identification and application of domain-specific approximations in HDC workloads. ApproxHDC extends the HPVM-HDC compiler infrastructure to enable retargetable compilation across diverse hardware backends, including CPUs, GPUs, and simulated ReRAM and PCM-based accelerators. The space of possible software and hardware approximations in HDC is exponentially large, making exhaustive exploration intractable; ApproxHDC employs efficient search and analysis techniques to navigate this space and identify high-impact approximations. We further integrate hardware-level approximation mechanisms within the HDC accelerator to demonstrate ApproxHDC's ability to exploit both software and hardware approximations. Experimental evaluation shows that ApproxHDC achieves up to 17.25x speedup on CPUs, 14.97x on GPUs, and 4.69x on SpecPCM while staying within user-specified quality-of-service constraints, outperforming the state-of-the-art MicroHD framework by 3.49x. HDC-specific search space pruning reduces the design space by 71 to 491 orders of magnitude automatically and up to 89 more with developer guidance, enabling discovery of high-quality configurations within minutes.

title: BitLLM: Efficient Low-Bit, Conversion-Hiding LLM Decoding on Mobile GPUs
abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models (LLMs) has unlocked remarkable capabilities across various domains. However, deploying LLMs on mobile devices remains challenging because of their high computational and memory requirements. Low-bit quantization (e.g., 4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) can reduce model size while preserving accuracy, but its practical efficacy on mobile GPUs has been limited so far. In this paper, we identify that the performance gap stems primarily from frequent data type conversions between quantized and floating-point values, and dynamic and inefficient memory access patterns caused by the growing Key-Value (KV) cache during autoregressive decoding. We introduce BitLLM, a mobile inference engine that addresses type conversion overhead and suboptimal memory accesses in quantized LLMs. Our approach features an adaptive layout and packing strategy for the KV cache that ensures efficient memory access throughout LLM decoding. This is coupled with an integer-native execution pipeline that defers and overlaps type conversion outside the compute hot path, keeping the critical MatMul stages in the integer domain. Implemented on off-the-shelf mobile GPUs, BitLLM outperforms leading engines, i.e., LLAMA.CPP, MNN-LLM, LiteRT-LM, and MLC-LLM, achieving average speedups of 1.78×, 1.73×, 1.58×, and 1.47×, respectively, across various models and quantization levels. Under long-context generation, BitLLM reduces average energy consumption (per token) by up to 88.9%.

title: Knowledge and attitude about evidence-based practice in Iranian nurses: A systematic review
abstract: The objective of this systematic review was to assess the knowledge and attitudes of Iranian nurses regarding evidence-based practice. A comprehensive and systematic search was conducted across various international electronic databases, including Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science, as well as Persian databases such as Iranmedex and the Scientific Information Database (SID). The search utilized keywords derived from Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), such as “knowledge”, “attitude”, “evidence-based practice”, and “nurses”, covering studies published up to June 28, 2025. The quality of the included studies in this systematic review was assessed using the Appraisal Tool for Cross-Sectional Studies (AXIS). A total of 1,314 nurses were included across eight cross-sectional studies. The findings revealed that the knowledge of nurses regarding evidence-based practice was generally low in most studies. Several factors demonstrated a significant positive relationship with nurses’ knowledge of evidence-based practice, including level of education, work experience, age, attitude, practice, male gender, participation in evidence-based practice workshops, and having published articles in journals. Conversely, the number of beds in hospitals was found to have a significant negative relationship with knowledge. Additionally, the attitude of nurses towards evidence-based practice was reported as moderate in most studies. Factors such as level of education, work experience, practice, and having published articles in journals showed significant positive correlations with nurses’ attitudes toward evidence-based practice. In conclusion, this review reveals a significant gap between Iranian nurses’ supportive attitudes and their limited EBP knowledge. Bridging this divide will require concerted efforts in curriculum reform, professional development, and organizational support. With appropriate investment and leadership, the nursing profession in Iran can move toward more effective and widespread integration of evidence-based practice in clinical care.

title: Association Between Red Cell Distribution Width and Glycemic Control in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Northern Iran
abstract: Red cell distribution width (RDW) is a routine and inexpensive hematological parameter that has recently been explored as a potential biomarker of metabolic and inflammatory disorders. This study investigated the associations between RDW, platelet distribution width (PDW), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Objectives: To evaluate the association between red cell distribution width and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. This cross-sectional study included 160 adults with T2DM attending diabetes clinics affiliated with Guilan University of Medical Sciences, Iran. Demographic characteristics, clinical variables, and hematological indices were collected from medical records. Glycemic control was assessed using fasting blood sugar (FBS) and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). Associations were evaluated using Spearman's or Pearson's correlation coefficients, and comparisons between controlled (HbA1c < 7%) and uncontrolled (HbA1c ≥ 7%) groups were performed using appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests. RDW demonstrated a weak but statistically significant positive unadjusted correlation with HbA1c (r = 0.280, P < 0.001). However, the difference in RDW between patients with controlled and uncontrolled glycemic status was not statistically significant (P = 0.188), and multivariable adjustment was not performed. Therefore, RDW should be considered an exploratory rather than a confirmatory marker. RDW showed a weak positive association with HbA1c, but its modest correlation and non-significant between-group difference indicate that it should be considered an adjunctive, rather than a substitute, marker for glycemic control. PDW and NLR were not consistently associated with glycemic control. Further prospective studies with larger populations and multivariable adjustments are warranted.

title: Serum iron profile dynamics and short-term mortality in critically ill patients: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: Iron metabolism dysregulation is a common feature of critical illness and may affect outcomes through its roles in oxygen transport, immune regulation, and oxidative stress. Although serum iron and ferritin have been proposed as prognostic biomarkers in intensive care unit (ICU) patients, their temporal changes and associations with short-term mortality remain unclear. This study evaluated the relationship between serial measurements of serum iron and ferritin and in-hospital mortality. To evaluate the association between serial (day-1 and day-7) serum iron and ferritin measurements and 7-day in-hospital mortality in a cohort of critically ill patients, and to assess the discriminative performance of a multivariable model including these biomarkers. This retrospective cohort study included 413 consecutive adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of a tertiary referral teaching hospital between January and December 2025. Clinical and laboratory data were retrospectively extracted from electronic medical records. Serum iron and ferritin concentrations measured on ICU admission (day 1) and on day 7, or at the last available assessment for patients discharged or deceased before day 7, were evaluated for their association with 7-day in-hospital mortality using multivariable logistic regression analysis. The overall 7-day mortality rate was 23.0% (95/413). After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and ICU length of stay, higher day 1 iron (OR: 0.517; 95% CI: 0.390–0.686; P<0.001) and ferritin levels (OR: 0.896; 95% CI: 0.857–0.937; P<0.001) were independently associated with lower mortality. In contrast, elevated day 7 iron (OR: 1.858; 95% CI: 1.426–2.421; P<0.001) and ferritin levels (OR: 1.115; 95% CI: 1.066–1.166; P<0.001) were associated with increased mortality. The model demonstrated high discrimination (AUROC 0.996; 95% CI 0.988–1.000). Serum iron and ferritin demonstrate a time-dependent biphasic association with short-term mortality. Serial monitoring may improve risk stratification in critically ill patients.

title: Frequency of Dyslipidemia and Associated Factors Among Patients with Helicobacter pylori Infection Attending an Academic Referral Center in Northern Iran
abstract: Helicobacter pylori infection is one of the most common chronic bacterial infections worldwide and, beyond mucosal gastroduodenal pathology, has been linked to systemic extra-gastrointestinal manifestations including altered serum lipid homeostasis and accelerated atherogenesis. Dyslipidemia is a major modifiable risk factor for ischemic heart and cerebrovascular disease. To determine the frequency of dyslipidemia and analyze its association with demographic, clinical and lifestyle variables among patients with H. pylori infection attending the Razi Educational-Medical Center in Rasht, Northern Iran. This cross-sectional analytical study was conducted on 200 patients with confirmed H. pylori infection (established by histopathology of endoscopic gastric biopsies) during 2021-2022. Demographic data, anthropometric parameters (BMI), lifestyle variables (smoking), chronic comorbidities and fasting serum lipid profile (total cholesterol [TC], triglycerides [TG], HDL-C and LDL-C) were extracted from clinical records and the laboratory server. Statistical analysis was performed with SPSS version 26 using the Chi-square test, independent t-test and Fisher's exact test at a significance level of P<0.05. Of the 200 patients studied, 137 (68.5%) had dyslipidemia and 63 (31.5%) did not. The mean age was 59.72 +/- 16.84 years; 87 patients (43.5%) were male and 113 (56.5%) were female. Mean TC, TG, HDL-C and LDL-C were 185.08 +/- 28.41, 136.06 +/- 46.11, 48.79 +/- 8.41 and 118.15 +/- 24.36 mg/dL, respectively. Applying NCEP-ATP III criteria, elevated LDL-C was present in 118 patients (95% CI: 61.9%-74.6%). Age, sex, occupation, BMI, smoking and comorbidities were not significantly associated with dyslipidemia (P>0.05), whereas a positive family history of dyslipidemia showed a significant association (P=0.017). Dyslipidemia was highly prevalent (68.5%) among patients with H. pylori infection in this Northern Iranian referral center, supporting a possible association between the infection and altered lipid metabolism. Classical demographic factors were not independently associated, highlighting the possible direct pro-atherogenic role of chronic H. pylori infection.

title: Engineering a Multi-Epitope Vaccine for Leishmania infantum: A combination of traditional immuno-informatic tools and python programming Approaches
abstract: Leishmaniasis, a significant health challenge in subtropical regions, requires effective and safe therapeutic options. Our primary objective was to design and evaluate a multi-epitope peptide-based vaccine, LIDVC, targeting Leishmania infantum. LIDVC was developed by integrating key epitopes from GP63, KMP11, and LACK antigens with the adjuvant Ov-ASP-1. Advanced bioinformatics tools assessed the vaccine's antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and population coverage. Structural integrity was confirmed through AlphaFold and DeepCDpred analyses, and molecular docking studies with TLR4 were performed. Our comprehensive computational evaluation demonstrated robust interactions between LIDVC and TLR4, favorable dynamic properties, and strong protective responses akin to those from natural infections. Codon optimization and in silico cloning showed potential for efficient expression in Escherichia coli. The LIDVC vaccine candidate shows promise against L. infantum, warranting experimental validation and preclinical studies. Our computational evaluation highlights LIDVC's potential as a safe and effective vaccine against leishmaniasis, addressing the need for improved therapeutic options in subtropical regions. Further studies will focus on experimental validation and developing a safe and effective vaccine against leishmaniasis.

title: Pharmacogenomic Evidence and Factors Influencing Treatment Response in Asthma and COPD
abstract: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are heterogeneous respiratory diseases in which treatment response varies substantially among individuals. Pharmacogenomics investigates how genetic variation may contribute to differences in drug efficacy and clinical outcomes. This narrative mini-review summarizes evidence on pharmacogenetic and pharmacogenomic associations with responses to commonly used respiratory medications in asthma and COPD, distinguishes candidate-gene findings from genome-wide and genotype-stratified trial evidence, examines limitations affecting clinical translation, and discusses research priorities. In asthma, the best-studied associations involve inhaled corticosteroids (ICS; GLCCI1, CRHR1, FCER2), β2-agonists (ADRB2), and leukotriene modifiers. A genome-wide study identified GLCCI1 rs37972 as associated with ICS response, and a systematic review found the most consistent candidate-gene evidence for FCER2 rs28364072, yet replication has been limited overall and even replicated variants explain only a small fraction of response variability. Two prospective genotype-stratified trials of ADRB2 Arg16Gly gave different clinical signals depending on the treatment regimen. In COPD, research is less developed, and a meta-analysis found no consistent association between the examined ADRB2 variants and β2-agonist response. Differences in populations, phenotypes, treatment regimens, and outcome definitions further limit comparisons. Although pharmacogenomics may eventually contribute to precision respiratory medicine, routine treatment decisions are not currently guided by most candidate pharmacogenomic markers in asthma or COPD. Larger and ancestrally diverse studies, independent replication, standardized response outcomes, and prospective evaluation of clinical utility are needed before broader implementation.

title: Bacterial etiology and antimicrobial resistance in hospital-acquired respiratory infections: A Six-year retrospective study in Northern Iran
abstract: Hospital-acquired respiratory infections are important healthcare-associated complications, particularly among critically ill patients, and are frequently associated with antimicrobial resistance. Local surveillance of bacterial pathogens and their antimicrobial susceptibility profiles is essential for informing infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship. This study aimed to investigate the bacterial etiology and antimicrobial resistance patterns of hospital-acquired respiratory infections in Northern Iran. This retrospective descriptive study reviewed medical records and hospital infection-control data for patients with hospital-acquired respiratory infections at Razi Teaching Hospital, Rasht, Iran, between 2018 and 2023. Demographic characteristics, hospital ward, length of stay, discharge outcomes, bacterial isolates, and antimicrobial susceptibility results were extracted. Bacterial identification and susceptibility findings were obtained from routine microbiology laboratory records. Among 3,726 recorded hospital-acquired infections, 1,231 (33.0%) were classified as respiratory infections. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) accounted for 1,215 cases (98.7%). The mean patient age was 61.15 ± 17.55 years, and 61.0% of patients were male. The mean hospital stay was 30.88 ± 30.29 days, and in-hospital mortality was 60.2%. Klebsiella spp. was the most frequently recorded bacterial group (40.2%), followed by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (15.2%), Acinetobacter spp. (14.3%), and Enterobacter spp. (9.6%). High resistance rates were reported across several organism-antimicrobial combinations, including cefazolin resistance in Klebsiella spp. (99.1%) and imipenem resistance in Acinetobacter spp. (99.2%). Hospital-acquired respiratory infections represented a substantial proportion of recorded healthcare-associated infections and were characterized by the predominance of Gram-negative bacteria, high reported antimicrobial resistance, and considerable in-hospital mortality. Strengthening infection prevention, validating susceptibility data, and implementing continuous local microbiological surveillance may support more effective infection control and antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Auditee and Auditor Factors Affecting Audit Delay with Audit Firm Reputation as Moderating Variable: Supporting SDG 16 in Tourism Firms
abstract: Objective: To examine the effects of auditee and auditor factors on audit delay and evaluates whether audit firm reputation moderates these relationships. The analysis focuses on tourism, restaurant, and hotel companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, while linking timely audited reporting to the transparency and accountability principles of Sustainable Development Goal 16. Method: The study employed a quantitative explanatory design using secondary data from audited annual reports for 2017–2021. Purposive sampling yielded 22 companies and 110 firm-year observations. Liquidity, firm size, financial distress, and audit opinion were tested as explanatory variables, while audit firm reputation was examined through moderated regression analysis. Results: Liquidity had no significant effect on audit delay. Firm size and financial distress significantly increased audit delay, whereas an unqualified audit opinion reduced the reporting lag. Audit firm reputation did not moderate the liquidity–audit delay relationship but significantly moderated the effects of firm size, financial distress, and audit opinion. Novelty: The study integrates auditee financial characteristics and auditor-related attributes within a single moderation model in a sector observed across pre-pandemic and pandemic periods. It extends audit-delay research by demonstrating that reputable audit firms do not uniformly accelerate reporting; their moderating role depends on the underlying company characteristic. The findings offer sector-specific evidence relevant to stronger corporate reporting discipline and the accountability orientation of SDG 16.

title: Impact of cognitive processes on work performance comparative study in teachers of the Cruz del Norte Educational Unit
abstract: This study examines the relationship between cognitive processes and job performance in teachers at the Cruz del Norte Educational Unit, focusing on attention, planning, organization, anxiety, and job stress. A mixed-method design was applied, combining quantitative and qualitative techniques such as psychometric tests, Pearson correlation, multiple regression analysis, Student’s t-test, the Delphi method, and the Ishikawa diagram. The results show that executive functions, particularly planning and organization, have a significant positive impact on job performance. Teachers with higher levels of these skills demonstrate better performance, with strong correlations (r = 0.72, p = 0.001; r = 0.65, p = 0.003). In contrast, anxiety and stress act as limiting factors. Multiple regression analysis indicates that anxiety (β = -0.4946, p < 0.0001) and stress (β = -0.3721, p < 0.001) negatively predict job performance. Additionally, job indiscipline—reflected in absenteeism and lateness—shows a strong negative correlation with performance (r = -0.74, p < 0.000). These findings highlight the importance of time management and organizational commitment, as well as the need to implement training and psychological support strategies to improve teacher performance and educational quality.

title: TEKNO Method: Total Evaluation based on Knowledge-driven Normalized Optimization for Multi-Criteria Decision Making
abstract: Multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) methods play an important role in supporting decisions involving multiple criteria with different characteristics and levels of importance. However, differences in normalization procedures, criterion treatment, and aggregation mechanisms can lead to variations in the resulting preference structures. This study proposes a new MCDM method, namely total evaluation based on knowledge-driven normalized optimization (TEKNO), which integrates normalization, relative evaluation, criterion weighting, optimization-based normalization, and total evaluation into a unified decision-making framework. The proposed method is designed to transform heterogeneous decision information into comparable evaluation values while preserving the relative contribution of each criterion. The applicability of TEKNO is evaluated through two decision-making case studies involving new store location selection and leasing customer selection. The evaluation framework includes ranking analysis, comparison with established MCDM methods, Spearman rank correlation analysis, and sensitivity analysis under variations in criterion weights. The results show that TEKNO achieves a Spearman rank correlation coefficient of 1.0000 for the new store location case and 0.9964 for the leasing customer selection case, indicating very strong agreement with the reference rankings. In addition, the ranking remains unchanged across the tested sensitivity scenarios, demonstrating the stability of TEKNO under variations in criterion weights. These findings indicate that TEKNO provides a transparent, systematic, and stable alternative for MCDM applications for practical decision support where reliable ranking, methodological transparency, and robustness across alternative evaluation conditions are required. Nevertheless, broader validation using diverse datasets, decision domains, weighting schemes, and statistical evaluation techniques is required to further establish its generalizability and comparative performance.

title: Decision-Making in the Age of Datafication: Interdisciplinary Reflections and Critical Intervention
abstract: Data and society share a dynamic relationship: data shapes our world while our world generates data. AI and planetary-scale computation have transformed datafication, converting decision-making into quantifiable data processed by algorithms rather than humans. Though perceived as neutral, datafication carries political implications, it marginalizes indigenous knowledge, reshapes power dynamics, and fragments legal accountability. In this book, we analyse datafied decision-making which is increasingly built on large scale data environments and managed by computational technologies, whereby computational and legal systems, power relations, and material infrastructures jointly reshape decision-making processes. Based on 11 studies examining datafied decision-making across labour, politics, AI, law, climate governance, healthcare, and infrastructure, this volume demonstrates how datafication’s exclusions perpetuate injustice, and how actors reclaim power through its gaps. In doing so, we aim to contribute to the cross-disciplinary and international discussion on automated and data-driven decision-making that is currently underway.
