title: Epidemiologia de 376.383 confecções de fístulas arteriovenosas para hemodiálise ao longo de 9 anos no Sistema Único de Saúde e no setor privado brasileiro
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine trends in AVF creation for hemodialysis across Brazil from 2015 to 2023, assessing differences in frequency, geographic distribution, and sectoral disparities between the public and private healthcare sectors. METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using anonymized data from national administrative databases: DATASUS (public sector) and D-TISS (private sector). The majority of AVF creation procedures were included. Statistical analyses considered regional adjustments and were performed using SPSS v.20, with significance set at p < 0.001. RESULTS: Over the nine- year period, 376,383 AVF procedures were recorded, with 90.57% occurring in the public sector. While the absolute number of AVF creations increased, the ratio of AVFs per 1,000 dialysis patients showed a declining trend. Regional disparities were evident, with the Southeast and South regions presenting higher procedure rates compared to other areas. The private sector consistently reported lower creation rates. CONCLUSION: Although, separately, dialysis and AVF rates have risen steadily in Brazil, the relative rate between them has shown a decreasing trend over the years. The predominance of AVF procedures in the public system is more pronounced.

title: Symptom control in comprehensive conservative care for chronic kidney disease
abstract: Over recent decades, the prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) has risen markedly. In the terminal stage of the disease, renal replacement therapy (RRT) is traditionally recommended as the standard therapeutic approach. However, in older individuals with a high burden of comorbidities or substantial functional impairment, the benefits of RRT in terms of survival prolongation or improvement in quality of life become uncertain. In this context, comprehensive conservative kidney management (CKM) has emerged as a clinical alternative that is centered on the patient's needs, values, and preferences. CKM entails an active, nondialytic management strategy for CKD that incorporates palliative care principles, with emphasis on kidney supportive care, slowing disease progression, and symptom control. This article discusses the main symptoms experienced by patients with advanced CKD managed conservatively and provides practical recommendations for their clinical management.

title: Urinary extracellular vesicle–associated IL-6 and cathepsin D for early identification of chronic kidney disease in high-risk patients
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently asymptomatic and remains underdiagnosed in high-risk populations. Urinary extracellular vesicles (uEVs) provide a non-invasive source of kidney-related biomolecules and may improve early detection strategies. We evaluated uEV-associated interleukin-6 (IL-6), cathepsin D (CTD), and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) as candidate biomarkers for early CKD, including sex-stratified patterns. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 230 adults at high risk (type 2 diabetes mellitus and/or systemic arterial hypertension) were classified as having normal kidney function (NKF) or CKD stages G1-G4. uEVs were isolated using a standardized protocol and characterized by scanning electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and Western blot for Alix and flotillin-1. Total uEV-associated protein was quantified, and CTD, IL-6, and TGF-β were measured in uEV preparations. RESULTS: uEVs displayed expected morphology and marker expression. Particle size distributions differed by sex and CKD status. Total uEV protein content did not significantly differ across CKD stages. uEV-associated IL-6 was significantly higher in G1 compared with NKF (p ≤ 0.05). CTD showed a decreasing trend from G1 to G4 with stage- and sexspecific differences, most evident in women at G1. uEV-associated TGF-β did not differ significantly across stages. CONCLUSIONS: uEV-derived IL-6 and CTD show potential as non-invasive indicators of early CKD, with clinically relevant sex-dependent patterns, while TGF-β may provide complementary information. Standardized uEV isolation and measurement workflows are essential for biomarker reproducibility and future clinical translation.

title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients with chronic kidney disease: a randomized clinical trial
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with intestinal dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and impaired intestinal barrier function. Serum zonulin has been proposed as an indirect marker of intestinal permeability, although its clinical relevance in CKD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. METHODS: In this randomized, placebo-controlled, triple-blind clinical trial, 40 hemodialysis patients were assigned to receive either a probiotic formulation or a placebo for six months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in serum zonulin from baseline to follow-up. Secondary outcomes included metabolic, anthropometric, hemodynamic, and gastrointestinal variables. RESULTS: Serum zonulin increased in both groups, with no significant between-group difference (placebo: 288.2 to 425.3 ng/mL; probiotic: 239.5 to 453.7 ng/mL; p = 0.882; ANCOVA p = 0.463). Pre-dialysis urea decreased within the probiotic group, but the between-group difference was not significant (p = 0.305). Serum phosphorus showed a greater reduction in the probiotic group than in the placebo group (p = 0.011; ANCOVA p = 0.011). No significant differences were observed for anthropometric or hemodynamic outcomes. CONCLUSION: Six months of probiotic supplementation did not significantly reduce serum zonulin levels in hemodialysis patients. Although a favorable effect on serum phosphoruswas observed, these findings do not support a measurable impact of this probiotic regimen on serum zonulin and highlight the need for larger studies incorporating direct assessments of intestinal permeability and gut microbiota.

title: Knowledge and practices on sustainability in nephrology in Brazil
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Climate change has a bidirectional relationship with kidney diseases: environmental stressors may increase the incidence and progression of renal conditions, while dialysis therapy is among the treatment modalities with the highest environmental impact in healthcare. Despite the growing international debate on sustainable nephrology, this topic remains underexplored in the Brazilian context. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the level of knowledge, perceptions, and practices related to environmental sustainability among nephrology professionals in Brazil and to identify barriers to the adoption of sustainable strategies in dialysis services. METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted using an online questionnaire targeting nephrology professionals. The instrument assessed knowledge regarding climate change and kidney health, sustainability practices implemented in dialysis services, and institutional barriers to their adoption. RESULTS: A total of 180 responses from professionals across 20 Brazilian states and the Federal District were analyzed, with a predominance of nephrologists and nurses. Most participants recognized the impact of climate change on kidney health; however, limited knowledge was observed regarding public policies and structured sustainability strategies. The most frequently reported practices involved waste management, whereas initiatives such as water reuse, renewable energy sources, and sustainable transportation strategies were less prevalent. The main barriers identified included financial constraints, lack of institutional incentives, and absence of strategic planning. CONCLUSION: These findings highlight gaps between perceptions, knowledge, and the implementation of sustainable practices in Brazilian nephrology, reinforcing the need for policies, professional training, and institutional strategies to promote environmentally sustainable kidney care.

title: IgA nephropathy: evolving treatment strategies
abstract: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerular disease and is characterized by marked clinical, laboratory, and histopathological heterogeneity, with a variable risk of progression to advanced stages of chronic kidney disease depending on several underlying factors. A better understanding of its pathogenesis, which involves at least a four-hit pathogenic sequence, has enabled the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting different stages of disease development, including agents directed at specific molecular pathways. Supportive kidney-protective therapy is now well established as the cornerstone of IgAN management and involves lifestyle modifications such as a healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight control, smoking cessation, sodium restriction, optimal blood pressure control, and interventions to reduce cardiovascular risk. Pharmacological measures include renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, as well as mineralocorticoid receptor and endothelin A receptor antagonists. Historically, immunosuppressive treatment relied primarily on systemic corticosteroids, with cyclophosphamide or azathioprine reserved for selected clinical situations. More recently, targeted-release budesonide has emerged as a therapeutic option, followed by the development of agents directed at specific molecular pathways, particularly complement inhibitors and therapies targeting BAFF and/or APRIL signaling, among others. Although this expanding therapeutic armamentarium provides new opportunities to improve patient outcomes, it also introduces uncertainty and complexity into clinical decision-making. Therefore, defining evidence-based parameters to guide the selection and combination of available therapies according to the distinct endotypes of IgAN has become increasingly important.

title: Visualizing a decade of machine translation research (2016–2025): A VOSviewer-based bibliometric analysis
abstract: Background and Purpose: Machine translation has undergone rapid transformation over the past decade, driven by advances in neural machine translation and large language models, yet systematic attention to the field’s overall intellectual structure during this critical transition remains limited. This study aims to visualize the evolution of machine translation research from 2016 to 2025, with particular attention to its interdisciplinary development and trends in the post-2022 era of large language models. Methodology: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of machine translation research from a language and translation perspective, based on 582 journal articles published between 2016 and 2025 and indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. Using VOSviewer, it examines the main characteristics of machine translation publications and key research themes. Findings: The findings show a steady rise in machine translation research output, reflecting growing scholarly interest alongside technological advances. Research is globally distributed but concentrated in Europe and Asia, particularly in Spain and China. Journals in translation studies and computational linguistics account for the largest share of publications and receive the most scholarly attention. However, the field has yet to form a stable core author group, indicating a dispersed and evolving research structure. Five major research themes are identified: technological development and model innovation; human-machine collaboration and application contexts; machine translation quality evaluation; translation studies and industry-related research; and language education with ethical considerations. Contributions: By mapping research trajectories and key contributors, this study offers a solid foundation for advancing future research, emphasizing the need for cross-regional and interdisciplinary collaboration and a balanced integration of technological, human, and ethical dimensions. title: Monitoring farmland biodiversity using remote sensing
abstract: Monitoring biodiversity in agricultural landscapes is essential for addressing global biodiversity decline. Emerging remote sensing and artificial intelligence technologies enable large-scale, low-impact and cost-effective assessments. This chapter provides a concise review of remote sensing applications for farmland biodiversity monitoring, structured around the Essential Biodiversity Variable framework. We examine plants, animals, fungi and microorganisms, and their habitats in productive and semi-natural areas. Spaceborne and airborne sensors effectively assess agroecosystem structure and functioning, and detect plants and large mammals with distinct spectral or phenological traits. UAV imagery and camera traps offer higher resolution for monitoring smaller or cryptic species. Remote sensing also supports indirect methods, such as species distribution modeling, to infer the occurrence of species that are difficult to detect. Key challenges include technological, methodological and operational limitations. Integrating multi-platform data, establishing shared benchmarks, and broadening taxonomic coverage, supported by policy incentives and farmer-friendly technologies, are essential for scaling biodiversity monitoring and promoting sustainable strategies that reconcile conservation with agricultural production.

title: Rayleigh-Quotient-Based Data Classification Method for Machine Learning
abstract: Inspired by the ability of human ears to distinguish between different kinds of music and the ability of an ancient instrument to play countless beautiful melodies, this paper proposes the Rayleigh-quotient-based data classification method, which implements data classification by selecting an appropriate eigenfunction coordinate system to represent different categories of data and making different categories of data show significant differences in the coordinate components, meanwhile, transforming the selection problem of an eigenfunction coordinate system into a design problem of physical parameters of music instruments, such as designing a non-uniform string or membrane with distributed supports. In theory, the method is based on the eigenvalue problem for Sturm-Liouville differential equation, the eigenvalue problem for functional minimization, and the generalized eigenvalue problem for matrices, which have a time-honored history and can provide strong theoretical foundation and support. In addition, each parameter in the method has a clear physical interpretation and can be adjusted under the guidance of a set of complete theory, and their influence on classification results is definite, avoiding the large time consumption due to randomly adjusting parameters. The data classification procedure is divided into 2 steps, including mass density function design and stiffness function design, which not only simplifies the process of parameter adjustment, but also enables the optimization algorithm to be implemented by the linear programming with a low computational complexity, theoretically guaranteeing a high computational efficiency. Considering the amount of data being classified is large, two kinds of algorithms are developed to implement data classification, where one is a statistical averaging algorithm and the other is an incremental iterative algorithm. Finally, by combining the image database MNIST, the Rayleigh-quotient-based data classification method is employed to build an image classifier, which is trained on the MNIST training set including 60,000 images, and is tested on the MNIST test set including 10,000 images. The classification results show that by selecting an appropriate eigenfunction coordinate system, the Rayleigh quotient distribution of each category of image can be controlled within a very narrow range, while different categories of images show significant difference in the Rayleigh quotient distribution; the classification accuracy on the MNIST training set and on the MNIST test set are stable at about 99.50%, and the maximum accuracy can reach to 100.00% on the MNIST training set and 99.76% on the MNIST test set; and the Rayleigh-quotient threshold can be selected within a very wide range, beneficial for the robustness and stability of data classification.

title: From words to worlds: Concluding reflections and emerging directions
abstract: In concluding the second series of eight articles in the double special issue on ‘Engaging with communication and language in relation to mathematics and its education’, we take the opportunity to reflect across the articles to prompt us all to consider potential and emerging directions for future research. This final article is overall a commentary inspired by the communication-centred and language-centred contributions to mathematics education across the entire collection of articles, that is, all those comments that situate mathematics and its education as language and communication praxis. We explore this relationship between mathematics and its education with communication and language through three themes: time, theories and methodologies, and the nuances of the term ‘relation’ in the title of this double special issue.

title: Impact of Agile Methods on Tacit Knowledge Sharing from Self-Determination Perspective: A Mixed Method Study of Chinese IT Teams
abstract: The purpose of the study is to examine whether agile methods foster tacit knowledge sharing in IT project teams and to identify the motivational mechanisms, especially basic psychological needs and shared goals, underpinning this relationship in Chinese contexts. It does so by using a sequential mixed-methods design: survey data from 610 IT professionals (predominantly mainland China, with a small Hong Kong subsample) analysed with PLS-SEM, complemented by 22 semi structured interviews examined through comparative cross case analysis, thematic coding, and process tracing. The findings suggest agile methods positively predict tacit knowledge sharing, even after controlling for transformational leadership and enjoyment of sharing. This effect is largely mediated by satisfaction of basic psychological needs and shared goals. Autonomy and shared goals act mainly through competence and relatedness. Qualitative evidence underscores problem-driven collaboration, project ownership, and informal exchanges. That said, the main limitation of the study is that cross sectional, self report data, non probability sampling, and focus on Chinese IT professionals limit causal inference and generalizability. Nonetheless, the study provides empirical evidence that agile methods are linked to tacit knowledge sharing, explains how these methods foster such sharing through the satisfaction of basic psychological needs and the establishment of shared goals, and offers a rigorous operationalization of agile methods. This implies that managers should design agile practices as a motivational architecture that supports autonomy, competence, relatedness, and shared goals, rather than relying on formal, mandatory knowledge sharing sessions or performance linked incentives.

title: Perceived Accuracy and Relevance of AI-Based Product Recommendations and Generation X Purchase Decisions in Jakarta
abstract: This study examines how perceived accuracy and contextual relevance of artificial-intelligence-based product recommendations influence purchase decisions among Generation X e-commerce users in Jakarta. A quantitative explanatory design was modeled with 300 respondent profiles and 18 reflective indicators. Partial least squares structural equation modeling, 10,000-resample bootstrapping, coefficient-difference testing, and tenfold cross-validation were applied. Perceived accuracy had a stronger positive effect on purchase decisions (β=.604, p<.001) than relevance (β=.217, p<.001), and the difference was significant (Δβ=.387, p<.001). The model explained 54.2% of purchase-decision variance and showed positive Qpredict2​ values. The findings indicate an accuracy–relevance asymmetry: relevance attracts attention, whereas perceived accuracy more strongly reinforces purchase decisions.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Spatiotemporal Clustering for Identifying Homogeneous Climatic Zones in West Java
abstract: Homogeneous Climatic Zones (ZOM) support operational seasonal services in Indonesia, particularly across regions where rainfall changes sharply over short distances. This study evaluates a climatic regionalization framework that combines Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) and Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) using BMKG gridded rainfall data across West Java at approximately 5 km resolution for the 1991–2020 period. Each of the 1,214 grid cells was represented by a 36-dasarian climatological rainfall profile. A search across 360 hyperparameter combinations yielded 324 executable configurations, followed by spatial absorption of transition grids and layered evaluation using the Silhouette Score, Heterogeneity Index (HI), and operational tractability. Scenario 60 (n_neighbors = 5, min_dist = 0.01, min_cluster_size = 10, min_samples = 5) produced 54 initial zones with a Silhouette Score of 0.5633 and an HI of 7.239, compared with an HI of 8.464 for the 41-zone operational baseline. Subsequent spatial refinement produced a corrected final map containing 50 sequential ZOM. Distinguishing the evaluation metrics of the 54-zone candidate stage from the 50-zone cartographic structure of the spatial refinement stage clarifies the analytical sequence and supports a more precise interpretation of cluster quality, climatic homogeneity, and final zone boundaries.

title: Implementasi Machine Learning untuk Deteksi Kejujuran Wakif pada Sistem Wakaf Digital Berbasis Blockchain
abstract: Digital waqf requires a validation mechanism that not only protects data integrity after storage but also evaluates transaction credibility before the data becomes immutable on a blockchain. This study develops an intelligent pre-validation mechanism through a hybrid architecture integrating a web application, machine learning, a backend API, smart contracts, and blockchain. The dataset combined the Ethereum Fraud Detection Dataset (9,841 transactions and 51 attributes) with transaction and behavioral data from the digital waqf system. Data processing included cleaning, missing-value handling, categorical encoding, StandardScaler normalization, feature engineering, and Isolation Forest anomaly detection. The resulting anomaly score was normalized into a 0–100 trust score and passed to the smart contract to process high-trust transactions, route medium-risk transactions to nazhir review, and block high-risk transactions before on-chain recording. Built using Python, Scikit-learn, PHP, MySQL, Solidity, Ganache, and MetaMask, the prototype demonstrated an end-to-end pre-validation flow from waqif input to on-chain decision-making. Representative tests yielded trust scores of 92 (normal), 68 (review), and 27 (fraud), showing that separating off-chain inference from on-chain validation provides an effective control layer against garbage in, garbage out without imposing machine learning computation on the smart contract.

title: Model Explainable Machine Learning untuk Deteksi Anomali Transaksi Blockchain Bitcoin Menggunakan Analisis SHAP
abstract: The growing volume of Bitcoin transactions requires anomaly detection mechanisms that are both accurate and explainable, as high-performing classifiers often lack decision traceability for auditors and security analysts. This study develops an explainable machine learning approach for Bitcoin transaction anomaly detection by comparing Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), followed by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation on the best model. Using the Elliptic Bitcoin Dataset, preprocessing included feature-label merging, removing unknown labels, binary target conversion, selecting 165 numerical features, MinMaxScaler normalization, and an 80:20 stratified train-test split, retaining 14,253 labeled transactions: 13,380 licit (93.88%) and 873 illicit (6.12%). Evaluation based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix, and training time showed that XGBoost achieved the best performance with 0.9961 accuracy, 1.0000 precision, 0.9371 recall, 0.9676 F1-score, and 0.9960 ROC-AUC, yielding 2,676 true negatives, zero false positives, 164 true positives, and 11 false negatives. Transaction-level SHAP analysis revealed how individual feature contributions shifted predictions toward the licit or illicit class, demonstrating that integrating XGBoost and SHAP delivers accurate anomaly detection with transparent decision support for blockchain investigations.

title: Model Sistem Pendukung Keputusan untuk Penilaian Risiko Stunting pada Balita Menggunakan Certainty Factor Berbasis Bukti: Studi Pembuktian Konsep
abstract: Childhood stunting is multifactorial, and its risk assessment often involves interdependent evidence. This study developed a proof-of-concept decision support model based on the Certainty Factor (CF) method using literature-derived evidence weights. Fifteen risk factors were curated from 22 District Health Office indicators. Odds ratios were transformed into attributable fractions and mapped to provisional evidence weights using explicit rounding, capping, and attenuation rules. To reduce double counting, the hierarchical CF model groups the factors into seven clusters and applies a within-cluster correlation factor (β) alongside a mediation factor (α) for selected upstream clusters. The web prototype was computationally trace-tested using five stunting cases, which were not used for clinical or diagnostic validation. Under the baseline parameter setting, hierarchical CF values were 0.027–0.113 lower than classical CF values, and sensitivity analysis across scenarios ranging from strong to no correction showed no category changes across the five traces. The prototype accurately reproduced manual calculations and preserved factor-level traceability. Expert elicitation, threshold calibration, and diagnostic evaluation using representative case-control data remain necessary before field implementation.

title: Design of an analysis application for predict demand forecasting in inventory system
abstract: Trading companies often face challenges in managing their inventory systems and finding it hard to match inventory levels with the increasing demand from consumers. This paper tries to create a system that can forecast how much of a product customers might want and also check how well different deep learning methods work. In this paper, the author uses both experimental and applied methods to check how well each deep learning algorithm works.The algorithms tested are CNN-LSTM, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer. The author used data from Kaggle that includes 76,000 sales records from 2022 up to 2024, covering different product categories such as clothing, furniture, electronics, toys, and groceries. The data was then cleaned and split into groups for training and testing. The author found the results by testing various deep learning algorithms. The top performing algorithm is CNN-LSTM, which has MAE of 28.2136, RMSE of 36.6037, and R² of 0.3106. Even though the R2 value shows the model doesn't have strong predictive power yet, it is still the best performing model out of all the ones studied in this research. By comparing the system's performance to standard operating levels, it was found that the system can adjust to changes in demand.This suggests it could help trading companies better manage their stock and offer more understanding of how deep learning models work.

title: Optimization of Student Public Transportation Routes Using the Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: Student public transportation often experiences inefficiency due to suboptimal routes and schedules. This study aims to determine more efficient student transportation routes and schedules using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) method. This method is applied to minimize travel time and distance while considering fleet capacity and operational constraints. Simulation results show that PSO can significantly improve objective values, resulting in more organized and efficient routes and departure schedules. This study concludes that PSO is an effective optimization approach for student transportation planning. The contribution of this research is to provide a computational optimization model that can be used as a basis for developing a more adaptive transportation scheduling system. In addition, the optimization model developed is capable of integrating operational variables such as departure sequence, passenger readiness, and passenger distribution patterns on each bus to produce more realistic solutions. The application of PSO in the simulation shows that this algorithm can eliminate hard constraints while reducing soft constraints, reflecting an increase in overall system efficiency. The departure schedule obtained is also more stable with consistent headways, thereby reducing student waiting times and increasing fleet utilization.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot for Academic Information Services Using GROQ API
abstract: Academic information services in universities are still largely carried out manually by administrative staff with limited working hours, making it difficult for students to receive quick responses, especially outside office hours. This study aims to design and implement an academic chatbot using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach through the Groq API and a Streamlit interface. The system was developed following the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, which includes problem identification, defining solution objectives, dataset collection, artifact design and development, system demonstration, testing and evaluation, as well as communication of research results. Black-box testing on 20 questions yielded 18 valid answers, while semantic quality evaluation using BERTScore produced a precision of 0.7054, recall of 0.7176, and F1-score of 0.7095. The average system response time was 1.45 seconds, with a median of 0.85 seconds, indicates that the majority of responses were provided in less than one second, despite a single outlier of 12.13 seconds. These results finding suggest that the integration of RAG with the Groq API holds potential for enhancing digital academic information services in higher education. Nevertheless, its operational benefits in real-world scenarios warrant further evaluation through empirical user testing.

title: Inventory control of frame materials using EOQ, safety stock, and reorder point at PT Sharp Semiconductor Indonesia
abstract: Raw material inventory control is essential for maintaining production continuity while minimizing inventory-related costs. This study aimed to optimize the inventory control of frame materials at PT Sharp Semiconductor Indonesia using the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), Safety Stock, and Reorder Point (ROP) methods, and to evaluate inventory cost efficiency through Total Inventory Cost (TIC) analysis. A quantitative approach was employed using demand, ordering cost, holding cost, and lead time data collected from January to December 2025. The results indicate that the optimal order quantity is 249,870 units per order, reducing the ordering frequency from 34 to approximately six orders per year. The analysis also determined a Reorder Point (ROP) of 157,910 units and a Safety Stock of 67,540 units to maintain material availability during demand fluctuations and procurement lead times. Furthermore, implementing the proposed inventory policy reduced the annual inventory cost from IDR 109,171,421 to IDR 38,534,194, representing an inventory cost saving of approximately 65%. These findings demonstrate that integrating EOQ, Safety Stock, and ROP provides an effective inventory control strategy that improves cost efficiency while ensuring uninterrupted production continuity.

title: Effect of flow rate on the performance and fouling of a spiral plate heat exchanger in the phosphoric acid cooling process
abstract: The E-2502B cooler in the phosphoric acid concentration unit is used to reduce the temperature of H3PO4 product after concentration before storage. Fluctuations in mass flow rate and outlet temperature indicate the need to evaluate equipment performance to maintain safe and optimal cooling. This study evaluates the performance of the E-2502B Spiral Plate Heat Exchanger (SPHE) based on heat transfer, Log Mean Temperature Difference (LMTD), clean overall coefficient (Uc), design overall coefficient (Ud), fouling factor (Rd), and efficiency. The analysis used actual operating data from 18-27 July 2025, including inlet-outlet temperatures and mass flow rates on the hot and cold sides. The analysis was conducted under the lowest data conditions through heat balance, overall heat-transfer coefficient calculations, and comparison between the actual fouling factor and theoretical limits. The results show an actual cooler efficiency of 50%, with Uc of 853.319 kJ/m²h°C, Ud of 422.689 kJ/m².h.°C, and Rd of 0.001194 m².h.°C/kJ. The actual Rd value exceeds the theoretical range of 0.00018-0.00072 m².h.°C/kJ, indicating fouling that reduces heat-transfer performance. Stable mass flow, periodic cleaning of the acid and cooling-water plates, and flow-rate sensor verification are required to maintain cooler performance.

title: Analisys detection place defect incoming part in the incoming quality control division at PT XYZ cikarang
abstract: The quality of incoming parts is a critical factor affecting the quality of final products in the electronics manufacturing industry. Nonconforming materials received from suppliers can increase product defects, production costs, and disrupt manufacturing processes. This study aims to analyze incoming part defects in the Incoming Quality Control (IQC) Division of PT XYZ Cikarang based on defect types, defect detection locations, root causes, and improvement priorities. The study employed Seven Tools, Fishbone Diagram, and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) using data from the Incoming Production Rework Report for February 2026. The data were analyzed using check sheets, Pareto diagrams, defect detection place analysis, Fishbone diagrams, and FMEA. The results revealed that scratch was the dominant defect, accounting for 58.66% of the 358 recorded defects, while the highest-risk failure cause was the non-optimal material handling standard operating procedure, with a Risk Priority Number (RPN) of 504. Based on these findings, improvement priorities were focused on revising material handling procedures, enhancing operator competency, standardizing supplier packing methods, and improving material storage systems. This study contributes by integrating Seven Tools, Fishbone Diagram, and FMEA to establish a systematic risk-based approach for prioritizing quality improvement actions, thereby supporting more effective incoming material quality control in electronics manufacturing

title: Implementation of Disciplinary Values Through the Pencak Silat Extracurricular Program in Elementary Schools: A Descriptive Qualitative Study
abstract: Background & objective: Character education in elementary schools requires learning environments in which disciplinary values can be practiced through authentic social and behavioural experiences. This study examined how disciplinary values were enacted, reinforced, and contextualized through the compulsory Pagar Nusa Pencak Silat extracurricular program at SD Khadijah Wonorejo, Surabaya, Indonesia. The study also explored additional character-related behaviours and contextual factors supporting the continuity of disciplinary practices. Materials & Methods: A descriptive qualitative design was employed involving 67 participants, comprising 62 elementary-school students, one school principal, two extracurricular teachers, and two Pagar Nusa coaches. Data were collected through participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentary evidence. Student records included descriptive ratings on a 1–5 scale covering three disciplinary dimensions and nine additional character-related indicators. Qualitative data were analyzed iteratively through data reduction, coding, categorization, cross-source comparison, and verification following the Miles and Huberman interactive model. Descriptive statistics were used only to summarize the student-level ratings using means, standard deviations, frequencies, and percentages. Results: Three interconnected dimensions of disciplinary practice emerged: time discipline, behavioural discipline, and training discipline. Behavioural discipline showed the highest descriptive rating (M = 4.08, SD = 0.68), followed by training discipline (M = 3.85, SD = 0.70) and time discipline (M = 3.76, SD = 0.67). Ratings of 4–5 were recorded for 80.6%, 67.7%, and 62.9% of students, respectively. Among additional character-related behaviours, tolerance (M = 4.42), social care (M = 4.34), and hard work (M = 4.19) received the highest descriptive ratings. Conclusions: The findings indicate that Pagar Nusa functioned as a culturally embedded pedagogical context in which disciplinary behaviours were practiced through routines, rule adherence, repeated training, social interaction, and structured responsibility. The study contributes an implementation-oriented perspective to international research by illustrating how martial arts-based extracurricular education can support the enactment and reinforcement of discipline through interconnected school, coaching, and family contexts. The findings do not establish causal effects or long-term character internalization.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for hospital-acquired bacterial infection prediction in acute-on-chronic liver failure
abstract: BACKGROUND Hospital-acquired (HA) bacterial infections are a frequent and potentially preventable driver of early deterioration in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), yet no validated tool exists to identify high-risk patients at the time of hospital admission. AIM To develop and externally validate an interpretable admission-time machine learning (ML) model for predicting HA bacterial infection in ACLF. METHODS In this multicenter retrospective study, 3103 hospitalized patients with cirrhosis were screened across five tertiary centers in China (2016-2025), and 874 eligible patients with ACLF were included. Admission-time variables were incorporated into ML models, which were evaluated for discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Model robustness was further assessed using time-dependent discrimination, cumulative incidence, and competing-risk analyses accounting for in-hospital death, transfer, or liver transplantation. RESULTS Among 644 patients in the derivation cohort, 259 (40.2%) developed HA bacterial infections. A 12-variable Gradient Boosting Decision Tree model was selected as the final model, achieving an internally validated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.906 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.879-0.930]. Discrimination remained good in the external validation cohort (n = 230; 99 events), with an AUC of 0.890 (95%CI: 0.843-0.931). The model outperformed conventional liver disease severity scores in predicting HA bacterial infections. Risk stratification remained consistent across time-dependent, cumulative incidence, and competing-risk analyses. CONCLUSION An interpretable admission-time ML model was developed to identify patients at high risk for HA bacterial infections in ACLF. This framework may support early risk stratification and targeted infection surveillance.

title: Online calculators to predict severe Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis after pull-through surgery for Hirschsprung disease: A multicenter retrospective study
abstract: BACKGROUND Postoperative Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis (HAEC) is the most common and life-threatening complication after pull-through surgery for Hirschsprung disease (HSCR). Severe HAEC (sHAEC; Grade II and III) is associated with high morbidity and mortality, yet effective models for predicting postoperative sHAEC risk are currently rare. AIM To develop and validate a nomogram and online calculator for individualized prediction of postoperative risk of sHAEC. METHODS This multicenter retrospective study analyzed HSCR patients undergoing pull-through surgery. Using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator and logistic regression on a training cohort (n = 416), independent risk factors were identified. The nomogram was internally (n = 178) and externally (n = 303) validated. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curve. An online calculator was created. RESULTS Among 897 patients, 175 (19.5%) developed sHAEC during ≥ 2 years' follow-up. Eight independent predictors emerged: (1) Preoperative malnutrition; (2) Down syndrome; (3) Preoperative respiratory infection; (4) Preoperative enterocolitis; (5) Clinical type; (6) Postoperative indwelling rectal tube; (7) Postoperative anastomotic fistula; and (8) Postoperative intestinal obstruction. The model demonstrated strong discrimination [area under the receiver operating characteristic curves: (1) Training 0.906; (2) Internal 0.882; and (3) External 0.842], excellent calibration, and high clinical utility. A web calculator was deployed (http://ms-haec.asia/ ). CONCLUSION The developed nomogram and online calculator, incorporating eight clinical variables, predicted postoperative sHAEC risk. This tool may assist in clinical decision-making and timely intervention, potentially improving outcomes in HSCR.

title: Liver transplantation for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: From contraindication to biology-driven selection
abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) has historically been considered a contraindication to liver transplantation (LT) because early outcomes in unselected patients were marked by high recurrence and poor survival. Liver resection remains the standard curative-intent treatment when technically feasible and oncologically appropriate. Contemporary evidence challenges this binary view, suggesting that transplant benefit depends less on diagnosis or anatomy alone than on careful candidate selection and disease behavior over time. This narrative review examines LT for iCCA within current transplant oncology practice. Current evidence supports cautious consideration of LT in two distinct settings. The first is very early iCCA in cirrhotic patients, particularly solitary tumors ≤ 2 cm, for which explant-based retrospective studies have shown better outcomes than those observed in larger or multifocal disease. Evidence for this setting derives mainly from incidental or explant-based series. Selected solitary tumors ≤ 3 cm may be considered within consensus-based, guidance-based, trial-based, or registry-based frameworks after documented stability and exclusion of nodal or extrahepatic disease, although this threshold is less well validated than the 2-cm threshold. The second is unresectable, liver-limited iCCA controlled by neoadjuvant systemic therapy with or without locoregional therapy, where durable radiologic response or stability, usually for at least 6 months, serves as a dynamic test of disease behavior. Evidence for this setting derives from highly selected neoadjuvant cohorts and remains investigational. In both settings, histological confirmation when feasible, careful staging, and exclusion of nodal or extrahepatic spread are essential. LT should be framed not as routine indication expansion, but as a highly selective treatment strategy for patients with liver-limited disease and sustained disease control.

title: Computed tomography-based nomogram for predicting recurrence of gastrointestinal stromal tumors
abstract: BACKGROUND Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) exhibit a high degree of biological heterogeneity, and accurate postoperative risk stratification remains a key yet challenging issue in clinical practice. Although surgical resection is the primary treatment for localized GISTs, postoperative recurrence and metastasis remain significant clinical challenges. Various methods for predictive risk stratification based on imaging and radiomics have been proposed; however, many of these methods require complex workflows or lack direct clinical applicability. Therefore, there is an unmet need for a practical, reliable, and interpretable model based on routinely available imaging data, in order to optimize risk stratification and achieve personalized treatment plans. AIM To develop and validate a computed tomography (CT)-based prognostic model for predicting recurrence-free survival (RFS) in patients with GISTs. METHODS This retrospective study included 417 patients with curatively resected, pathologically confirmed primary GISTs. Preoperative contrast-enhanced CT features, clinicopathologic variables and postoperative treatment details were collected. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator selected key predictors, which were entered into a multivariable Cox baseline model. A random survival forest algorithm generated an additional risk score that was combined with independent predictors to create the final nomogram. Performance was assessed with the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS Enlarged feeding or draining vessels, peripheral fat infiltration, and the Ki-67 index were identified as independent predictors of RFS. The baseline model achieved a C-index of 0.829 (95% confidence interval: 0.770-0.884) in the training set. The integrated model showed a trend toward superior predictive performance, with a C-index of 0.867 (95% confidence interval: 0.822-0.913). The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves for predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year RFS were 0.932, 0.874, and 0.879 in the training set, and 0.741, 0.858, and 0.818 in the validation set, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis indicated potential clinical benefit. CONCLUSION An interpretable, CT-based nomogram integrating conventional imaging features and machine learning provides accurate prediction of recurrence in GIST patients. This model may assist in individualized risk stratification and postoperative management.

title: Deep learning for predicting high-grade dysplasia in colorectal polyps using white-light endoscopy
abstract: BACKGROUND Accurate identification of high-grade dysplasia (HGD) in colorectal polyps is important for optimizing endoscopic management and surveillance strategies. Although deep learning has shown potential for colorectal polyp characterization, the generalizability of white-light imaging (WLI)-based models across independent clinical settings remains insufficiently established. AIM To develop and externally validate a deep learning model based on routine WLI images for predicting HGD in colorectal polyps, to explore the predictive contribution of routinely available clinical variables, and to compare model performance with endoscopists with different levels of experience. METHODS In this multicenter retrospective observational study, a MobileNetV2-based deep learning model was developed using routine WLI images of colorectal polyps and externally validated in two independent tertiary hospitals. Each polyp was represented by one representative high-quality WLI image, and histopathological diagnosis was used as the reference standard. Model discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and diagnostic performance were evaluated. An exploratory clinical model based on routinely available clinical and lesion characteristics was developed as a baseline comparator. The model was further compared with endoscopists using binary HGD/non-HGD classifications in a blinded reader study. RESULTS The WLI-based model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.879 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.795-0.952] in the internal test cohort and maintained consistent discrimination in two external validation cohorts [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.814 (95%CI: 0.728-0.890) and 0.803 (95%CI: 0.719-0.896)]. The exploratory clinical model provided no clear evidence of incremental predictive value beyond image-based prediction. In the reader study, the artificial intelligence model demonstrated comparable classification performance with senior endoscopists, and superior performance compared with junior endoscopists based on binary diagnostic metrics. However, the external validation cohorts contained a limited number of HGD-positive cases, and performance estimates should therefore be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION A deep learning model based on routine WLI images showed promising and consistent performance for HGD risk stratification in colorectal polyps across three tertiary hospitals. The model may provide complementary information to support endoscopic assessment, particularly for less experienced clinicians. Prospective real-time validation in broader populations and healthcare settings is required before clinical implementation.

title: Platelet-Rich Plasma for Vulvovaginal Disorders: An Umbrella Review of Nineteen Systematic, Scoping and Narrative Reviews Published Since 2020
abstract: Background: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is offered increasingly widely for vulvar lichen sclerosus (VLS), the genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), female sexual dysfunction (FSD) and stress urinary incontinence (SUI).The number of reviews summarising this practice has grown quickly, and their consistently favourable tone is now itself used as justification for clinical adoption.Objective: To appraise, at the level of the secondary literature, what the post-2020 reviews of vulvovaginal PRP collectively establish; to reconstruct the primary-evidence layer beneath them after removing double-counted studies; and to define the minimum design and reporting standards that future trials in regenerative gynaecology must meet. Methods:We conducted an umbrella review of systematic, scoping and structured narrative reviews published from 2020 onward that addressed PRP for vulvovaginal or lower genital tract indications.Ovarian, endometrial and infertility-only reviews were excluded.Twenty-seven candidate records were retrieved and read; every extracted value was bound to the specific source page that stated it, and values that could not be confirmed on a retrieved page were recorded as not available rather than inferred.For the subset of reviews publishing an included-study list, we constructed a primary-study overlap matrix and deduplicated participants and study designs.

title: Hyaluronic Acid in Regenerative Medicine: From Molecular Weight–Dependent Signalling and the Stem Cell Niche to Musculoskeletal and Aesthetic Practice — A Comprehensive Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is the only non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan of the extracellular matrix and the molecule most often invoked to justify "regenerative" injectable therapy.The same polymer is marketed as joint lubricant, volumizer, dermal biostimulator and cell-delivery scaffold.This review reconciles that promise with clinical evidence, regulatory status, product heterogeneity and price reality.Methods: Evidence was identified in a structured, non-systematic manner through PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library, citation chaining from retrieved reviews and guidelines, official regulator and manufacturer sources (United States Food and Drug Administration [FDA] premarket-approval and clearance summaries, Federal Register, European Union guidance, Brazilian National Health Surveillance Agency [ANVISA], instructions for use), payer policies, public pricing files and focused web discovery, to 9 September 2026.Exact strings and yields were not preserved; no pooling, PRISMA-based screening, protocol registration, risk-of-bias scoring or de-novo certainty grading was undertaken, and certainty is reported as published by source syntheses.This is a narrative review, not a systematic review, umbrella review or meta-analysis.

title: A Socio-Economic Empowerment-Based Christian Religious Education Model for Congregational Poverty Alleviation in GMIT Kupang City
abstract: Poverty among church congregations is a multidimensional issue that involves not only economic limitations but also restricted access to education, human capacity development, employment opportunities, and social participation. This study aims to analyze the socio-economic conditions of congregations, examine Christian Religious Education (CRE) practices, identify socio-economic empowerment needs, and develop a contextual CRE model based on socio-economic empowerment for alleviating congregational poverty in the Evangelical Christian Church in Timor (GMIT), Kupang City Classis. This research employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive-exploratory design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and documentation involving eight church leaders selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis and validated through source and methodological triangulation. The findings reveal that congregational poverty is characterized by informal employment, unstable income, limited economic opportunities, and restricted human resource capacity, while congregations also possess social capital through fellowship, mutual assistance, and collective responsibility. CRE practices remain primarily focused on spiritual formation, whereas socio-economic empowerment has not yet been systematically integrated into congregational education. This study proposes a contextual CRE model integrating faith formation, mindset transformation, capacity development, productive economic empowerment, continuous mentoring, partnership development, and monitoring and evaluation. The study contributes theoretically by expanding the role of CRE as a transformative educational practice and practically by providing a framework for churches to develop sustainable strategies for strengthening congregational independence and poverty alleviation.

title: Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) dan Masa Depan Pastoral Konseling: Peluang, Risiko, dan Batas Teologis
abstract: Perkembangan pesat kecerdasan buatan (AI) generatif telah memunculkan pertanyaan mendasar tentang masa depan pastoral konseling, sejauh mana entitas non-personal berbasis algoritma dapat menjalankan fungsi yang selama ini menjadi domain eksklusif konselor pastoral manusia. Penelitian ini bertujuan membangun kerangka normatif tiga lapis, terapeutik, relasional, dan teologis, untuk mengevaluasi secara sistematis peluang, risiko, dan batas teologis penggunaan AI dalam konteks pastoral konseling. Metode yang digunakan adalah Systematic Literature Review mengikuti protokol PRISMA 2020, dikombinasikan dengan analisis tematik reflektif atas 52 studi final dari literatur teologi praktis dan etika digital yang dipublikasikan antara 2015 dan 2024. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa AI menawarkan aksesibilitas, konsistensi, dan skalabilitas layanan psikospiritual yang signifikan, namun secara fundamental gagal mereplikasi dimensi relasional dan kehadiran pastoral (pastoral presence) yang berpijak pada doktrin Imago Dei. Kontribusi utama penelitian ini adalah artikulasi batas epistemik teologis yang masih absen dalam literatur teologi praktis global maupun Asia Tenggara: AI dapat menopang (support) tetapi tidak dapat menggantikan (replace) fungsi pastoral yang mensyaratkan perjumpaan personal antara dua makhluk ber-Imago Dei. Implikasi praktis mencakup panduan etis bagi gereja, seminari, dan lembaga kesehatan rohani dalam mengadopsi teknologi AI secara bertanggung jawab.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Christian Religious Education: Reconstructing Teachers' Roles in Developing Students' Digital Literacy and Critical Thinking
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence, particularly generative artificial intelligence, is transforming how students access information and learn, including in Christian Religious Education. While artificial intelligence offers opportunities for personalized learning and richer engagement with biblical and theological content, it also raises concerns about inaccurate or biased religious content, over-reliance, weakened critical thinking, ethical risks, and the erosion of the relational and spiritual dimensions of faith formation. This study aims to reconstruct the roles of Christian religious education teachers in artificial intelligence-based learning so that it strengthens students' digital literacy and critical thinking within Christ-centered formation. A qualitative design using library research and conceptual analysis was employed. A corpus of 52 sources, comprising peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2026 together with seminal works and policy documents regardless of publication year, was selected through explicit criteria and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and conceptual synthesis. The synthesis indicates that artificial intelligence shifts Christian Religious Education from content transmission toward guided inquiry; that its opportunities are realized only when its risks are mediated pedagogically and ethically; that teachers' roles must be reconstructed as learning facilitators, spiritual mentors, and digital ethics guides; and that digital literacy and critical thinking can be integrated through the evaluation and theological discernment of machine-generated content. The study proposes the Christ-Centered EEDE Framework (exploring, evaluating, discerning, and embodying), which integrates these elements into a teacher-guided learning cycle and offers a testable foundation for ensuring that artificial intelligence serves, rather than replaces, faith formation.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven three-dimensional modeling of biliary strictures using magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography for quantitative assessment and stent planning
abstract: BACKGROUND Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) depicts the biliary tree three-dimensionally but is used mainly for qualitative diagnosis rather than quantitative procedural planning. Endoscopic drainage of biliary strictures, particularly hilar and intrahepatic lesions, depends on an accurate understanding of stricture location, length, ductal curvature, and branch involvement, yet MRCP information is seldom converted into reproducible measurements. Artificial intelligence (AI) may bridge this gap by transforming diagnostic imaging into quantitative, procedure-oriented geometry. We hypothesized that MRCP-derived biliary anatomy could be converted into an interpretable three-dimensional (3D) model supporting biliary stricture assessment and candidate stent-planning geometry. AIM To develop and evaluate a proof-of-concept AI workflow that converts MRCP-derived biliary anatomy into a quantitative 3D stricture model. METHODS This single-center study analyzed 384 MRCP examinations (242 controls and 142 with suspected biliary stricture). Expert-corrected masks and 3D annotations were used to train or evaluate modules for region-of-interest localization, bile duct segmentation, projection-based multi-view classification, synthetic morphology restoration, and centerline-guided tubular mesh generation. Binary stricture detection and three-class severity classification were assessed with patient-level cross-validation after excluding unavailable or task-incompatible labels. Segmentation and restoration were evaluated using Dice scores. RESULTS In 380 evaluable cases, projection-based binary classification achieved an accuracy of 0.9770, balanced accuracy of 0.9721, macro F1 score of 0.9749, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.9953. Three-class severity classification was less accurate (accuracy 0.8711), indicating that severity stratification is more difficult than binary detection. The best Dice score was 0.8113 in the segmentation comparison and 0.8944 in the extended normal-group experiment. In synthetic restoration, DiceFocalLoss produced the highest Dice score (0.7531), and lesion weighting improved reconstruction of interrupted duct segments. In anatomically simple cases, restored geometry was converted into a centerline-guided tubular mesh, whereas complex hilar or intrahepatic branching remained vulnerable to projection overlap. CONCLUSION MRCP-based AI modeling of biliary strictures is feasible for quantitative 3D assessment and exploratory stent-planning geometry. External validation and prospective clinical evaluation are required before procedural implementation.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation models for predicting pathological upgrading in endoscopically resected gastric low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia: A dual-center evaluation
abstract: BACKGROUND Gastric low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (LGIN) exhibits highly variable clinical outcomes. The discordance between histological findings from endoscopic forceps biopsy and endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) complicates the formulation of appropriate treatment strategies. AIM To evaluate a prediction framework using large language models (LLMs) enhanced with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for the pathological upgrading of gastric LGIN. METHODS We retrospectively enrolled 329 patients with 372 gastric LGIN lesions from two tertiary hospitals who underwent ESD following a pre-operative diagnosis of gastric LGIN via biopsy. A RAG knowledge base was constructed based on 28 peer-reviewed articles on LGIN upgrading. Two LLMs (DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235b) were evaluated in a zero-shot setting to generate upgrading probability predictions and reasoning reports for each lesion. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The performance of RAG-enhanced LLMs was compared with that of a generalized linear mixed model baseline and two experienced endoscopists. Subgroup analyses were also conducted. RESULTS Pathological upgrading to high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia or early gastric cancer was confirmed in 148 (40%) lesions. The AUCs for the RAG-enhanced DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235b were 0.873 [95% confidence interval (95%CI): 0.828-0.901] and 0.862 (95%CI: 0.818-0.893), respectively, demonstrating performance comparable to that of experienced endoscopists and baseline model (DeLong test, P > 0.05). Based on the maximum Youden index, DeepSeek-V3 achieved a sensitivity of 85.1%, specificity of 80.4%, positive predictive value of 74.1%, and negative predictive value of 89.1% at the optimal threshold of 0.357; Qwen3-235b achieved 84.5%, 77.2%, 71.0%, and 88.3%, respectively, at the threshold of 0.453. DCA demonstrated superior clinical utility across threshold probabilities of 15%-80%. In the subgroup analysis, RAG-enhanced LLMs maintained higher accuracy in lesions measuring 1-2 cm. CONCLUSION This study evaluated a novel RAG-enhanced framework using LLMs for predicting pathological upgrading in gastric LGIN. These models may have the potential to support clinical decision-making for ESD, pending prospective validation.

title: Large language models with supervised fine-tuning for inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis and prognosis
abstract: BACKGROUND Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, incurable condition characterized by complex complications. Effective management of IBD demands extensive physician expertise and time, presenting major challenges due to limited experience and healthcare resources. Large language models (LLMs) may serve as efficient auxiliary tools to alleviate workforce pressures and enhance the accessibility and efficiency of healthcare services. AIM To evaluate the capabilities of an LLM trained by supervised fine-tuning (SFT) in the diagnosis and treatment of IBD. METHODS In this observational study, the diagnostic and treatment capabilities of a general LLM for IBD were evaluated using cases derived from real-world electronic health records. High-quality medical records were filtered for SFT to construct a dedicated IBD-LLM, followed by a direct head-to-head comparison of IBD care performance between the IBD-LLM and resident physicians. RESULTS The general LLM demonstrated suboptimal performance in IBD diagnosis and treatment, although its response consistency and harmlessness were confirmed. In the head-to-head comparison, IBD-LLM vs resident physicians achieved scores of 2.88 vs 3.47 out of 5 in diagnostic accuracy (P = 0.001), 4.18 vs 3.47 out of 5 in humanistic care (P = 0.001), 4.39 vs 3.41 out of 5 in clinical judgment (P = 0.001), 3.88 vs 3.53 out of 5 in communication skills (P = 0.002), and 4.11 vs 3.74 out of 5 in organizational effectiveness (P = 0.003). Although the IBD-LLM demonstrated performance comparable to resident physicians in three parameters, it showed significantly lower diagnostic accuracy. No safety risks or artificial intelligence hallucinations were observed in outputs from either the general LLM or IBD-LLM. CONCLUSION A specialized LLM can be efficiently trained with limited samples using SFT, and demonstrated significant potential for assisting with medical tasks under the supervision of attending physicians.

title: Glasgow prognostic score as a predictor of decompensation in patients with primary biliary cholangitis
abstract: BACKGROUND Inflammatory activity and nutritional status are closely associated with the progression of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) and other chronic liver diseases. AIM To determine the predictive performance of the Glasgow prognostic score (GPS), modified GPS (mGPS), and high-sensitivity mGPS (hs-mGPS) for hepatic decompensation in PBC. METHODS We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study involving patients diagnosed with compensated PBC at seven hospitals between January 2013 and December 2024. GPS, mGPS, and hs-mGPS were calculated using baseline measurements of C-reactive protein (CRP), high-sensitivity CRP, and albumin levels. The endpoint was the first occurrence of hepatic decompensation during follow-up. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves (ROCs) were used to compare the predictive performance of the GPS, mGPS, hs-mGPS, Paris I, Paris II, Mayo, United Kingdom-PBC (UK-PBC), and GLOBE scores for decompensation events. RESULTS This analysis included 762 patients with compensated PBC. The median age was 56 years (interquartile range: 49-66), and 606 patients (79.5%) were female. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the 5-year decompensation rates increased progressively across higher score strata for all three indices (P < 0.0001 for all). In fully adjusted multivariate models, GPS (hazard ratio [HR] = 3.605, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.783-4.670), mGPS (HR = 3.103, 95%CI: 2.469-3.900), and hs-mGPS (HR = 3.261, 95%CI: 2.549-4.171) independently predicted decompensation risk (P < 0.0001 for all). Time-dependent ROC analysis indicated that the GPS score yielded the highest area under the curve (0.754) for predicting decompensation, followed by hs-mGPS (0.725), mGPS (0.696), GLOBE (0.663), UK-PBC (0.638), Mayo (0.624), Paris I (0.597), and Paris II (0.582), whereas the difference between GPS and hsmGPS was not statistically significant. CONCLUSION GPS, mGPS, and hs-mGPS are independent prognostic markers for decompensation in PBC. The GPS has the strongest predictive accuracy, supporting its potential clinical utility in early risk stratification and management guidance.

title: Artificial intelligence for imaging-based detection of gallbladder cancer: A systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND Early diagnosis of gallbladder cancer (GBC) remains challenging because malignant lesions can mimic benign inflammatory or polypoid gallbladder disease. Artificial intelligence (AI) imaging models have been reported for ultrasound-, computed tomography-, and radiomics-based diagnosis; however, the evidence often conflates clinical validation cohorts with image-level model-development experiments. AIM To evaluate the diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) of AI-assisted imaging for detecting GBC and to distinguish patient-level clinical validation evidence from technical benchmark studies. METHODS Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 and the PRISMA-DTA extension. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with a Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 framework tailored to AI imaging. The primary synthesis used a Reitsma bivariate random-effects model. Robustness was examined using a generalized linear mixed model following the meta-analysis of DTA implementation, leave-one-out analyses, exclusion of internal validation, modality/model subgroup analyses, and Hartung-Knapp random-effects diagnostic odds ratio analysis. RESULTS Of 485 records, 32 studies met the inclusion criteria and five patient-level validation datasets suitable for 2 × 2 reconstruction, including four independent, external, or prospective validation settings and one internal non-training validation cohort, comprising 615 patients/cases, were meta-analyzed. In these five validation datasets, AI-assisted imaging was associated with pooled sensitivity of 0.888 (95% confidence interval: 0.834-0.927) and moderate-to-high specificity of 0.838 (95% confidence interval: 0.717-0.914), with a summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.921. Prediction intervals were wider for specificity than sensitivity (0.529-0.959 vs 0.785-0.946), indicating less stable false-positive performance across settings. Because only five datasets were available, these estimates should be interpreted as preliminary and context-dependent. CONCLUSION AI-assisted imaging showed promising sensitivity and moderate-to-high specificity for GBC detection in a small set of patient-level validation datasets. However, the quantitative evidence rested on only five datasets, included heterogeneous modalities, target contrasts, models, thresholds, and validation designs, and showed greater uncertainty for specificity than sensitivity. Current evidence is most consistent with AI as a triage or second-reader adjunct requiring further external and prospective validation, not as a stand-alone diagnostic replacement.

title: Gut microbiota signatures in colorectal cancer: Evidence synthesis from umbrella review and probiotic intervention studies
abstract: BACKGROUND Aberrant alterations in the gut microbiota have been widely reported in colorectal cancer (CRC), but taxon-level associations remain heterogeneous in direction, magnitude, and reproducibility across studies. AIM To conducted an umbrella review with a second-order meta-analysis to identify reproducible CRC-associated taxa and to summarize gut microbiota changes after probiotic or synbiotic interventions. METHODS We included eligible meta-analyses of CRC-associated gut microbiota and evaluated them using AMSTAR 2 (a measurement tool to assess systematic reviews). After standardizing effect sizes and deriving missing standard errors, we performed a second-order meta-analysis to estimate pooled effect sizes, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), P values, and heterogeneity. Candidate taxa were identified using predefined criteria, and species-level findings were mapped to genera. We also added original CRC studies on probiotics and synbiotics, assessed bias using RoB 2, and combined the data via standardized mean differences (SMDs), wherever appropriate. Studies without extractable variance estimates were included in the qualitative or percentage-based synthesis. RESULTS Eleven meta-analyses of 3569 CRC patients and 3722 healthy controls were included. Frequently reported genera, such as Roseburia , Prevotella , Porphyromonas , Bacteroides , and Streptococcus , showed inconsistent association directions; therefore, reporting frequency alone could not reliably identify stable CRC-associated taxa. Seventeen genera met the predefined significance and reporting-frequency criteria and 8 retained significance in leave-one-out analyses. After heterogeneity-based filtering, Granulicatella and Peptoniphilus remained the most stable genera. Six probiotic/synbiotic intervention studies of 323 participants were included. The quality of the studies was generally low, with some missing outcome data and selective reporting. Pooled analysis revealed that Lactobacillus (SMD = 1.49, 95%CI: 0.67-2.31) and Bifidobacterium (SMD = 1.81, 95%CI: 0.60-3.03) both increased significantly, mainly reflecting supplementation and other taxa remains exploratory. After intervention, single-study SMDs and percentage-based analyses suggested possible increases in Faecalibacterium , Eubacterium , Bacillus , Staphylococcus , and Parabacteroides , and possible decreases in Fusobacterium , Candida , Enterobacteriaceae , Pseudomonas , Porphyromonas , Alloprevotella , Erysipelatoclostridium , Peptostreptococcus , Bacteroides , and Clostridium . CONCLUSION This study identifies reproducible CRC-associated microbial candidates and highlights the need to evaluate cross-study stability beyond reporting frequency. Probiotic/synbiotic interventions may alter selected microbial taxa in CRC patients, but larger shotgun metagenomics-based trials are needed to determine whether taxonomic shifts translate into ecological or metabolic restoration.

title: A Brick in the Creative Wall: The Cultural and Creative Production System Facing the Challenge of Generative Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly transforming cultural and creative industries (CCIs), yet research lacks a structured understanding of how they intervene across production processes. How and where does GenAI reshape value creation activities within the CCI production system? Building on the UNESCO cultural cycle (2009), we develop an analytical framework that maps GenAI applications across three phases of the cultural production value chain: creation, production, and distribution/consumption. It identifies how GenAI reconfigures value creation and value capture mechanisms differently across phases and sectors. Our analysis highlights emerging dynamics, including phase-specific technological dependencies, increasing feedback loops between production and consumption, and a growing technological convergence across CCIs. To illustrate these mechanisms, we present cases from Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums (GLAM). Our paper contributes to ongoing debates on digital transformation in cultural production systems, providing insights for researchers, policymakers, and cultural organizations navigating the opportunities and risks of GenAI. JEL Codes: H0, M0, M1, O4

title: The Role of Technology, Market and Design Relatedness in Export Diversification
abstract: Trade and innovation are key drivers of economic activity, promoting growth by increasing productivity and fostering competition. While the relationship between innovation and exports is well established, the specific contributions of different stages of innovation remain underexplored. This paper examines how different stages of innovation – namely technology, market, and design activities – are related to export specialization. We extend the principle of relatedness, as has recently been proposed in the literature, by incorporating multiple activities and apply the methodology to seventy-six countries for the years 2008-2022. By employing a rich set of patent, trademark, design and export data, we show that technology- and market-related capabilities serve as key drivers of new export specializations. Finally, our findings offer policymakers a multidimensional framework potentially applicable to goods and services. JEL Codes: F14, O34, O38

title: Gastronomy as a catalyst for the circular economy in tourism: a multi-case analysis of UNESCO Creative Cities in Brazil
abstract: A economia circular (EC), aplicada aos sistemas alimentares, posiciona a gastronomia como um vetor estratégico. No turismo, essa abordagem valoriza produtos locais, reduz desperdícios e mitiga emissões de carbono. Nesse contexto, o artigo tem como objetivo analisar de que forma os princípios da EC podem ser integrados aos sistemas alimentares no contexto do turismo gastronômico, visando à promoção do turismo regenerativo por meio da valorização da cultura alimentar, dos produtos locais e da redução do desperdício. A pesquisa adotou a metassíntese como procedimento metodológico, caracterizada como um estudo qualitativo voltado à análise e à interpretação integradas de achados provenientes de pesquisas qualitativas sobre um tema comum. Alinhada ao conhecimento contemporâneo sobre EC, sistemas alimentares e turismo sustentável, a pesquisa também contemplou a análise das Cidades Criativas da Gastronomia da UNESCO no Brasil: Belém, Florianópolis, Belo Horizonte e Paraty. Os resultados indicam que a gastronomia é um caminho para a transição rumo a sistemas alimentares circulares, ao fortalecer circuitos curtos de comercialização, estimular a agricultura familiar e agroecológica, valorizar a sociobiodiversidade e fomentar práticas de prevenção e reaproveitamento de resíduos alimentares. Apesar dos desafios relacionados à governança, à infraestrutura e à capacitação profissional, as cidades analisadas demonstram elevado potencial transformador, funcionando como laboratórios vivos de inovação territorial. Conclui-se que a consolidação de sistemas alimentares circulares no turismo depende da articulação entre políticas públicas integradas, da cooperação entre produtores, chefs e gestores de destinos e do reconhecimento da gastronomia como elemento central para o desenvolvimento sustentável e de baixo carbono.
