title: A Comprehensive Review of Research Trends in Aluminum Alloys: New Technologies in Microstructure Investigation and Mechanical Properties Improvement
abstract: Aluminum alloys are widely used in aerospace, automotive, and electronics due to their light weight, strength, and formability. Recent advances in electron microscopy and numerical simulation have deepened the understanding of how microstructure governs tensile strength. This study combines a bibliometric mapping of the literature with a metallurgical interpretation of the field: an initial 3,831 records (1990-2025) retrieved from Scopus were screened to 3,101 and refined to a final dataset of 2,916 documents analyzed with R-Studio (Bibliometrix) and VOSviewer. The most frequent keywords are aluminum alloys, microstructure, and tensile strength, and they are shown to map directly onto the core strengthening mechanisms of precipitation hardening, grain refinement, and recrystallization control. The average citation per article is 20.35 and the average number of authors per article is 4.67, indicating strong research collaboration. Although the annual growth rate of articles is -4.99%, research quality has increased significantly through advanced imaging such as scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM, TEM) and atom-probe tomography. Particular attention is given to coherent L12-ordered Al3RE precipitates (Al3Sc, Al3Er, Al3Yb), whose lattice misfit with the aluminum matrix controls strengthening, creep, and recrystallization resistance, with ytterbium highlighted as a low-cost alternative to scandium. International collaborations account for 16.44% of published articles. The findings confirm that coupling experimental and computational methods is essential for developing aluminum alloys with optimized mechanical properties.

title: Efficient IP Lookup Using a B-Tree on Expanded Trie
abstract: As routing tables continue to increase in size, IP address lookup has become a critical performance bottleneck in packet forwarding. A fundamental challenge arises from the variable-length nature of IP prefixes, which requires longest prefix matching (LPM) to identify the appropriate next-hop router. This paper presents BTET (B-tree on Expanded Trie), an efficient data structure designed to support high-performance IP address lookup. BTET combines the hierarchical organization of B-trees with the Controlled Prefix Expansion (CPE) technique to achieve efficient lookup and update operations. The core of the proposed structure consists of a collection of B-trees, where each expanded prefix is partitioned into multiple segments, and each segment is stored in the B-tree corresponding to its expansion level. Before insertion, every prefix is expanded using the CPE technique. Experimental results demonstrate that BTET provides high memory efficiency while requiring only a small number of memory accesses during lookup operations. These characteristics make the proposed data structure a practical and scalable solution for deployment in modern routing environments.

title: Detection of Unmarked Non-Metallic Underground Pipelines Using Fine-Grained Strontium Ferrite-Based Powders
abstract: An obvious global trend is the spread of plastic pipelines in the construction and repair of underground utilities, including gas distribution pipelines. Despite the advantages of non-metallic pipes, their use is associated with a number of specific problems characteristic of plastic materials. One of such significant problems facing the gas industry is the problem of detecting underground non-metallic utilities and selectively identifying them from adjacent facilities. Pipelines not linked to the global coordinate system in a timely manner can lead to significant economic costs in case of abnormal situations during construction and installation works. The paper investigates an original method of searching for non-metallic utilities associated with the introduction of magnetic powder into the gas flow. It is shown that in the case of the site location in the urban area it is a low-information and ambiguous method. On the contrary, in the open area, in the absence of third-party ferromagnetic interference, this method is not only potentially applicable, but deserves close attention and further research, for which the appropriate design of the test site is proposed. Potential application of the method will increase the informative value of data on the underground location of non-metallic pipelines by 15% for gas distribution pipelines of various diameters, considering the achievement of a magnetic induction level above the pipeline in the range of 60-120 nT.

title: Technological Assurance of the Quality of Slide Bearing Shells Based on Two-Stage Magnetic Abrasive Finishing
abstract: The article describes the methodology of a two-stage finishing process for slide bearing shells made of bronze. The goal of the first finishing stage was to form a base roughness profile with uniform values of the controlled parameters. Based on the results of the first stage, regression equations were derived. These equations make it possible to evaluate the effectiveness of the influence of the process variable factors (tool rotational speed, feed rate, processing time, and workpiece diameter values) of magnetic abrasive finishing on the value of the controlled parameters. The results showed that the parameters of tool rotational speed and processing time have the greatest influence. In the second stage of the experimental research, a two-factor experiment (varying the time and abrasive grain sizes) was conducted. The aim of this stage was to test the possibility of applying oil-retaining grooves onto the formed profile. The results showed that the most noticeable grooves are formed at a processing time of 6 minutes and an abrasive grain size of 350 μm. The roughness parameters did not increase significantly compared to the values after the first processing stage. The need for further research to evaluate the operational characteristics of the machined workpieces during wear testing is established.

title: Neural Network-Assisted Reliability Analysis of Optimized Steel Moment Frames Based on Seismic Collapse Safety
abstract: Rigorous collapse-capacity-based design and probabilistic reliability analysis form the foundation of performance‑based design, enabling engineers to make risk‑consistent, cost‑effective decisions under uncertainty. This study brings these two themes together in a unified framework. The first part uses a deterministic PBDO workflow for 3‑, 6‑, and 12‑story steel moment-resisting frames (MRFs) that explicitly controls collapse capacity, employing a simplified single-pushover estimator within a metaheuristic to produce baseline and multi‑level collapse safety designs. Deterministic design frameworks omit important sources of uncertainty in seismic demand and structural capacity, and they are ill‑suited to problems where the limit‑state function is expensive to compute. To address these limitations, the current study performs a probabilistic structural reliability assessment of the optimally designed frames using Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) based Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS), accelerated by surrogate modeling. The proposed approach integrates feedforward multilayer perceptron (FFMLP) neural network surrogate models with the LHS-based MCS to evaluate failure probabilities without requiring extensive nonlinear structural analyses. The numerical results clearly illustrate the efficiency and advantages of the proposed methodology.

title: AI, Neuro-Inclusion and Inclusive Development in the Global South: A Governance Framework for Equitable Participation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming education, employment, healthcare, mobility, communication, and public services, yet its benefits are not equally accessible to neurodivergent individuals, particularly in the Global South. Conventional digital inclusion approachesemphasizetechnologicalaccesswhileoftenoverlookingcognitiveaccessibility,sensory differences,communicationpreferences,anddiverse interactionpatterns.This manuscriptproposes an integrated framework for AI-enabled neuro-inclusion that places neurodiversity, accessibility, human autonomy, transparency, privacy, and participatory design at the center of responsible AI development. The framework connects technology design with institutional governance and measurable inclusion outcomes across education, employment, public services, and digital participation. It examines neuro-inclusive software development, AI-assisted sensory accessibility assessment, and accreditation-based standards as implementation mechanisms. Using India and the wider Global South as application contexts, the manuscript positions neuro-inclusion as a component of responsible innovation, equitable digital transformation, and sustainable human development

title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
abstract: The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. Each city separately trains a local deep learning model using local traffic, environmental, and disaster-related data, while only privacy-protected model updates are exchanged with a central aggregator. The proposed solution leverages secure aggregation and differential privacy to ensure data privacy and facilitate efficient cross-city knowledge sharing. Extensive experiments on multi-modal urban traffic datasets, including junction-level surveillance traffic data, highway traffic time-series data, and disaster-influenced traffic data, validate that the proposed solution outperforms state-of-the-art centralized and federated learning baselines by up to 8-12% in RMSE error while substantially mitigating privacy leakage. The results also validate enhanced anomaly detection and disaster-caused traffic disruption prediction performance across cities with limited local traffic data. The obtained results validate the effectiveness of the proposed PP-FL framework as a scalable, secure, and efficient paradigm for next-generation intelligent transportation systems.

title: Impact of Unauthorized Vehicles on Road Safety Using Machine Learning in Bangladesh
abstract: The rising number of unauthorized vehicles in rural Bangladesh has led to an alarming increase in road accidents, particularly on rural highways. Despite a significant body of research on road safety in developed countries, limited studies have focused on road safety in Bangladesh, especially concerning unauthorized vehicles. This study applies machine learning to analyze road traffic accidents involving unauthorized vehicles using data collected between 2018 and June 2023 from high-risk regions in Bangladesh, including Pabna and Sirajganj. A total of 72 accidents were examined and classified into head-on, rear-end, and pedestrian-related collisions. The traffic accident data was categorized into four distinct classes based on their causes: overspeeding, overtaking, reckless driving, and unknown causes. A total of 179 accidents were reported during the study period, with unauthorized vehicles contributing to 41.00% of the total incidents. Among the machine learning models tested, the CatBoost Classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 89%, with strong performance metrics, including an F1-score of 0.8457. The study also incorporated SHAP values to identify key predictors of accident severity, with vehicle type, weather conditions, and driver behavior being the most influential factors. Head-on collisions were the most frequent accident type, with auto vans accounting for 22.2% of cases. Reckless driving was the leading cause, primarily affecting individuals aged 25–44 years. Unauthorized vehicles, particularly auto vans, CNGs, and motorcycles, were involved in most incidents, with the Pabna–Natore corridor accounting for 56.5% of cases. These results highlight the critical role of unauthorized vehicles in traffic-related fatalities and underline the urgent need for stricter enforcement of regulations. This research provides valuable insights into the role of unauthorized vehicles in road safety and offers actionable recommendations for policymakers to reduce accidents and fatalities. The findings emphasize the need for improved legislative frameworks and better road infrastructure to enhance road safety in rural Bangladesh.

title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
abstract: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, leagility, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints.

title: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Thermo-Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Water-Cooled Photovoltaic Modules Using a Helical Pipe Network with Twisted Tape Inserts
abstract: High and spatially non-uniform temperatures reduce the electrical output of photovoltaic (PV) modules and accelerate hotspot-related degradation. While previous research has looked into water-cooled PV/T systems and the use of twisted-tape inserts as separate solutions, there's a noticeable absence of studies that combine these approaches. Specifically, there is a lack of investigation into optimizing the arrangement of cooling pipes before incorporating internal flow enhancements. Moreover, experimental evidence is essential to confirm if such a dual strategy can genuinely improve the performance without imposing significant hydraulic disadvantages. This research directly tackles these issues by introducing and validating a two-step optimization strategy for water-cooled PV/T modules. Our work commenced with a computational assessment of four different helical pipe arrangements (100 × 150, 100 × 100, 100 × 50, and 80 × 80 mm). After this initial evaluation, the most promising configuration was further refined by adding either four or ten twisted-tape inserts. The best-performing layout was then enhanced using four and ten twisted-tape inserts. Simulations in three dimensions, investigating conjugate heat transfer, were performed using ANSYS Fluent. These simulations were carried out under a heat flux load of 800 W/m², with incoming water at a temperature of 25 °C, and across a range of Reynolds numbers from 5,000 to 11,000. The configuration featuring an 80 × 80 mm layout emerged as the optimal baseline. This setup successfully lowered the average temperature of the PV surface to 45.62 °C when the Reynolds number was 11,000. Concurrently, it achieved an electrical efficiency of 16.05% and an electrical power output of 205.49 W. The subsequent introduction of ten twisted-tape inserts led to a further reduction in temperature, bringing it down to 42.30 °C. This enhancement also boosted the electrical efficiency to 16.44% and the power output to 210.48 W. To confirm these findings, experimental validation was conducted. The results from these experiments showed mean absolute percentage errors of 1.46% for the baseline setup and a slightly lower 1.23% for the configuration enhanced with inserts. An important consideration, the pumping power required for these systems remained below 3 W across all tested conditions. The distinct contribution of this research lies in its comprehensive approach, which unifies several key aspects within a single design framework. This includes optimizing the helical pipe layout, harnessing the flow enhancement provided by twisted tapes, evaluating the uniformity of temperature, and undertaking experimental validation of the thermo-hydraulic performance. This integrated methodology effectively demonstrates that improvements in hotspot management and overall electrical performance can be realized without incurring substantial demands on hydraulic energy.

title: BEHAVIORAL AND TEMPORAL FACTORS IN MALICIOUS-NODE DETECTION FOR RPL-BASED 6LoWPAN NETWORKS: A CONTROLLED SYNTHETIC STUDY
abstract: This controlled synthetic study examines how forwarding evidence, topology-oriented evidence, temporal context, and classifier choice influence malicious-node identification in RPL-oriented 6LoWPAN settings. Node behavior is characterized using inter-arrival time, packet forwarding ratio, rank inconsistency, and parent change rate. Thirty paired runs are conducted with 600 independent node profiles and 20 observations per profile, using a common decision horizon and one test prediction per node. CNN-LSTM mean F1-score increases from 72.01 ± 7.57% with a single observation to 89.11 ± 4.64% with four observations and 94.84 ± 3.09% with eight observations. The improvement from four to eight observations is significant in the main experiment but not under later attack activation, indicating that the benefit of longer behavioral histories depends on attack timing. At four observations, Random Forest achieves a mean F1-score of 92.72 ± 2.59%, compared with 89.11 ± 4.64% for CNN-LSTM, although this advantage is not consistently reproduced across sensitivity scenarios. Combining forwarding and topology evidence significantly improves performance over forwarding evidence alone and remains robust across all sensitivity analyses. Attack-specific recall reaches 100.00% for blackhole, 79.33% for selectiveforwarding, and 76.67% for the wormhole-like topology-anomaly profile. > These findings characterize behavioral observability within the controlled generator rather than operational RPL detection rates and motivate subsequent validation using packet- and topology-level traces.

title: Adversarial robustness of dental panoramic radiograph classifiers against gradient-based perturbations
abstract: Introduction: Deep learning classifiers for dental radiographs are increasingly deployed, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations is unmeasured. Methods: A frozen ResNet-18 backbone and a linear head were trained on 182 annotated teeth from the DENTEX dataset and attacked with the fast gradient sign method and projected gradient descent at budgets from 1/255 to 16/255, comparing a baseline model, an adversarially trained model and a median-filter defense. Results: The baseline classified 63.6% of held-out teeth correctly. Both attacks flipped every correctly classified tooth at a budget of 1/255. The fast gradient sign method fell to 77.1% attack success at 16/255, whereas projected gradient descent remained at 100%. Neither adversarial training nor the median filter reduced attack success, and adversarial training lowered clean accuracy to 54.5%. Conclusions: A transfer-learning dental radiograph classifier with a frozen backbone and linear head is catastrophically vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, and the simple defenses tested do not restore robustness.

title: Enhancing Elementary Students' Science Process Skills through Game-Based Learning in Science Education
abstract: Science process skills (SPS) are essential for elementary students because they enable active engagement in scientific practices such as observing, questioning, predicting, experimenting, collecting data, interpreting data, and concluding. However, science instruction still offers limited opportunities for students to engage directly in these scientific activities, tending to emphasize conceptual understanding over process. This study analyzed the effect of board game-assisted Game-Based Learning on elementary students' SPS in energy-transformation content and identified how these skills developed following the intervention. A quantitative, quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was used with 52 fourth-grade students: 24 in the experimental group and 28 in the control group. SPS were measured using a performance assessment covering seven indicators. Data were analyzed using normality and homogeneity tests followed by an Independent Sample t-Test. The experimental group's mean score increased from 66.88 to 84.17, while the control group increased from 65.18 to 77.68; the Independent Sample t-Test indicated a significant difference between groups after the intervention (t(50) = -3.593, p < .001), with a large effect size (Cohen's d ≈ 1.00). These findings suggest that board game-assisted Game-Based Learning (JoyR1D3) is a promising interactive alternative for developing elementary students' SPS.

title: Technology-Enhanced Hybrid Service-Learning in Higher Education: Insights from a Bibliometric Study
abstract: Technology-Enhanced Hybrid Service-Learning (HSL) has emerged as an innovative pedagogical approach that integrates experiential community engagement with digitally mediated learning environments in higher education. Despite its growing implementation, scholarly knowledge on the intellectual structure, development trajectory, and thematic evolution of HSL remains fragmented. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of HSL research in higher education, drawing on 154 peer-reviewed journal articles indexed in the Scopus database between 2010 and 2026. Using PRISMA-guided screening procedures and bibliometric tools including biblioMagika®, VOSviewer, and OpenRefine, the study analyses publication trends, citation patterns, influential contributors, leading institutions and countries, source titles, highly cited documents, and keyword co-occurrence networks. The findings reveal a marked acceleration in research output from 2010 onwards, coinciding with the global expansion of hybrid and online learning models. While early publications were limited in number, they demonstrated high citation impact, forming a strong conceptual foundation for subsequent scholarship. The United States leads in publication volume, whereas Malaysia and Hong Kong demonstrate particularly strong citation performance relative to output. Prominent source titles reflect the interdisciplinary nature of HSL, spanning educational technology, sustainability, and experiential learning domains. Keyword co-occurrence analysis highlights “service learning,” “higher education,” and “student engagement” as central themes, alongside growing emphasis on online learning and e-service learning modalities. Overall, the study demonstrates that Technology-Enhanced Hybrid Service-Learning represents a dynamic and increasingly mature research domain characterised by global participation, collaborative authorship, and evolving thematic integration of pedagogy and technology. By systematically mapping the field’s intellectual structure and scholarly influence, this study provides an updated foundation for future research, pedagogical innovation, and policy development in higher education.

title: Prediksi Hasil Tanaman Padi Menggunakan Random Forest dengan Seleksi Fitur Berbasis Feature Importance dan Optimasi Hyperparameter GridSearchCV
abstract: Rice production in Indonesia fluctuates due to agronomic, spatial, and climatic factors. This study develops a rice production validation model using Random Forest Regressor with feature importance-based feature selection and GridSearchCV hyperparameter optimization. Agricultural data from BPS for 2018-2024 were combined with annual NASA POWER weather data from 37 provinces in Indonesia. The model predicts rice productivity and converts the prediction into production using actual harvested area. Feature selection reduced 32 initial predictors to 16 final features. The optimized model achieved production R² of 99.79%, adjusted R² of 99.73%, RMSE of 115,600.28 tons, MAE of 61,194.75 tons, MAPE of 6.95%, and SMAPE of 6.86%. It is important to note that the high production R² of 99.79% is substantially driven by the mathematical dominance of actual harvested area as a multiplier in the production conversion formula, rather than solely reflecting the predictive power of the climate model. The core predictive performance of the model at the productivity level (R² = 75.45%, MAPE = 6.95%) more accurately represents the model’s generalization capability. Research limitations include limited historical data for newly established provinces in Papua and the relatively short study period of 2018-2024. These results indicate that the proposed method provides accurate validation for rice production analysis.

title: Pengaruh Earning Per Share, Struktur Modal, dan Kinerja Keuangan terhadap Harga Saham
abstract: This study aims to examine and empirically prove the effect of earnings per share, capital structure, and financial performance on stock prices in consumer non-cyclicals sector companies listed on the indonesia stock exchange during the 2021–2025 period. This study employed a purposive sampling method, resulting in a sample of 54 companies with a total of 270 observations. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 13, and the Random Effect Model (REM) was selected as the appropriate model. The results indicate that Earnings per Share does not have a significant effect on stock prices, and capital structure does not have a significant effect on stock prices. Meanwhile, financial performance has a significant effect on stock prices. title: Pengaruh Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Financing to Deposit Ratio (FDR), Non-Performing Financing (NPF), dan Nilai Tukar Rupiah terhadap Profitabilitas (ROA) pada PT Bank BCA Syariah Tbk Periode 2023–2025
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Financing to Deposit Ratio (FDR), Non-Performing Financing (NPF), and the Rupiah exchange rate on the profitability (ROA) of PT Bank BCA Syariah Tbk during the 2023 to Q3 2025 period. Secondary data from quarterly financial reports and Bank Indonesia exchange rates were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results show that the independent variables simultaneously have no significant effect on ROA, as indicated by an F-statistic of 0.872 with a p-value of 0.532. Although the R Square value was recorded at 36.8%, the negative Adjusted R Square value of -5.4% indicates that the research model is statistically inadequate for predicting ROA. Given the limited sample size (n = 11), these findings suggest that profitability may be influenced by factors beyond the model, although this conclusion requires further testing with a larger sample size.

title: Hybrid Intelligence as a Tool for Textual Decoding: Integrating the Literary Detective Framework in Higher Education
abstract: This paper explores the transformative integration of Hybrid Intelligence (HI) within the landscape of higher philological education, specifically operationalized through the innovative 'Literary Detective' pedagogical framework. Amidst the shifting cognitive baselines of the digital era, this study addresses the crisis of sustained deep attention by proposing a synergistic model of textual archaeology. The research focuses on the intricate process of multidimensional decoding, wherein human cultural intuition collaborates with the computational power of Large Language Models (LLMs) to excavate latent intertextual layers across a diverse literary corpus.The study provides a comparative analysis of foundational and modern texts, demonstrating how a structured Decoding Matrix facilitates the identification of complex cultural codes in the cosmological epics of Vaja-Pshavela, the impressionistic prose of Niko Lortkipanidze, and the tragic war poetry of Mirza Gelovani, alongside the works of Homer, Margaret Atwood, and Ana Kalandadze. The findings reveal that Artificial Intelligence, when utilized as a cognitive scaffold rather than a replacement for authorial voice, significantly amplifies the student's capacity to navigate intertextual networks and resolve “artificial hallucinations” through intuitive filtering. Empirical evidence suggests that this hybrid approach not only increases the efficiency of thematic identification by approximately 38% but also fosters advanced critical thinking and digital literacy. Ultimately, the paper argues for a paradigm shift in the humanities, positioning the student as an active investigator in an AI-augmented hermeneutic environment, ensuring the continued relevance of philological rigor in a post-digital academic world.

title: Narsisme yang Berkuasa dalam Representasi Relasi Kuasa Pada Film “The Housemaid” (2025)
abstract: This study analyzes how Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD) power relations are represented through the character Andrew in the film “The Housemaid” (2025). Employing a qualitative approach based on John Fiske’s semiotic analysis, the research examines 23 scenes across three levels, reality, representation, and ideology, focusing on Andrew's marital relationship with Nina and his employer-domestic worker dynamics with Millie. The findings reveal that at the reality level, Andrew's NPD power relations manifest through repetitive patterns of love bombing, gaslighting, verbal manipulation, and arbitrary punishment. At the representation level, his dominance is constructed through cinematographic techniques, specifically low-angle shots of Andrew and high-angle shots of Nina and Millie. Ideologically, the film reproduces and deconstructs patriarchy, social class, and gender-based violence, which are ultimately challenged by the women's resistance. In conclusion, the film systematically exposes normalized psychological abuse, highlighting the crucial role of media literacy.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integration in Education: Teachers’ Utilization, Perceptions, and Implementation Challenges
abstract: This study explored the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in chemistry instruction, focusing on teachers’ utilization patterns, perceptions, and the challenges they encounter. A sample of 18 chemistry teachers from various institutions participated, providing insights into the types and frequency of AI tools used, including ChatGPT, ChemCollective, and PhET Interactive Simulations. Findings indicate that generative AI tools—particularly ChatGPT—are the most widely adopted due to their accessibility, versatility, and ease of integration. In contrast, subject-specific and creative AI platforms remain underutilized, suggesting that familiarity, perceived complexity, and awareness significantly influence adoption patterns. Teachers demonstrated strongly positive perceptions of AI integration in both curriculum and instruction, recognizing its potential to enhance content delivery, student engagement, personalized learning, and the development of 21st-century skills. No significant differences were found across institutions, indicating a shared readiness to integrate AI in chemistry education. Despite these favorable perceptions, effective implementation is constrained by technical limitations, infrastructure gaps, data quality concerns, usability challenges, ethical issues, and privacy risks. Teachers also expressed concerns about over-reliance on AI and the potential reduction of meaningful teacher–student interaction, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a balanced, human-centered approach. Overall, the findings support the strategic and guided adoption of AI as a pedagogical enhancement tool rather than a substitute for professional judgment and instructional expertise. The results highlight the need for structured, discipline-specific professional development that emphasizes prompt literacy, critical evaluation of AI outputs, ethical awareness, and pedagogical alignment. Strengthening technological infrastructure, establishing sustained institutional support systems, and developing clear guidelines for responsible AI use are essential to ensure effective, equitable, and ethically grounded integration of AI in chemistry education.

title: Pengaruh Work Life Balance dan Fleksibilitas Kerja terhadap Loyalitas Karyawan dengan Work Engagement sebagai Variabel Mediasi di PT Bhumi Varta Technology
abstract: Within the context of PT Bhumi Varta Technology, where employee turnover increased by 9.5 percentage points during 2025, this study examines the effects of work-life balance and work flexibility on employee loyalty, considering both direct and indirect pathways via work engagement. The trend is hypothesized to be associated with the adoption of a hybrid work model, which may intensify work-life integration issues, increase stress, and contribute to employee burnout. A quantitative approach was used, employing survey-based data collection. The population consisted of 150 employees, and a purposive sampling method selected 110 respondents who had worked for at least one year. Data were measured using a 1–5 Likert scale. Analysis was conducted using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. Results show that work-life balance has a significant positive effect on work engagement (H1 accepted) and employee loyalty (H4 accepted). Work flexibility significantly improves work engagement (H2 accepted), but no significant direct effect on employee loyalty was found (H5 rejected). Work engagement is the strongest predictor of loyalty (H3 accepted) and significantly mediates the effects of both work-life balance (H6 accepted) and work flexibility (H7 accepted), including full mediation for the latter. The model shows moderate predictive power (R-square = 0.636).

title: Pengaruh Store Atmosphere, Service Quality, dan Brand Image terhadap Minat Beli Mahasiswa pada Kopi Kenangan Cabang MERR Rungkut Surabaya
abstract: Observing changes in the lifestyle of young people, particularly university students, coffee shops are no longer viewed merely as places to purchase coffee. Nowadays, coffee shops have also become social spaces where students can work on assignments, engage in discussions, and spend time with friends. On the other hand, the competition among coffee shops in Surabaya, particularly in the MERR area, is becoming increasingly intense. This situation encourages Kopi Kenangan MERR Rungkut branch to maintain and increase purchase intention among university students. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the influence of store atmosphere, service quality, and brand image on students’ purchase intention at Kopi Kenangan MERR Rungkut, Surabaya. research employs a quantitative approach using a causal associative research design. The population consists of university students in Surabaya who have visited at Kopi Kenangan MERR Rungkut Surabaya. The research sample consists of 96 respondent. The sampling technique used is non-probability sampling with a purposive sampling method. The data were then analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with the assistance of SmartPLS. the study shows that Brand Image is the most influential factor in increasing university students’ Purchase Intention at Kopi Kenangan MERR Rungkut Surabaya. Meanwhile, Store Atmosphere and Service Quality have positive effects, but their effects have not been proven to be significant.

title: Digital Technology Integration and Academic Performance in Tertiary Mathematics: A Meta-Analytic Review of Pedagogy and Learning Results
abstract: This study aims to assess the influence of digital technologies on undergraduate mathematics performance. A meta-analytic approach was employed, synthesized from 26 independent samples across 17 peer-reviewed articles (1990–2025), with a cumulative sample size of 2,010 participants. The findings indicate a large overall effect size (g=0.978), suggesting that digital technologies significantly enhance academic achievement compared to traditional instructional methods. Moderator analysis indicated that blended learning environments achieved the highest effect size; furthermore, the impact of digital technology integration on academic performance was most pronounced in the fields of Trigonometry and Calculus. Additionally, mathematics-specific software was found to exert a significant influence on the observed effect sizes. Furthermore, the use of standardized assessments yielded a smaller effect size compared to instructor-designed tests. Additionally, no significant differences were observed regarding student equivalence in terms of group composition. The study concludes that the impact of digital tools is contingent upon specific moderator variables; these factors should be integrated into instructional design to optimize learning outcomes in university mathematics.

title: Pengaruh Literasi Digital terhadap Etika Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence pada Mahasiswa Perguruan Tinggi
abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education has transformed the way students seek information, complete assignments, and understand academic materials. However, AI use also raises ethical issues, including plagiarism, overreliance on instant answers, and a lack of transparency in acknowledging AI assistance. This study aims to analyze the effect of digital literacy on the ethical use of AI among university students. A quantitative survey method was employed. Data were collected using a 1–5 Likert-scale questionnaire from 125 respondents, with 119 complete responses analyzed. Digital literacy was measured using 12 items, while ethical AI use was measured using 12 items. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity testing, reliability testing, correlation, and simple linear regression. The results show that digital literacy has a positive and significant effect on ethical AI use. The correlation coefficient of 0.638 indicates a strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination of 0.406 indicates that digital literacy explains 40.6% of the variation in ethical AI use. The regression equation is Y = 1.196 + 0.706X. These findings indicate that students with higher digital literacy tend to use AI more ethically, responsibly, and transparently. This study recommends strengthening digital literacy programs with an emphasis on AI ethics in higher education.

title: Chatbot Workflow Automation Using n8n as an Innovation in Digital Academic Services in Higher Education
abstract: Improving the quality of digital academic services in higher education requires systems that are fast, responsive, structured, and accountable. While chatbots are commonly used as digital service tools, their implementation often focuses on conversation rather than effective management of service processes. This study develops workflow automation using n8n, a node automation tool, to support academic service tasks. Employing the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, the research includes problem identification, solution design, artifact development, and system evaluation. The result is a modular, reusable, node-based workflow automation model that manages academic service processes. Evaluation across four different service scenarios demonstrated that the workflows operated as intended, enhancing service accessibility, process clarity, and consistency in service delivery. This model offers a practical framework for higher education institutions to adopt and implement efficient digital academic services.

title: AI and Classroom Assessment in Pre-service Teacher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Thematic Evolution, and Future Directions
abstract: Assessment preparation in teacher education remains a persistent concern as pre-service teachers are increasingly expected to design valid assessments, generate meaningful feedback, interpret learning evidence, and exercise professional judgment in AI-mediated classrooms. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of research on artificial intelligence-enhanced classroom assessment in pre-service teacher education from 2005 to 2025. Using Scopus-indexed publications, the study analyzed 344 documents from 242 sources to map publication trends, citation patterns, influential authors and institutions, geographic distribution, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence networks, and thematic evolution. Results show that the field is young but rapidly expanding, with an annual growth rate of 29.61% and a sharp increase in publications from 2022 onward, reflecting the growing influence of generative AI, ChatGPT, automated feedback, learning analytics, and intelligent learning systems. Co-citation analysis revealed three intellectual foundations: teacher knowledge and research foundations, generative AI-mediated pedagogical practice, formative feedback and automated assessment. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified four major thematic clusters: AI integration and ethical teacher education, intelligent learning systems and data-driven student learning, AI-supported feedback and personalization, and assessment analytics and evidence-based grading. The findings suggest that AI-enhanced classroom assessment is not merely a technological issue but a pedagogical and professional concern requiring assessment literacy, AI literacy, ethical judgment, and teacher agency. The study contributes a field-level understanding of this emerging research domain and highlights the need for more focused, ethical, and context-sensitive studies on how pre-service teachers design, evaluate, and use AI-supported classroom assessments.

title: Eksplorasi Model Smart Halal Business Incubator Berbasis Artificial Intelligence untuk Mendukung Transformasi Digital UMKM Halal di Kabupaten Deli Serdang
abstract: The global halal industry has experienced rapid growth, prompting the Indonesian government to strengthen the halal MSME ecosystem through certification, mentoring, and digitalisation programmes. However, halal MSMEs in developing regions such as Deli Serdang Regency still face constraints, including limited mentor availability, restricted market access, slow halal certification processes, and the low utilisation of artificial intelligence (AI) in business incubation. This study aims to explore an AI-based Smart Halal Business Incubator model that can support the digital transformation of halal MSMEs in Deli Serdang Regency. The study employs an exploratory qualitative approach using the systematic grounded theory strategy of Strauss and Corbin, involving halal MSME actors, academics, local government, halal process assistants, business incubator managers, investors, and halal certification bodies as purposively selected informants until data saturation was reached. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, FGDs, observation, and documentation, and were analysed through open, axial, and selective coding. The findings yield a new conceptual framework, the AI-Driven Smart Halal Business Incubation Framework (ASHBI Framework).

title: Konstruksi Makna Iklan Pornografi Terselubung pada Pengguna Platform X (Studi Kualitatif dengan Perspektif Gender pada Pengguna Aktif)
abstract: The circulation of disguised pornographic advertisements on Platform X reflects the misuse of digital public space through hijacked viral topics, censored images of women’s bodies, and affiliate links promoting adult products. This study explores how active Platform X users interpret this phenomenon from a gender perspective. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the research draws on Berger and Luckmann’s Social Construction Theory, van Zoonen’s Gender and Media Consumption Theory, and Sandra Harding’s Standpoint Theory. Eight active users, including four men and four women aged 18–35, were purposively selected. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, digital documentation, and a literature review. The findings show that male participants viewed these advertisements as information disruption and exploitation of women’s bodies, while female participants associated them with insecurity, image misuse, and objectification. Most users responded by ignoring, blocking, or reporting the accounts.

title: The Effect of Generative AI and Gamification on Enhancing Students’ Motivation Based on the ARCS Model
abstract: High school biology learning is often hindered by abstract concepts and cognitive overload, leading to low student motivation. Although generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and gamification show instructional potential, their combined motivational effects remain underexplored. Grounded in the ARCS model, this study examined the impact of integrating ChatGPT-based GenAI and gamification on students’ Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. A longitudinal quasi-experimental repeated measures design was conducted with 52 high school biology students over eight weeks. Motivation was measured at four time points using a validated ARCS questionnaire and analyzed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results showed significant improvements across all ARCS dimensions from pre- to post-intervention (p < .001). Attention and relevance increased steadily, confidence improved in later stages, and satisfaction rose overall. Reported challenges included limited personalized AI feedback, competition-induced anxiety associated with leaderboard-based competition, and increased cognitive load resulting from complex AI-generated content. The findings indicate that GenAI-supported gamification can enhance motivation in biology learning when supported by careful pedagogical design.

title: Toward Prompt Literacy in AI-Assisted EFL Writing: A Conceptually Driven Narrative Review
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in English as a foreign language (EFL) writing for idea generation, planning, drafting, feedback, revision, and editing. However, its educational value depends not only on model capability but also on the quality of learners’ interactions with AI. This conceptually driven narrative review examines how prompt literacy has been conceptualized, its core dimensions, its role across the writing process, and its pedagogical and research implications. A transparent review procedure was used to synthesize 46 recent empirical studies and review papers published from 2023 to early 2025. The findings conceptualize prompt literacy as a multidimensional competence encompassing operational, strategic, evaluative, metacognitive, and ethical capacities. These capacities enable learners to define writing goals, obtain useful support, evaluate AI-generated outputs, preserve authorial voice, and integrate feedback responsibly. The review argues that prompt literacy should be treated as an explicit pedagogical objective rather than an incidental technical skill. It proposes an integrative framework linking learner conditions, prompt literacy dimensions, writing-process functions, and educational outcomes, while offering a clearer conceptual foundation and a practical agenda for instruction and future research in AI-assisted EFL writing.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Struktur Modal, dan Pertumbuhan Penjualan terhadap Financial Distress pada Perusahaan Subsektor Konstruksi BUMN yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2019–2024
abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of profitability, capital structure, and sales growth on financial distress in state-owned construction subsector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2019–2024 period. Using purposive sampling, four sample companies were observed over six years, yielding 24 observations. This study adopts a quantitative associative approach, utilizing secondary data drawn from the companies' annual financial statements. Panel data regression analysis was conducted using the Common Effect Model (CEM) with the aid of EViews software. The results indicate that, partially, profitability measured by Return on Assets (ROA) has a positive and significant effect on financial distress, with a t-statistic of 4.453947 > t-table of 2.08596 and a significance value of 0.0002 < 0.05. Capital structure measured by the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) has a negative and significant effect on financial distress, with a t-statistic of −2.503676 and a significance value of 0.0211 < 0.05. Sales growth has no significant effect on financial distress, with a t-statistic of 1.032783 < t-table of 2.08596 and a significance value of 0.3140 > 0.05. Simultaneously, the three variables have a significant effect on financial distress, with an F-statistic of 27.36258 > F-table of 3.098 and a significance value of 0.000000 < 0.05. The Adjusted R² of 77.47% indicates that these three variables explain 77.47% of the variation in financial distress, while the remaining 22.53% is influenced by factors outside the research model.

title: Analisis Sentimen Masyarakat terhadap Kebijakan Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) di X Menggunakan Metode Support Vector Machine (SVM)
abstract: The Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) policy has elicited diverse responses on social media platform X, necessitating sentiment analysis to objectively understand public opinion. This study employs Support Vector Machine (SVM) with TF-IDF weighting to classify 3,796 opinion data into positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. Results show the SVM model achieves an accuracy of 76.05%. Public perception is predominantly positive (1,431 data), followed by neutral (1,258), and negative (1,107). Word Cloud analysis indicates optimism based on hopes for improved student nutrition, while negative opinions highlight concerns about food safety and budget transparency. In conclusion, MBG enjoys strong public support, but the government should prioritize food safety and transparent financial management to reduce public unrest. Identifying negative sentiments provides a basis for critical evaluation and future policy improvements.

title: Human-AI Communication Symbiosis: How Educators Reconstruct Authority and Identity in the Algorithmic Era
abstract: The present schooling system is currently facing a dual disruptive crisis, spurred by the encroachment of social media algorithms and generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). While these forces impact the way students learn and think about information, they also induce an epistemological overhaul in the ecology of instructional communication. Students, with their visual rhetorical frameworks from digital platforms and the use of AI for analytical processing, present an apparent disciplinary crisis for their educators-a communication crisis in disguise. Applying Karl Weick's Sensemaking theory, this paper examines school leaders and Guidance Counselors in Samarinda, Indonesia's understanding of these ambiguities and reconceptualization of their roles. Through qualitative case studies based on teachers' pedagogical narratives, this study shows that teachers' epistemological authority is diminishing as they negotiate the hegemonic algorithmic communication. They respond to the students' fear of cognitive degradation by reorienting from a "knowledge transmitting" communicative practice towards "ethical verifiers" and "empathetic listeners." A Human-AI symbiosis is being created with the machine as information provider and humans as ethical validators and empathic listener. Implications were made for the development of policies related to algorithmic communication literacy and the application of tactical empathy in the classroom.

title: Pengaruh Work-Life Balance dan Perceived Organizational Support terhadap Turnover Intention pada PT ISS Facility Services di Bintaro, Tangerang Selatan
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the effect of Work-Life Balance and Perceived Organizational Support on Employee Turnover Intention at PT ISS Facility Services Bintaro Tangerang Selatan, both partially and simultaneously. The method used is quantitative with an associative descriptive approach. The population in this study was 63 employees of PT ISS Facility Services, with a sample of 63 respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression tests, and hypothesis tests (t-test and F-test) with the help of SPSS version 26. The results of the partial analysis show that the Work-Life Balance variable (X1) has a negative and significant effect on Turnover Intention (Y), so that H0 is rejected and H1 is accepted. The variable Perceived Organizational Support (X2) has a negative and significant effect on Turnover Intention (Y), so that H0 is rejected and H2 is accepted. Simultaneously, Work-Life Balance and Perceived Organizational Support have a positive and significant effect on Turnover Intention, indicated by the calculated F value of 56.282 > Ftable 3.15, and a significant value of 0.000 < 0.05, so that H₀ is rejected and H3 is accepted. The R Square value of 0.652 shows that the two independent variables are able to explain 65.2% of the variation in Turnover Intention, while 34.8% is influenced by other factors outside the research. Thus, the regression model used is declared feasible and able to explain the contribution of the variables Work-Life Balance and Perceived Organizational Support to Turnover Intention at PT ISS Facility Services Bintaro Tangerang Selatan.

title: Effect of AI-Based Learning Tools on Student Engagement and Academic Performance in Higher Education: A Self-Determination Theory Perspective
abstract: The study aimed to evaluated how students use of AI-based learning tools shapes their engagement and academic performance in higher education using the self-determination theory (SDT). The study investigated how the three psychological need dismissions of students which are autonomy, competence, and relatedness according the SDT are supported by their use of AI-based learning tools. A cross-sectional survey research design was used in the study. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire from 452 undergraduate computing students who were purposively sampled based on their use of AI-based learning platforms. From the finding of the study, the students indicated that, AI-based learning tools support their autonomy needs through self-paced, personalized and self-directed learning. The corrective immediate feedback feature of AI-based learning tools also supports their confident and mastery of complex concepts. However, their relatedness need was least satisfied which reflects a limitation of AI-based learning tools as they fail to replicate genuine peer connections. All the three dimensions were positively and significantly correlated with academic performance which was measured with their grade point average (GPA). Competence emerging as the having strongest correlation with academic performance (r = .387, p < .01), followed by autonomy (r = .241, p < .01), and relatedness (r = .198, p < .01). The findings suggest that AI tools support key psychological needs associated with student engagement, although their contribution to academic performance appears indirect and mediated through motivational processes.

title: Automatic Evaluation of Open-Ended Mathematics Questions with Machine Learning
abstract: The main purpose of this research is to develop an effective and objective scoring model for evaluating open-ended mathematics questions using machine learning algorithms predicting the academic performance of secondary school students in mathematics. Data was collected from 350 fifth-grade secondary school students, and the responses were digitized. For the classification of student answers, state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), were employed. The study utilized TF-IDF and BoW techniques to convert the text-based answers into numerical representations. Key features were then extracted from this digitized text data using the Chi-square (Chi2) feature selection method. The classification models were evaluated using performance metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall. Among the algorithms tested, the SVM model combined with the TF-IDF method achieved the highest performance, with 96.57% accuracy and a 96.49% F1 score.

title: Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical QC and QA and its Applications across the Industry
abstract: Quality Control (QC) and Quality Assurance (QA) are key elements in the pharmaceutical sector. They help to ensure the safety, efficacy and consistency of medicines. This article discusses the purpose of QC and QA for pharmaceutical manufacturing in the modern era and outlines their development, principles and problems relating to the application of technology and universal quality standards. The article reaffirms the need for continuous and seamless improvement in the maintenance of quality system improvements that are responsible for global health standards and that can be applied to licensed drugs in a wide range of settings, ensuring the effectiveness of medicines delivered to patients in a sustainable manner. QC and QA are important components in pharmaceutical production. Their combined function is to ensure that all products are safe, efficient and reliable. As the industry evolves and moves toward digitalization, automation and data-centric systems, QC and QA evolve from reactive functions to predictive and preventive tools. Continuous improvements, regulatory compliance and the adoption of technology will shape the future of pharmaceutical quality. This paper also analyzes the beneficial use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the pharmaceutical sector throughout all phases, from drug discovery to drug development, as well as in various departments. Besides necessitating less human labor, it also improves the efficacy of clinical research and pharmaceutical output while diminishing the likelihood of mistake. The report examines the existing challenges in the implementation of AI within the pharmaceutical sector. Furthermore, it evaluates existing challenges and proposes remedies.

title: MediBot: Healthcare Assistant
abstract: Healthcare systems over the world are facing a lot of pressure. This is because there are many patients and not enough healthcare professionals. Also, some people do not have access to medical advice when they need it. The MediBot is a computer program that uses intelligence to talk to people about their medical symptoms. People can tell MediBot what is wrong with them in their words. Then MediBot tries to figure out what might be wrong. Suggests some over-thecounter medicines that people can buy without a prescription. MediBot uses a special language system called BioMistral-7B (ResearchGate, n.d.). It also uses information from the RxNorm and FDA to ensure the medicine suggestions are safe and correct. The program has a user-interface that people can interact with. It also has a backend system that interprets symptoms checks for safety and validates medicines. In a test MediBot was able to correctly identify some common medical conditions. It also suggested some over-the-counter medicines that are normally recommended for those conditions. These early results show that MediBot can be a tool for people to get some basic medical help. This is especially true in places where people do not have access to healthcare professionals. However people should still go see a doctor for a medical consultation. MediBot is not a replacement for a doctor (*ScienceDirect). Mediterr. Bot*. system is a starting point for people who need medical help. *Mediterr. Bot*. can help people with medical conditions and suggest some, over-the-counter medicines.

title: Prescribing Change: Implementing an AI-Driven Smart Pharmacy Framework in Ujjain
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study assessed operational, financial and technology-adoption challenges among retail pharmacies in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, and used the findings to design a context-appropriate AI-driven smart pharmacy framework. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional descriptive survey with mixed-methods instrumentation was conducted among 56 retail pharmacies across four geographic zones of Ujjain using a 26-item questionnaire. Quantitative responses were analysed using frequencies, percentages, descriptive statistics and cross-tabulations; open-ended responses were coded thematically. Results: Thirty-seven pharmacies (66.1%) reported no digital billing or inventory system. Thirty-seven (66.1%) experienced stock shortages at least once or twice per month. Twenty-six (46.4%) reported monthly inventory/expiry losses of ₹5,000-₹20,000 and five (8.9%) reported losses above ₹20,000. The manuscript's conservative midpoint calculation estimated collective monthly loss at ₹5.125 lakh. The leading adoption barrier was data-entry time (42.9%), followed by training difficulty (28.6%) and software cost (26.8%). Forty-seven respondents (83.9%) were willing to adopt an AI system immediately or conditionally, while 36 (64.3%) preferred a fixed monthly fee of ₹1,500. Conclusion: The findings identify a substantial usability and affordability gap rather than simple rejection of technology. The proposed RxScan framework integrates smart billing, inventory and expiry management, pharmacist-supervised prescription OCR, ordering and analytics. It remains a proposed design and requires prospective evaluation before effectiveness claims.

title: The Evolving Role of Clinical Pharmacists in Pre-, Peri-, and Post-Operative and Critical Care Settings: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Surgery is increasingly recognized as a complex, longitudinal therapeutic process spanning preoperative preparation, anesthesia, intraoperative care, and postoperative recovery rather than an isolated operating room event. Because this continuum is highly medication-intensive and subject to challenges like polypharmacy, rapid drug administration, physiological instability, multiple transitions of care, and communication failures, the perioperative environment carries a high risk for preventable medication errors. This review explores the evolving role of the clinical pharmacist, transitioning from a passive dispenser to an active, multidisciplinary collaborator throughout the surgical pathway. In the preoperative phase, clinical pharmacists improve patient safety by constructing a best possible medication history, clarifying continuation or cessation plans for high-risk home therapies (such as anticoagulants and antidiabetics), and delivering patient education to reduce morning-of-surgery non-adherence. In the intraoperative phase, they support anesthesia providers through system-level and case-level interventions, including the standardization of medication trays and labeling, antimicrobial prophylaxis stewardship, and multimodal analgesic design. Postoperatively, pharmacists collaborate with anesthesiologists to optimize acute pain management, support opioid stewardship, manage thromboembolism prophylaxis, and coordinate comprehensive discharge reconciliation to prevent drug duplication or omission. Collaborative models-such as joint acute pain services and pre-anesthesia consultations-render medication reviews clinically actionable and significantly enhance therapy optimization. Although challenges like staffing constraints, training gaps, and inconsistent clinical integration persist, the future of perioperative pharmacy lies in proactive, technology-enabled care incorporating clinical decision support, barcode administration, and artificial intelligence to solidify clinical pharmacists as core contributors to surgical patient safety.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Quality by Design in Pharmaceutical Formulation Development: Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
abstract: The development of pharmaceutical formulations is changing. It is moving away from trial-anderror ways. Now modern approaches rely on science and data. Quality by Design or QbD offers a structured way to develop medicines. It starts with defining the Quality Target Product Profile or QTPP. Then it identifies Critical Quality Attributes or CQAs. It also looks at Critical Material Attributes or CMAs and Critical Process Parameters or CPPs. Design of Experiments or DoE helps in planning studies. This leads to the creation of a design space and a control strategy. Traditional QbD methods may not work well when variables are complex. They may not handle effects or strong interactions between factors. Artificial intelligence machine learning and predictive models can help. These tools can find patterns in data from experiments, formulations and manufacturing. This review looks at how AI fits into every stage of formulation development. It covers preformulation excipient selection, compatibility prediction, formulation optimization and predicting CQAs. It also includes identifying CMAs and CPPs. AI helps with process monitoring, Process Analytical Technology or PAT design space development and control strategy design. Applications are shown in solid dosage forms, modified-release systems, nanoparticulate and lipid-based formulations, continuous manufacturing, personalized medicines and 3D-printed medicines. Some challenges exist. These include data, overfitting models, models that are hard to understand lack of validation difficulties in scaling up regulatory issues and the need for diverse expertise. New ideas, like twins, continuous process verification, hybrid models that combine mechanics and AI generative AI and federated learning may push the field forward. In the end AI should support science not replace it. Experimental verification and mechanistic understanding are still essential.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Biomarkers for Alzheimer's Disease: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by amyloid-β plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles, necessitating early and accurate diagnosis for effective intervention. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced the discovery and interpretation of AD biomarkers by enabling the integration of complex, multimodal datasets, including neuroimaging, molecular, genetic, and digital biomarkers. AI-driven approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, have demonstrated high accuracy in identifying early pathological changes, predicting disease progression, and distinguishing AD from mild cognitive impairment. Emerging digital biomarkers derived from speech, motor activity, cognitive tests, and wearable sensors further expand non-invasive diagnostic capabilities. Despite promising results, challenges such as data heterogeneity, lack of external validation, limited interpretability ("black-box" models), and difficulties in clinical translation remain substantial barriers. Future research is expected to focus on multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, longitudinal modelling, and personalized prediction frameworks, along with improved standardization and regulatory validation. AI-based biomarker research holds potential to transform early diagnosis, prognosis, and precision medicine in Alzheimer's disease.

title: ADVANCED TECHNIQUES FOR OCCLUSION DETECTION AND CLASSIFICATION IN FACIAL RECOGNITION SYSTEMS
abstract: Performance degradation under partial or complete occlusion of key facial regions, caused by items such as face masks, scarves and sunglasses, remains one of the most persistent obstacles facing modern facial recognition systems. Overcoming this limitation matters for the dependable operation of security, surveillance, access control and authentication platforms that must function in unconstrained, real-world settings. This research introduces a hybrid facial recognition framework built around two complementary mechanisms: Canny edge-based preprocessing, which sharpens structural facial contours, and a targeted data augmentation pipeline, which increases the diversity of training examples through synthetic and geometric transformations. Together, these mechanisms were designed to strengthen the model's reliance on occlusion-resistant structural cues rather than raw pixel intensity. The framework was tested on two widely used public benchmarks, Labeled Faces in the Wild and the AR Face Database, augmented with artificially generated masks, sunglasses and scarf occlusions to mirror real-world conditions. A convolutional neural network trained from scratch served as the recognition backbone, taking single-channel grayscale or edge-map images as input. > Recognition performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, False Acceptance Rate (FAR), and False Rejection Rate (FRR). > Across all occlusion types, the proposed pipeline outperformed a baseline model trained directly on raw images, with average recognition accuracy rising by more than 10 percentage points alongside parallel gains in precision, recall and F1 score. Average FAR decreased from 6.8% in the baseline model to 3.4% in the proposed framework, while FRR decreased from 9.1% to 5.7%, demonstrating improved verification reliability. Because the same network architecture was used in every condition, these gains can be attributed specifically to the preprocessing and training strategy rather than to added model complexity. The results indicate that pairing edge-based structural enhancement with augmentation offers a lightweight yet effective route to occlusion-robust facial recognition, with clear relevance for deployment in real-world security and authentication contexts.

title: Global Health Sustainability: Next-Generation Healthcare Models and Pharmaceutical Innovations
abstract: Global Health Sustainability: Next-Generation Healthcare Models and Pharmaceutical Innovations presents a comprehensive exploration of emerging paradigms that are transforming healthcare systems and pharmaceutical sciences in the pursuit of sustainable development. As healthcare systems worldwide confront unprecedented challenges - including demographic transitions, climate change, emerging infectious diseases, antimicrobial resistance, rising healthcare costs, and unequal access to quality healthcare - the need for innovative, resilient, and sustainable healthcare models has become increasingly critical. This edited volume examines how multidisciplinary research, technological advancements, and evidence-based policy interventions can collectively contribute to building equitable, efficient, and future-ready healthcare systems. The book integrates contemporary research from the fields of healthcare management, pharmaceutical sciences, digital health, biotechnology, public health, engineering, and health policy, offering a holistic understanding of global health sustainability. It explores foundational concepts such as healthcare sustainability frameworks, universal health coverage, community-based healthcare, and One Health approaches before progressing to advanced topics including digital health ecosystems, artificial intelligence, machine learning, health informatics, precision medicine, smart diagnostics, and intelligent clinical decision-support systems. The volume further highlights cutting-edge pharmaceutical innovations encompassing advanced drug delivery systems, nanomedicine, biologics, biosimilars, precision therapeutics, pharmacovigilance, green pharmaceutical manufacturing, and regulatory science, emphasizing their role in improving healthcare accessibility, safety, and long-term sustainability. Designed as a valuable reference for researchers, academicians, healthcare practitioners, pharmaceutical professionals, postgraduate students, policymakers, and industry stakeholders, this volume bridges the gap between scientific research and practical implementation. By integrating theoretical foundations with emerging technologies and policy perspectives, Global Health Sustainability: Next-Generation Healthcare Models and Pharmaceutical Innovations contributes meaningfully to the global discourse on sustainable healthcare and provides a roadmap for advancing innovative, inclusive, and resilient healthcare systems capable of meeting the evolving health needs of populations worldwide.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Credit Card Approval Prediction Using Class Imbalance Handling Methods in the PyCaret AutoML Framework
abstract: Credit card approval processes are often performed manually, leading to inefficiencies, higher operational costs, and inconsistent decision-making. This study comparatively evaluates several machine learning models under different class imbalance handling strategies to predict credit card approval using the PyCaret AutoML framework. Two experimental scenarios were conducted on a dataset of 25,128 credit card applications, namely PyCaret's built-in SMOTE-based imbalance handling and random undersampling. In the SMOTE-based scenario, the Random Forest model achieved high accuracy, but its recall for the minority class was only 36.11%. In contrast, random undersampling produced more balanced performance, with the Gradient Boosting model achieving 100% recall. These findings indicate that class imbalance handling plays a critical role in credit card approval prediction, and that random undersampling provides more reliable minority-class detection than PyCaret's built-in SMOTE approach for the evaluated dataset.

title: Beyond technology: Scientific taste and judgment in nutritional science
abstract: Nutritional science is entering an era of unprecedented technological possibilities. Artificial intelligence, multi-omics, and precision nutrition are expanding our ability to generate and integrate information, but not necessarily our ability to understand what matters. In this Perspective, I reflect on the qualities that define a great nutritional scientist in this changing landscape, drawing on experiences accumulated throughout my career in clinical and nutritional research. I argue that scientific taste, understood as the ability to recognize important questions, choose methods that serve them, and distinguish meaningful findings from statistical or biological signals, is becoming increasingly important. I discuss the challenges of moving from association to causation, determining whether precision nutrition genuinely improves health, and interpreting increasingly complex data and artificial intelligence. Scientific progress also requires intellectual humility, learning from failure, and communicating uncertainty responsibly. Finally, I reflect on scientific leadership and mentorship as essential contributions to the future of our discipline. The most enduring legacy of a scientist may not be the number of publications or the sophistication of the tools used, but the people helped to become independent scientists and the questions they are encouraged to pursue. Technology can increase the power of science. Scientific taste determines where that power should be directed.

title: Analisis Perbandingan Kinerja Arsitektur CNN Dan Transformer dalam Klasifikasi Gambar AI-Generated dan Gambar Asli
abstract: The advancement of generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of increasingly realistic facial images that are difficult to distinguish from authentic images, thereby creating a need for automated classification methods capable of maintaining both accuracy and consistency in detection. This study compares the performance of two deep learning architecture groups, namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformers, for the binary classification of AI-generated images and real images. Four models were evaluated: ResNet50 and MobileNetV2 as CNN representatives, and Vision Transformer (ViT) and Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT) as Transformer representatives. The dataset was obtained from the 140k Real and Fake Faces dataset on Kaggle, with 28,000 images used in a balanced distribution: 20,000 images for training, 4,000 for validation, and 4,000 for testing. The experimental workflow followed the CRISP-DM framework, comprising business and data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, and deployment. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix, and classification report. The results show that DeiT achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 86.98%, precision of 86.81%, recall of 87.20%, and F1-score of 87.00%, followed by MobileNetV2, ViT, and ResNet50. In aggregate, the Transformer-based models achieved an average accuracy of 79.5%, which was 7% higher than that of the CNN-based models. The DeiT model was subsequently implemented in a Gradio-based prototype application capable of receiving user-uploaded images, performing inference, and displaying the predicted classification label along with its confidence score.
