title: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Evaluating Class Imbalance and Rare-Attack Observability in IoT Security Benchmarks
abstract: IoT intrusion-detection studies often treat a benchmark as adequate once it is large, recent, and widely used.That assumption can fail.This study audits five public IoT and IIoT security benchmarks-CICIoT2023, Edge-IIoTset, ToN-IoT, BoT-IoT, and IoT-23-from their published class populations and introduces no synthetic classifier results; the audit combines Shannon entropy, Hill diversity, Simpson concentration, Gini inequality, rank-frequency tail fitting, rare-class observation probability, Wilson uncertainty, and a constrained power-tempered sampling model.Across the five corpora, record counts range from 461,043 to 73,370,443, normalized entropy from 0.421 to 0.600, and effective Shannon diversity from 2.20 to 3.98 classes.Size is a poor proxy for label adequacy.IoT-23 is the clearest case: its 6.05 million records include a singleton class, so a random 1% sample has only about a 1% probability of observing that label, while the worst-case Wilson half-width for a class-conditioned proportion is 0.445.We then define q i (τ) = p τ i / ∑ k p τ k and prove that its entropy is non-increasing in τ; at a 1% training budget with a target of 25 expected observations in the rarest class, the minimum-flattening exponent is 1.000 for CICIoT2023, 0.855 for Edge-IIoTset, 0.807 for ToN-IoT, 0.954 for BoT-IoT, and 0.450 for IoT-23.The last case needs an approximately 2,500-fold uplift of the singleton label.Such an uplift changes training exposure to one observation; it cannot create independent evidence.The resulting audit protocol therefore separates training rebalancing from evaluation validity and gives quantitative checks that can be applied before IoT benchmark results are interpreted as class-wide security evidence.

title: Sustainability through IoT and Big Data Analytics in Tertiary Industry: A Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: The tertiary industry is increasingly influenced by digital technologies that support service efficiency, data-driven decision-making and sustainability-oriented transformation.This study reviews the way the Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data Analytics (BDA) contribute to sustainability in service sectors, including healthcare, education, tourism, hospitality, logistics, transport, finance and smart-city services.A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis were conducted using Scopus and Web of Science for records dated from 2015 through 28 February 2025.From 1,969 initial records, 551 were used for bibliometric and metadata analysis and 136 studies were included in qualitative synthesis.The publication trend, productive sources, authors, countries, subject areas, keywords and science-mapping pattern were studied by using Bibliometrix, Biblioshiny and VOSviewer.The findings show rapid growth after 2019 and strong concentration in computer science, engineering, smart healthcare, smart cities and digital sustainability research.The main contribution is an integrated service-sector synthesis showing that IoT functions as the sensing and connectivity layer, while BDA, AI, cloud-edge architectures, blockchain and predictive analytics convert service data into monitoring, optimization, decision support and automation.Sustainability outcomes appear across environmental, economic and social dimensions, including energy savings, emissions reduction, waste recovery, cost efficiency, healthcare access, inclusion and service quality.Finally, the review concludes that IoT and BDA, among other factors, have sustainable value if supported by governance, data quality, cybersecurity, interoperability, skills and organizational readiness.

title: Baseline of the energy management system for an agrivoltaic complex in the Yaqui Valley
abstract: This article presents the development of an energy baseline for an agrivoltaicsystem located in the Yaqui Valley, Sonora, Mexico, in accordance with ISO 50001:2018.The baseline was established by quantifying electricity and fuel consumption (gasolineand diesel) associated with agricultural activities, including irrigation, planting, andharvesting. Energy data were analyzed by two-month periods, and a linear regressionmodel was applied to the months with the highest activity, excluding low-consumptionperiods to avoid distortion. The consumption analysis was performed by dividing thetotal energy consumption during the corresponding period by the number of hectaresharvested. The results revealed that fuel use accounts for a significant share oftotal energy consumption, underscoring the need to evaluate all energy sources.The resulting baseline model enables disaggregation of fixed and variable loads andserves as a valuable tool for performance monitoring, energy audits, and continuousimprovement strategies. This baseline can be used as a reference for future energymanagement initiatives in similar agricultural settings.

title: Comprehensive Review of IoT-based Smart Agriculture: Technologies, Applications and Barriers
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) into agriculture is increasingly transforming conventional farming practices into intelligent, connected, and data-driven systems, offering opportunities to enhance productivity, and resource-use-efficiency and promote sustainable food security.This study presents a comprehensive systematic literature review of IoT-based smart agriculture, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA 2020) framework.A total of 203 peer-reviewed publications between 2020-2024 were systematically reviewed to examine three interconnected dimensions; IoT technologies, agricultural applications, and implementation barriers.The technological analysis covers sensing technologies, embedded controllers, communication protocols, and computing architectures with particular attention to programmable logic controllers (PLCs), ESP32, microcontrollers, and Raspberry Pi platforms, wireless sensor networks, long range wide area network (LoRaWAN), NB-IoT, Zigbee, and cloud, edge, and hybrid computing architectures in supporting data processing, intelligent analytics, and real-time decision-making approaches.Practical applications-oriented analysis identifies enormous contributions in crop monitoring, precision farming, livestock management, irrigation automation, soil health monitoring, and pest and disease management.Across these domains, we then reviewed the improving performance of IoT technologies, including crop yield increases of up to 78%, water-use efficiency of up to 64% in crop-monitoring applications, water-use efficiency improvements of approximately 21-48% in smart irrigation systems, and pesticide-use reductions of 43-82% in selected pest and disease management applications.Despite these benefits, their widespread adoption remains constrained by high-initial and maintenance costs, inadequate rural connectivity and digital infrastructure, limited technical expertise and energy, interoperability limitations, concerns of data security and privacy challenges.In response to these challenges, we examined an emerging approach, including low-cost open-source platforms, resilient and self-healing hardware architecture, energy-efficient communication protocols, solar-powered systems, ruggedized sensing devices, localized edge intelligence, and hybrid networking and computing architectures.Furthermore, we presented an integrated agricultural IoT framework that connects data acquisition, communication, computing, data visualization, and system management to illustrate how technological components can be coordinated within agricultural ecosystem.Overall, this study consolidate integrated synthesis of recent IoT developments, critically examines the relationships between technological capabilities and implementation challenges, providing a comprehensive evidence base for researchers, technology developers, policymakers, and agricultural practitioners.Its findings offer strategic insights for advancing scalable, cost-effective, and sustainable IoT-enabled agricultural systems and strengthening their contribution to title: Editorial 60
abstract: The editorial of issue 60 of Estudios de Literatura Colombiana reflects on the contemporary role of literary studies and their relationship with cultural studies and textual analysis. It highlights the importance of interdisciplinary approaches that bring together semiotics, stylistics, literary historiography, translation studies, publishing studies, and the sociology of literature. It introduces the articles in the issue, which address questions concerning literary value and prestige, canon formation, the circulation of literary works, cultural representations, and Afro-Colombian identities. It also presents a non-peer-reviewed section featuring documents, reflections, interviews, and book reviews. Finally, the editorial reaffirms literature’s capacity to create meaning in times of crisis and defends the value of rigorous research, responsible knowledge production, and academic and university publishing in the face of the challenges posed by artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital capabilities on firm performance in the digital economy: A mediation model of business model innovation
abstract: PURPOSE: This study examines the relationships among AI capabilities, digital capabilities, and firm performance in the digital economy, with a particular focus on the mediating role of business model innovation. Despite substantial investments in AI and digital technologies, many firms struggle to translate these advancements into improved performance, often because they lack effective organizational mechanisms to convert technological potential into value. By addressing this issue, the study seeks to contribute to the literature by empirically examining business model innovation as a mediating mechanism linking technological capabilities and firm performance. METHODOLOGY: The study employs a quantitative approach using survey data collected from 286 firms in Vietnam. The data are analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the direct and indirect relationships between AI capabilities, digital capabilities, and firm performance, with business model innovation as a mediating variable. FINDINGS: Both AI and digital capabilities are positively associated with firm performance, directly and indirectly through business model innovation. In addition, both AI capabilities and digital capabilities are positively associated with business model innovation, with the estimated coefficient for AI capabilities being numerically larger than that for digital capabilities. Business model innovation is also positively associated with firm performance, suggesting its role as a mediating mechanism linking technological capabilities to firm performance. IMPLICATIONS: This study contributes to the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory by highlighting the role of business model innovation as a mechanism through which technological capabilities are associated with firm performance. The findings suggest that firms may benefit from aligning AI capabilities and digital capabilities with business model innovation to enhance performance outcomes. ORIGINALITY & VALUE: This study provides empirical evidence on the mediating role of business model innovation in the relationship between AI capabilities, digital capabilities, and firm performance. By integrating the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, it offers a more comprehensive understanding of how technological capabilities are associated with firm performance in the digital economy.

title: Combining codified and experiential knowledge: Co-presence, interaction, and the work of integration
abstract: PURPOSE: Research on codified and experiential knowledge has focused on whether firms that draw on both innovate more successfully, while what the combination consists of remains unspecified. This editorial asks what passes between the two kinds of knowledge, separates the three claims that combination carries, and reads the six contributions through the three aspects that follow. METHODOLOGY: The argument is conceptual. It re-reads that literature, where the two kinds of knowledge belong to the science-and-technology-based (STI) and doing-using-interacting (DUI) modes of innovation, and asks what each kind of evidence can establish. It then extends to arrangements in which one party is an artificial intelligence system. FINDINGS: Combination carries three claims about codified and experiential knowledge: co-presence, that both are present in the same organization; interaction, that the two are statistically dependent; and integration, that knowledge moves between them, so that formal findings change practice and practice reaches formal inquiry. Evidence for one does not establish the others, and most studies observe co-presence, test interaction, and draw conclusions about integration. The contradictory results reported for complementarity are what that pattern produces. When one party is a machine, use is recorded but judgment is not, so co-presence is most easily mistaken for integration. IMPLICATIONS: For theory, integration is organized work. Evidence should come from where that work takes place: what was examined, what entered a decision, and what changed as a result. For practice, the connection has to be designed and paid for: deciding what is fixed centrally and what is left to those doing the work; giving each stage what it needs, including an owner, a budget and a mandate when a result passes to those who will run it; and naming who carries the running cost. When a system supplies answers, someone must still be able to judge them. ORIGINALITY & VALUE: The editorial distinguishes three claims that the literature conflates and derives three aspects of the work, boundary, sequence, and maintenance, through which the six contributions are read.

title: Image Classification of Two-phase Flow Patterns Inside Effervescent Atomization Nozzles Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: The accurate classification of two-phase flow patterns within effervescent atomization nozzles is challenging due to the absence of unified standards and the existence of transitional regimes. To address the aforementioned challenge, this article proposes a novel image classification method leveraging a modified VGG-16 architecture. Five distinct flow pattern categories are then identified in high-speed images: bubbly, slug, churn, bubbly-slug mixed, and bubbly-churn mixed flows. The original flatten layer is replaced with a lightweight adaptive feature aggregator (LAFA) layer to reduce the number of trainable parameters and improve feature discrimination. This layer integrates attention mechanisms and multi-scale dilated convolutions. Ablation experiments are conducted, demonstrating that the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 97.47%, outperforming VGG-16, ResNet50, and DenseNet121 which accuracies are (94.07–94.17, 97.08, and 97.29%, respectively. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping and decision boundary analysis are also conducted. The obtained results show that the proposed model focuses on physically meaningful regions, with misclassifications mainly occurring in critical transition zones between flow patterns. This article presents an objective, automated, and high-accuracy solution for flow pattern recognition, providing technical support for future studies on effervescent atomization mechanisms.

title: Ground Truth-Oriented Fake News Detection Using Sentiment-Aware Hybrid Ensemble Learning and Bi-Directional LSTM Networks
abstract: Fake news is the spreading of misinformation or disinformation.The proliferation of fake news on social media makes it difficult for one to procure reliable information online.Our motive is for information to be freely and widely available to all, while maintaining the integrity of said information.Ground truth refers to the actual reality or a baseline truth.Existing research focuses on the importance of deciphering the ground truth value and into a feature-oriented approach [1].This paper contributes to the existing body of literature by meticulously selecting features and leveraging emotional cues through natural language processing (NLP), to address the issue of fake news detection.This is done by availing of the Truth Seeker [2] and Liar [3] datasets.The models used are an ensemble model which is a combination of Naive Bayes, passive aggressive classifier with a layer of deep neural network and Bi-directional LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) networks with sentiment analysis.Our findings suggest that sentiment analysis can serve as a valuable tool for enhancing the detection of fake news.

title: Design of Active Yaw Gaze-Locking Control for Quadcopters in Tower Orbital Inspection
abstract: Close-range 3D photogrammetric inspection of tall towers with quadcopters is degraded by wind, which pushes the vehicle off its scanning orbit and changes the camera-to-structure distance. Conventional flight controllers track a time-parameterized trajectory, so wind-induced lag must be corrected in both space and time. This paper presents a cascaded geometric vector field (VF) guidance law combined with active yaw gaze-locking for helical tower scanning. The VF decouples spatial convergence from timing, an outer velocity PI loop rejects wind through its integral action by tilting the vehicle into the wind, and the yaw channel is dedicated to keeping the camera pointed at the tower axis. In 6-DoF simulations with a 4.5 m/s mean wind, gusts, and Dryden turbulence, 30 paired Monte Carlo runs with PSO-tuned gains show that the VF reduces the mean cross-track error by 70.6% relative to PID trajectory tracking and by 48.3% relative to nonlinear guidance logic (NLGL), and reduces the stand-off distance variation by 65.8% (p < 0.001). Because the gaze-locking law uses the measured position, the camera pointing error remained about 0.8° for all guidance laws, showing that pointing accuracy is set by the yaw loop and is decoupled from path following.

title: Community social activities and cost stickiness: An ASEAN comparative analysis
abstract: This study investigates whether costs associated with community-based social activities exhibit asymmetric adjustment behavior. It then explores how socially embedded commitments shape cost rigidity in multinational settings. Prior research on cost stickiness has largely explained asymmetric cost behavior through economic adjustment costs and managerial discretion, whereas studies linking corporate social responsibility to cost rigidity remain predominantly descriptive and confined to single-country contexts. Limited attention has been paid to the underlying mechanisms through which community-focused social engagement may constrain firms’ ability to adjust costs downward. Understanding how socially embedded activities influence cost behavior is critical for firms engaged in sustained community relationships, where cost decisions may be constrained by relational obligations and reputational considerations rather than purely economic factors. Using 3,376 firm-year observations from publicly listed companies in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines from 2015 to 2023, this study applies the asymmetric cost behavior model to measure cost stickiness. Data on community social activities (COM) were sourced from CSRHub, while financial data were obtained from OSIRIS. Regression analysis and country-specific comparisons were conducted. Findings reveal that costs associated with COM do not uniformly exhibit high stickiness at the aggregate level. However, substantial cross-country variations are observed, suggesting that the degree of social embeddedness has a distinct influence on cost adjustment behavior across contexts. Results indicate that socially embedded costs may resist downward adjustment not because of regulatory constraints but due to implicit relational and reputational commitments. This study contributes to the management accounting literature by introducing a social capital theory-based explanation for asymmetric cost behavior. It highlights that cost rigidity can arise from non-economic constraints embedded in firms’ social relationships. Findings encourage a rethinking of cost flexibility assumptions in organizations with sustained community engagement.

title: Automatic Organ-at-Risk (OAR) Segmentation for Cervical Cancer Radiotherapy Using a U-Net Architecture with an Attention Gate Mechanism
abstract: Organ-at-risk (OAR) delineation in cervical cancer radiotherapy is essential to protect healthy tissues from excessive radiation exposure. However, manual delineation is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer and intra-observer variability, highlighting the need for efficient and consistent automated segmentation. This study compares standard 2D U-Net and 2D U-Net with an Attention Gate Mechanism for segmenting the bladder, rectum, bowel bag, and femoral heads using pelvic CT images from 100 cervical cancer patients at RSUD Dr. H. Abdul Moeloek, Lampung. The models were trained using a combination of Soft Dice Loss and Binary Cross Entropy and evaluated through patient-based 5-fold cross-validation. The Attention U-Net achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0,8772 for the femoral heads. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (α = 0.05) revealed significant differences only in selected metrics for the femoral heads. In contrast, bowel bag segmentation performance declined, with a DSC reduction of 0,0203 and an increase in Hausdorff Distance 95 (HD95) of 2,37 mm. These findings indicate that the Attention Gate does not consistently improve segmentation performance and remains suboptimal for organs with substantial anatomical deformation and heterogeneity.

title: Proteomic profiling of oocyte quality in bali cattle identifies candidate biomarkers
abstract: Oocyte quality critically determines cattle fertilization success and embryo development, yet selection still relies on subjective morphological grading of cumulus oocyte. This study aimed to identify protein-based quality indicators by comparing the proteomes of good quality (GQ: Grade A-B) and poor quality (PQ: Grade C-D) oocytes from Bali cattle (Bos javanicus). Oocytes were collected from 15 Bali cattle ovaries at a local abattoir and classified morphologically. High resolution LC -MS/MS proteomic profiling was performed, followed by differential abundance analysis and multivariate modelling. Multivariate analysis revealed clear separation and distinct clustering between groups, with key discriminatory proteins highlighted via Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) ranking. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses of top discriminatory proteins revealed significant enrichment of oxygen-related categories, including oxygen binding and haemoglobin-associated functions. An integrated biomarker selection pipeline retaining only proteins with VIP scores >1, statistically significant differences, and enriched Gene Ontology (GO) keyword mapping yielded three candidate biomarkers: ALB, HBE1, and HBB. ALB was predominantly associated with GQ oocytes, while HBE1 and HBB were linked to PQ oocytes. All three achieved perfect discriminatory performance in Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis (Area Under the Curve/AUC = 1.0). These study findings indicate that the oocyte quality of Bali cattle is associated with distinct proteomic signatures, with oxygen-related molecular processes emerging as key differentiating features. ALB, HBE1, and HBB represent promising biomarkers to complement morphological assessment and support more objective oocyte quality evaluation in reproductive biotechnology

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: consequências da sua aplicabilidade nos processos judiciais
abstract: O primeiro trabalho sobre a Inteligência Artificial- IA foi reconhecido em 1943, mas apenas em 1995 passou a ser reconhecida como uma ciência, desde então passou a ser aplicada em diversas áreas da sociedade, desde o comércio até as áreas de saúde e educação, estando sendo aplicada também nos dias atuais pelo poder judiciário no andamento dos processos judicias. Nesse sentido, torna-se necessário um estudo a repeito da forma que a Inteligência Artificial vem sendo aplicada e suas eventuais consequências para a sociedade, devendo ser verificada se sua aplicação infringe os direitos fundamentais, bem como demais questões éticas da sociedade. Este artigo busca fazer um estudo acerca das mudanças e consequências ocasionadas pela aplicação da inteligência artifical, além da influência humana sobre seu desenvolvimento e formação de seus vieses, bem como os riscos e benefícios que ela pode trazer à sociedade tendo em vista sua aplicação pelo poder judiciário nos processos judiciais para agilizar o andamento processual, reduzir custos e para a tomada de decisões.

title: A INTERSEÇÃO DAS NOVAS TECNOLOGIAS E A DEMOCRACIA: REFLEXÕES A PARTIR DO BRASIL
abstract: A interseção entre tecnologia e democracia ao longo dos séculos tem moldado a organização e decisões sociais. Desde a cifra de 1684 até os dias atuais, com mídias sociais, bots, blockchain e inteligência artificial, a relação entre inovação tecnológica e processos democráticos tornou-se complexa. Este artigo investiga o impacto das tecnologias contemporâneas, como mídias sociais e social bots, na integridade e funcionamento dos processos democráticos. As hipóteses divergem sobre o impacto dessas tecnologias. Para alguns, o impacto é significativo; para outros, o impacto e pequeno, o que mantém a prevalência de fatores tradicionais. A pesquisa adota abordagem exploratória e o método hipotético-dedutivo, com a utilização da técnica de pesquisa bibliográfica. Entre os objetivos específicos, destacam-se a busca da compreensão do valor da informação, a análise do papel das mídias sociais na formação da opinião pública e a compreensão do papel dos bots na disseminação de informações. A conclusão do trabalho é que a ascensão de bots e algoritmos representa um enorme desafio para a democracia, pois reconfigurar a dinâmica política e interfere profundamente na formação de opiniões. Neste novo cenário, a busca pela transparência e pelo estabelecimento de responsabilidades emergem como imperativos, exigindo uma abordagem multifacetada para garantir a integridade dos processos democráticos diante do avanço da tecnologia.

title: AS POSSIBILIDADES DO USO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO ONLINE DISPUTE RESOLUTION (ODR): PLATAFORMAS DIGITAIS COMO FERRAMENTAS DE AUTOCOMPOSIÇÃO
abstract: Este estudo tem como objetivo avaliar o emprego de recursos de Inteligência Artificial (IA) na Online Dispute Resolution (ODR), modalidade de Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) realizada por meio das Tecnologias Digitais de Informação e Comunicação (TDICs). Busca-se compreender de que forma a incorporação da IA tem potencializado os processos de resolução de litígios online, seja pela automação de etapas procedimentais, seja pela ampliação da eficiência e da celeridade na análise de conflitos, e examinar os desafios éticos, jurídicos e institucionais decorrentes dessa integração tecnológica, especialmente no que se refere à imparcialidade, à transparência e à proteção dos direitos fundamentais das partes envolvidas. Para tanto, apresentam-se as definições de ADR, ODR e IA, os fundamentos da inter-relação entre IA e ODR, os sistemas de IA de apoio e substitutivos de decisão e as controvérsias que cercam a sua adoção, à luz das diretrizes da CEPEJ e da OCDE e das resoluções do Conselho Nacional de Justiça sobre o uso da IA no Poder Judiciário. Conclui-se que a IA-ODR não deve ser vista apenas como ferramenta de auxílio à resolução de conflitos, mas como meio de resolução em si, razão pela qual o seu desenvolvimento exige abordagem estratégica e prospectiva, orientada pelos princípios da transparência, da verificabilidade e da controlabilidade dos algoritmos, de modo que não prejudique o acesso à justiça.

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL E SUA (IN)APLICABILIDADE FRENTE A AUTONOMIA PRIVADA DO SER HUMANO
abstract: A presente pesquisa se propõe a relatar acerca da importância e do uso extremo que a inteligência artificial tem no âmbito atual da sociedade, bem como relacionar mencionado feito com a autonomia privada e o direito que o ser humano possui frente ao algoritmo o qual demonstra e fornece seus dados pessoais. Mencionado tema deve ser de extrema importância posto o grande uso o qual a inteligência artificial vem tendo na sociedade a qual atualmente não se desenvolve sem o uso de algoritmos conforme será explanado. A autonomia privada trata-se de direito fundamental primordial ao ser humano, se voltando a boa-fé que este há de demonstrar nos negócios jurídicos os quais irá utilizar com sua expressão de vontade livre e desimpedida de vinculação. A metodologia adotada na presente pesquisa foi a pesquisa bibliográfica, bem como a demonstração de exemplos atuais e muito utilizados no cotidiano de cada usuário de inteligência artificial.

title: Title Pending 10324
abstract: The extraordinary success of recent Large Language Models (LLMs) on a diverse array of tasks has led to an explosion of scientific and philosophical theorizing aimed at explaining how they do what they do. Unfortunately, disagreement over fundamental theoretical issues has led to stalemate, with entrenched camps of LLM optimists and pessimists often committed to very different views of how these systems work. Overcoming stalemate requires agreement on fundamental questions, and the goal of this paper is to address one such question, namely: is LLM behavior driven partly by representation-based information processing of the sort implicated in biological cognition, or is it driven entirely by processes of memorization and stochastic table look-up? This is a question about what kind of algorithm LLMs implement, and the answer carries serious implications for higher level questions about whether these systems have beliefs, intentions, concepts, knowledge, and understanding. I argue that LLM behavior is partially driven by representation-based information processing, and then I describe and defend a series of practical techniques for investigating these representations and developing explanations on their basis. The resulting account provides a groundwork for future theorizing about language models and their successors.

title: Artificial Coherence Intelligence (ACI): Behavioral Demonstration of a New Intelligence Class
abstract: This publication presents a controlled behavioral demonstration of Artificial Coherence Intelligence (ACI), a proposed class of artificial reasoning systems characterized by invariant-bound coherence rather than optimization, prediction, or scale. ACI systems are defined by their ability to preserve identity, proportionality, and internal stability as reasoning unfolds under sustained pressure, contradiction, and uncertainty. The study examines AIngel v2.01 as a reference runtime to assess whether coherence-preserving behavior can be instantiated and observed within a constrained evaluation context. Through structured interaction sequences involving escalating contradiction, ambiguity, ethical tension, and recursive demand, the system exhibits stable correction patterns, sustained orientation, and bounded adaptation across repeated trials. These observations support the feasibility and internal consistency of the proposed ACI classification within a controlled setting. Rather than asserting implementation independence or general-purpose validity, this work focuses on clarifying behavioral criteria by which coherence-oriented reasoning may be identified and evaluated without disclosing construction methods or internal mechanisms. The contribution is classificatory and evidential in scope, demonstrating that coherence can function as an invariant-governed property of reasoning rather than an emergent byproduct of alignment or training scale. The findings are situated within the broader framework of Coherence Science, which treats coherence as a candidate constraint on persistence in adaptive systems operating over long horizons. While limited to a single reference instance, the work provides a grounded starting point for comparative evaluation, replication, and further formalization of coherence-preserving intelligence.

title: A Conceptual Framework for Automating Reservoir Characterization Workflows Using NLP and Data Integration
abstract: Reservoir characterization is a critical process in the energy industry, providing insights into subsurface properties essential for efficient exploration, production, and management. Traditional workflows are hindered by inefficiencies in handling diverse datasets, reliance on manual processes, and the challenges of integrating structured and unstructured information. This paper proposes a conceptual framework to automate reservoir characterization workflows by leveraging advanced technologies such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), data integration tools, and visualization systems. The framework encompasses four key components: data acquisition and preprocessing, text analysis through NLP models, a robust integration layer for harmonizing datasets, and intuitive visualization tools for enhanced decision-making. The framework aims to improve efficiency, accuracy, and collaboration in reservoir studies by automating and streamlining these processes. The paper also discusses the anticipated benefits, including faster decision-making and greater insight, alongside challenges such as computational demands, data quality issues, and the need for domain-specific model customization. Strategies to mitigate these challenges and recommendations for future research and practical implementation are proposed. This framework represents a transformative approach, offering a scalable solution to modernize reservoir characterization and drive innovation in the energy sector.

title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Application of Lean Construction Principles in Building Projects: Benefits, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
abstract: Question: How have Lean Construction principles been applied in building projects, and what challenges and benefits have been identified in their implementation? Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to systematically review the application of lean principles in building projects to determine widely used tools, associated benefits, barriers, and research gaps. It aims to explore the evolution of the lean idea from a foundational approach to a digital-integrated framework. Research Method: A systematic literature review conducted using the PRISMA framework. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using Specific Keywords. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria and removing duplicates, 83 studies published between 2007 and 2025 were included in the analysis. Findings: The review reveals that the Last Planner System® (LPS®) is the most widely implemented tool, offering quantifiable benefits in cost, time, and workflow. Value Stream Mapping (VSM) and 5S improve operational efficiency but remain limited in application. Tools such as Just-in-Time (JIT), Target Value Design (TVD), and Set-Based Design (SBD) are underexplored. Significant barriers include interoperability issues, less leadership initiative, and inadequate training. The integration of the Lean-BIM-Digital framework is evolving but lacks empirical validation. Limitations: Most reviewed studies are case-based and qualitative, making them difficult to generalize. Research is mainly focused on the construction phase, with minimal attention to design and procurement stages. Implications: The findings show the need for standardized performance indicators, stronger empirical methods, and broader application of lean-digital integration. Industry practitioners and policy makers can use these insights to improve lean implementation. Value for Authors: This review tries to connect fragmented knowledge, provides a comprehensive approach to lean practices in building projects, and guides future research toward quantifiable, technology-oriented solutions. title: Risk Mitigation Design in the Supply Chain Process of Arabica Cofee Fort Alla
abstract: The Arabica coffee supply chain in Fort Allé is subject to a number of risks that have the potential to disrupt supply continuity and product quality. The objective of this study is to identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies that can be integrated into the value chain. The research scope encompasses the identification, prioritization, and design of field-based countermeasures. The Delphi method was employed to identify risk events and agents, and the House of Risk (HOR) approach was utilized for analysis, evaluation, and prioritization of strategies. The data collection process entailed a multifaceted approach, encompassing observational studies, in-depth interviews, the administration of questionnaires, brainstorming sessions, and focus group discussions with cooperative stakeholders. The study identified 14 risk events and 33 risk sources, leading to the formulation of 14 preventive measures. The integration of coffee crops with secondary crops was prioritized (ETDk: 5184), as it enhances both sustainability and profitability. The proposed strategies are embedded within the coffee value chain, offering practical guidance for cooperatives and agroindustry actors to strengthen supply chain resilience and increase added value. The results of this study can serve as a reference for decision-making by cooperatives, agroindustry players, and policymakers in designing coffee supply chain strengthening programs that focus on risk mitigation and increasing added value based on sustainability.

title: Industrial Production in the Transition from Communism to Capitalism: A Croatian Case Study
abstract: This article presents a social scientific case study that chronicles the remarkable business journey of a successful Croatian industrialist, who was recently named European Entrepreneur of the Year. Selected from among 150,000 entrepreneurs in 33 countries in one of the most prestigious, independently judged business competitions, he began his 55-year career in a 35-square-meter garage workshop in communist Croatia. Through semi-structured interviews with the winner, fellow industrialists, colleagues, and family members, the article sheds light on a rarely told story that traces the ideological and political challenges faced in industrial production in the transition of countries from communism to capitalism. The detailed analysis contributes to our understanding of the continuing obstacles to democratic nation-building and economic development faced by former communist countries in overcoming their historically anti-capitalist legacy.

title: Measuring Social Proficiency: Development of a Questionnaire
abstract: In the era of artificial intelligence, uniquely human abilities such as empathy, nuanced communication, and adaptability remain irreplaceable. At the same time, rising loneliness (Luhmann et al., 2023) and declining social skills (DiTommaso et al., 2003; Turkle, 2015) highlight the need to better understand and foster social proficiency, particularly as technology reshapes interpersonal interaction. Existing measures provide valuable foundations but fail to capture the multifaceted, contemporary dynamics of social communication. The Social Proficiency Questionnaire (SPQ) aims to establish a concise, validated measure encompassing six key dimensions to assess and promote social proficiency in modern contexts: receptivity, assertiveness, appreciativeness, authenticity, adaptability, and resilience.

title: Implementation of a Deep Learning Approach with the Project Based Learning Model in the Element of Fashion Style and Design Development
abstract: This study aims to examine the effects, improvements, and differences in the skills and work attitudes of students through the integration of a Deep Learning approach with the Project Based Learning PjBL model in the Style and Design Development element of the Fashion Design and Production subject at vocational high schools. The study employed a quasi-experimental method with a pretest posttest non-equivalent control group design. The participants consisted of 41 eleventh grade students from the Fashion Design Program at SMK Widya Praja Ungaran, including 21 students in the control class that implemented conventional PjBL and 20 students in the experimental class that implemented PjBL integrated with the Deep Learning approach. The research instruments consisted of a skills assessment rubric and a work attitude scale that had been validated by six experts using the Percentage of Agreement test. Data were analyzed using the N Gain test and the Independent Sample t Test. The findings indicate that the N Gain value of skills in the experimental class reached 65.4%, which falls within the moderate category and is higher than the control class with 53% in the less effective category. The N Gain value of work attitude in the experimental class reached 92% in the effective category, while the control class obtained 72% in the fairly effective category. The results of the t test show significant differences in skills t = 13.175, p = 0.000 < 0.05 and work attitudes t = 3.212, p = 0.003 < 0.05. These findings indicate that the integration of a Deep Learning approach within the PjBL model significantly improves student skills and work attitudes in vocational fashion design learning.

title: Rethinking Public Policy and Governance in a Globalized Era: Advancing the Interdisciplinary Research
abstract: This editorial introduces the Journal of Policy Affairs (JPA) as a comprehensive, open-access platform dedicated to advancing rigorous scholarship in public policy, governance, and institutional studies. It situates the journal within the contemporary global context characterized by economic volatility, digital transformation, environmental challenges, social inequality, and increasing interdependence among nations. The editorial outlines the journal’s core aim to bridge theory and practice by publishing high-quality, interdisciplinary research that contributes to both academic discourse and policy implementation. Emphasizing methodological pluralism and global inclusivity, JPA welcomes diverse analytical approaches that address the design, execution, evaluation, and reform of public policies across varied institutional settings. The editorial further elaborates on the journal’s thematic priorities, including public administration, political economy, public finance, environmental governance, social policy, digital governance, crisis management, and international policy coordination. By highlighting the interconnected nature of modern governance challenges, it underscores the need for comparative and cross-disciplinary research capable of informing evidence-based policymaking. Ultimately, this editorial articulates JPA’s vision of fostering intellectually robust and practically relevant scholarship that strengthens institutional resilience, promotes inclusive development, and contributes to more effective and accountable governance systems worldwide.

abstract: As the integration of Big Data technologies continues to transform industries, the management of personal data privacy has become an increasingly critical concern. This paper explores user-centric approaches to Big Data privacy, emphasizing personal data control mechanisms that empower individuals to protect their data in a digitalized world. Through a detailed analysis, the study provides actionable recommendations for improving Big Data privacy governance

title: SECURING BIG DATA IN THE INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT): PRIVACY AND SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming industries by connecting billions of devices and enabling the generation and collection of vast amounts of data, commonly referred to as Big Data. While this data presents numerous opportunities for innovation, it also raises significant privacy and security concerns. This paper explores the security and privacy challenges in securing Big Data within the IoT ecosystem, and proposes frameworks and techniques for addressing these issues. By examining existing vulnerabilities, security protocols, and emerging technologies, the study provides recommendations for ensuring data protection in the IoT environment. Key challenges such as data encryption, access control, and secure data transmission are discussed, alongside solutions like blockchain and federated learning for enhancing privacy in IoT systems.

Empirical evidence and case studies are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of these practices in real-world settings. The study concludes by proposing a roadmap for designing trustworthy Big Data environments that align technological innovation with ethical responsibility.

title: NUISS: A User-Centered Prototype for International Student Administrative Support
abstract: This study applies a streamlined User-Centered Design (UCD) approach, enhanced with AI elements, to address common administrative challenges faced by international students, such as information fragmentation and unclear processes. Using National University (NU) as a case study, the research followed core UCD stages to develop the prototype of the NU International Student Services (NUISS). These stages included task analysis informed by user stories, persona development, prototype design, and a heuristic evaluation. The high-fidelity prototype integrates three key modules-Visa Services, Certification, and Paymentwith an AI-powered assistant for proactive, personalized support. The structure is designed to enhance accessibility and minimize cognitive load. An evaluation that centered on "consistency and standards" uncovered major interface problems; this led to design refinements that boosted visual clarity and balance in a significant way. The final prototype shows that applying UCD principles in a focused way, combined with AI enhancements, can create efficient and user-friendly administrative experiences, and it offers a replicable model for similar educational contexts.

title: The Kirk-Spock Leadership Framework for Balanced Human-AI Collaboration in Construction Project Management
abstract: Question: What leadership approach can sustain human adaptability and resilience in construction project management in the age of Artificial Intelligence (AI)? Purpose: The purpose is to develop and demonstrate a framework that helps construction project managers effectively use AI while actively preserving their critical thinking, intuition, and emotional intelligence. Research Method: This study adopts a Design Science Research (DSR) approach to develop the Kirk–Spock Leadership Framework (KSLF) for balanced human–AI collaboration in construction management. Findings: The paper proposes that while AI offers efficiency, only a balanced human–AI leadership model can prevent skill loss and build more resilient leaders. Limitations: The paper’s limitations stem from its conceptual nature, limited case evidence, reliance on cross-industry analogies, and lack of longitudinal validation for the proposed framework. Implications: The paper suggests that sustaining human cognitive engagement alongside AI is crucial for both theory and practice, resulting in stronger leaders, healthier teams, and more adaptable organizations. Value for authors: The authors’ value lies in creating a new leadership framework (KSLF) and providing both theoretical and practical guidance for sustaining human leadership capacity in AI-augmented construction management. title: Antecedents to trust and a Moderating role of website quality and online shopping Experience
abstract: In the present era, due to the diffusion of technology, internet usage has increased substantially. As a result, consumers' online purchase intention increased substantially. This study examined the impact of four antecedents on trust and the impact of trust on online purchase intention. The study also examined the impact of trust on online purchase intention. And the moderating role of website experience on trust and online purchase intention. The study collected 336 samples using convenience sampling. We found that all six articulated hypotheses were accepted. These findings align with past studies. The study found that brand engagement positively affects trust. Perceived security promotes trust. Fashion innovation positively affects. Social motivation is positively associated with trust. Trust and online purchase intention are positively associated. Website experience moderates the relationship between trust and purchase intention. Given the importance of the website, we recommend that online vendors improve the quality of their websites. In this context, the vendors ensure that their webpages are user-friendly. Moreover, they communicate to consumers that their personal and financial data are secure. And they don't share their data with others. This study underscores that trust is both a mediator and a prerequisite in the online purchase decision-making process. Perceived service quality plays a central role in fostering trust, while perceived risk serves as a significant moderator that may amplify or diminish the effect of trust on purchase intention. Findings also show that consumers increasingly rely on website design, user experience, online reviews, and brand familiarity to assess credibility. Moreover, the study highlights the broader impact of digitalization, where consumers are becoming more informed but also more cautious. Future strategies should emphasize not only technological efficiency but also emotional and relational engagement to compensate for the lack of physical presence in e-commerce interactions.

It further explores critical themes such as board effectiveness, regulatory systems, innovation governance, public–private interfaces, and anti-corruption mechanisms, while advocating for inclusive and globally representative scholarship. title: Human vs machine judgment in safety-critical logistics: a philosophical inquiry into trust and control
abstract: This article examines the differences between human judgment and algorithmic decision-making in critical logistics systems, focusing on the implications for the concepts of trust and control. The aim of the study is to determine whether AI-based systems can perform functions equivalent to human judgment and what implications this has for operational safety and accountability in complex logistics systems. The study is based on an interdisciplinary analysis, including a review of the literature on artificial intelligence, system safety, and human factors research, as well as a philosophical analysis. This is supplemented by a case study of selected incidents related to the operation of automated systems in high-risk environments, which allows the identification of practical limitations in integrating humans and algorithmic systems. The results indicate that decisions generated by algorithmic systems are statistical and optimization-based, which distinguishes them from human judgment, which takes into account context, uncertainty, and emotions. Consequently, trust in AI systems takes the form of an indirect, user-dependent relationship rather than an autonomous property of the technology. At the same time, increasing levels of automation lead to a diffusion of responsibility and a reduction in direct control over decision-making processes. The findings indicate that full automation of decisions in critical safety systems. Consequently, trust in AI systems takes the form of an indirect, user-dependent relationship rather than an autonomous property of the technology.

title: The Sociolinguistics of Machine Identity: LLM Personality and Ideology Propagation
abstract: Do large language models (LLMs) possess a measurable "personality," and how do the linguistic properties of training corpora shape their cognitive style and downstream reasoning? This paper approaches these questions from a sociolinguistic perspective on machine "identity." This manuscript is positioned explicitly as a conceptual perspective paper: it does not present original experimental data, nor does it constitute a systematic review with defined search strategies or inclusion criteria. Instead, it synthesises key published findings into two original theoretical frameworks intended to guide future empirical and engineering work. We examine evidence that LLMs exhibit reliable, valid Big Five personality traits—particularly in large, instruction-tuned models—and that continued pre-training on domain-specific corpora may shape those traits through measurable linguistic features: imperative ratio, type-token ratio (TTR), and syntactic complexity. We then analyse how standard-language ideology embedded in training corpora is amplified in model outputs, disadvantaging dialect and minority-language communities. Building on these findings, we propose two conceptual contributions: (1) a Personality Engineering (PE) framework for targeted continued pre-training to cultivate task-appropriate cognitive profiles, and (2) a Language Ideology Propagation Model (LIPM) mapping the pipeline from corpus composition to societal impact. Both frameworks are explicitly conceptual and require empirical validation before they can function as operational guidelines. Their value lies in structuring future research and providing a shared vocabulary for cross-disciplinary collaboration, with direct implications for responsible AI deployment.

title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Korean Language Learning: Applications, Challenges, and Instructional Strategies
abstract: This conceptual narrative review examines the role of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in Korean language learning. The paper synthesizes recent scholarship on AI-assisted language learning, Korean language education, technology acceptance, and educational ethics to develop an analytical framework for responsible classroom use. The review focuses on four dimensions: Korean language skills, Korean-specific linguistic and cultural features, instructional design, and governance risks. The analysis suggests that generative AI can support listening, speaking, reading, and writing when tasks are explicitly designed around Korean phonology, morphology, pragmatics, and learner purposes such as TOPIK preparation, study abroad, employment, and popular-culture engagement. It also identifies challenges in cultural-pragmatic accuracy, hallucinated expressions, assessment validity, data privacy, unequal access, teacher readiness, and learner dependency. The paper concludes that generative AI should function as a mediated learning resource rather than a substitute for teachers, learner judgment, or culturally grounded interaction.

title: AI-Assisted Identity and Access Threat Detection Using the AITIR Framework for Public-Sector Cybersecurity Environments
abstract: In public-sector cybersecurity, the password has become the prize. Agencies have moved their services into the cloud and now hand out access to employees, contractors, and members of the public alike, and that change has dragged the fight off the network perimeter and onto the credential itself. We describe AITIR, short for Adaptive Identity-and-access Threat Intelligence and Response, a layered machine-learning framework that watches for identity-based attacks as they happen and coordinates a response inside the governance rules agencies already have to follow. Three models share the detection work: a gradient-boosted classifier reads each access attempt, a bidirectional sequence model reads the order of an account's actions, and a graph-based behavior-analytics module flags the moment a session drifts away from an identity's usual company. Sitting on top of them, an explainable triage layer passes only the high-confidence, well-justified alerts to a person. To test the design, we assembled a corpus of about 14.8 million authentication and access events, part public benchmark data and part synthetic identity telemetry, and pushed credential stuffing, password spraying, privilege escalation, session hijacking, and insider misuse through it. AITIR scored an F1 of 0.967 and an area under the ROC curve of 0.985, ahead of all five baselines. Over a four-quarter deployment simulation it cut successful identity-based intrusions by 31.4 percent, brought mean time to detect down by 62 percent, and trimmed false positives by 41 percent against a conventional operations baseline. A cost-benefit model, scaled to a national public-sector portfolio, points to roughly US$10.2 billion in avoided cost a year and about 79,000 analyst hours given back. Those last two numbers are projections built on stated assumptions, not audited savings, and we say so plainly. The paper closes on the governance, staffing, and validity questions that decide whether any of them survives contact with a real agency.

title: Islamic Education in the Digital Age: Challenges and Adaptation Strategies
abstract: Islamic education in the digital age has undergone major changes with the introduction of technology into the teaching and learning process, but it has also given rise to problems such as unequal access to devices and the internet, low digital literacy among some educators, and the use of unverified online teaching materials. This study aims to explore these challenges and formulate adaptation strategies to maintain the relevance and quality of education using a descriptive-analytical library research method using a descriptive-analytical approach conducted systematically through literature searches in scientific databases (e.g., Google Scholar, DOAJ, ERIC, Garuda/SINTA) using keywords related to the digitization of Islamic education, followed by the selection of sources based on relevance, recency (mainly within the last 10 years), academic credibility (peer-reviewed journal articles, scientific books/book chapters, proceedings, theses/dissertations), as well as supporting policy documents and official institutional reports. This was followed by an evaluation of source quality (publisher reputation, clarity of methods, consistency of findings, traceability of references) and thematic content analysis to map issues of access, educator competence, value-based curriculum, and the collaboration ecosystem. the results of the study show that digitization opens up opportunities to improve accessibility and variety of teaching media, but requires the strengthening of an adaptive curriculum based on Islamic values, improving teachers' digital literacy competencies (platform selection, learning design, source verification, digital ethics), and collaboration between schools, parents, and the community so that digital learning does not run “alone”; Therefore, it is recommended that there be continuous training for educators, integration of religious values in technology-based learning, and equitable access to technology in all regions.

title: Algorithmic Justice and Responsible AI Journalism: A Comparative Communication Policy Perspective in East Asia
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence and automated content curation rapidly reshape the global media landscape, the intersection of algorithmic justice and media governance has become a critical frontier for sustainable development. This study provides a comparative communication policy analysis of China and South Korea, focusing explicitly on how their distinct regulatory toolkits address the tension between algorithmic fairness and platform accountability in AI journalism. While China utilizes a top-down, state-centric regulatory framework emphasizing ideological security, algorithmic registration, and strict synthetic media labeling, South Korea employs a multi-stakeholder co-regulation model driven by personal data protection, anti-monopoly platform intervention, and civil society oversight. Through a detailed textual analysis of key policy documents—including China's Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendations and South Korea's Guidelines for AI Service Ethics to Protect Users—alongside empirical evidence from prominent algorithmic news curation platforms (Toutiao and Naver), this paper evaluates the implementation efficacy and structural trade-offs of each nation's approach. We demonstrate that while both models mitigate the risks of digital infodemics and algorithmic bias, they face contrasting trade-offs between regulatory efficiency and editorial independence. Finally, this study introduces the "Policy-Media-Society" (PMS) responsive governance framework, clarifying how systemic institutional adaptations can advance UN Sustainable Development Goal 16 (SDG 16) by ensuring public access to transparent, verified information.

title: Role of Stakeholder Engagement in Policy Implementation Success: Mediating Role of Communication Quality, Coordination Effectiveness, and Institutional Trust
abstract: This study investigates the impact of stakeholder engagement on policy implementation success in Bangladesh’s health sector, focusing on the mediating roles of communication quality, coordination effectiveness, and institutional trust. Grounded in governance and stakeholder theory, the study develops and tests a comprehensive structural model to explain how participatory mechanisms translate into effective policy outcomes. Data were collected from 460 respondents representing government health officials, healthcare providers, NGO partners, and local administrators. The analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine direct, indirect, and sequential relationships among constructs. The findings reveal that stakeholder engagement has a significant positive effect on policy implementation success. Moreover, communication quality, coordination effectiveness, and institutional trust significantly mediate this relationship, forming both parallel and sequential pathways. The results further indicate that coordination effectiveness exerts the strongest direct influence on policy implementation success, while institutional trust plays a critical psychological and relational mediating role. The model demonstrates strong explanatory and predictive power, confirming the robustness of the proposed governance framework. The study contributes to the literature by advancing a multi-layered mediation model that explains how stakeholder engagement operates through interconnected governance mechanisms. It also provides empirical evidence from a developing country context, where institutional complexity and coordination challenges are particularly pronounced. The findings offer important implications for strengthening participatory governance structures in health policy systems.

title: Effect of Evidence-Based Policymaking on Public Service Delivery Efficiency: Evidence from the Indian Technology Industry Policy
abstract: This study examines the relationships among Evidence-Based Policymaking (EBPM), Data Analytics Capability (DAC), Policy Implementation Quality (PIQ), and Public Service Delivery Efficiency (PSDE) in the context of the Indian technology industry. Drawing on a quantitative, cross-sectional survey of 380 policy stakeholders, including government officials, industry professionals, and consultants, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed conceptual model. Results indicate that both EBPM and DAC have significant positive effects on PSDE, with PIQ partially mediating these relationships. The findings highlight the critical role of effective policy implementation in translating evidence-based and data-driven practices into enhanced service delivery outcomes. The study contributes theoretically by integrating EBPM, DAC, and implementation quality into a unified model and empirically validating their interrelationships. Practically, it underscores the importance of investing in evidence-based practices, analytical capabilities, and high-quality implementation mechanisms to improve governance performance, transparency, and citizen satisfaction. Limitations include the cross-sectional design and sector-specific focus, suggesting future research could explore longitudinal approaches and multi-sector comparisons.

title: Research on Attention Guidance and User Autonomy in AI-Powered Immersive Environments
abstract: As artificial intelligence gets deeply embedded into immersive environments, attention-guiding technology delivers ever more precise and efficient outcomes. Still, this improved efficiency carries an overlooked design risk: excessive AI guidance may steadily erode user agency and undermine exploratory behaviors as well as the process of meaning-making. This paper builds a critical conceptual framework to rethink attention-oriented design within AI-driven immersive settings. It defines excessive guidance and establishes theoretical links between this concept and three core facets of user agency: perceived control, voluntary choice and decision-making authority. Based on these findings, the paper calls for a paradigm shift from attention optimization to curiosity-led design. It also puts forward actionable behavioral measurement indicators covering exploration scope, average dwell time, path-following ratio, active choice frequency and recall test performance. The proposed framework supplies a new theoretical tool for human-computer interaction research in immersive scenarios and helps shift AI's role from a fixed route provider to an exploratory collaborator.

title: Integrarea inteligenţei artificiale în oraşele viitorului / The role of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in the city of tomorrow
abstract: Artificial intelligence offers various benefits to the field of architecture. These benefits include increased efficiency, improved design quality, improved durability and reduced cost. It can streamline various architectural processes such as design and construction, leading to faster project execution time and reduced labor costs. In addition, it can automate repetitive tasks such as drafting and documentation, freeing up time for architects to focus on more creative and complex tasks. Artificial intelligence can analyze and optimize design solutions, resulting in improved design quality. By considering multiple design constraints and criteria, it can suggest design options that meet the project's goals while taking into account environmental, social, and economic factors. In addition, it can help identify design flaws and improve safety and functionality. Artificial intelligence can contribute to sustainability in various ways, such as optimizing the energy performance of the building, reducing material waste and improving the quality of the indoor environment. By analyzing building data, it can optimize building systems and operations, reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions. Likewise, it can help architects make informed decisions about material selection and waste reduction strategies.

title: COMBATING THE ROCKFALL HAZARD: A REVIEW OF APPROACHES AND TECHNOLOGIES USED FOR RISK ASSESSMENTS AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: Rockfalls pose a significant hazard in mountainous and hilly regions worldwide, threatening infrastructure, public safety, and ecosystems. Triggered by factors such as seismic activity, intense rainfall, erosion, and geomorphological instability, these events often result in severe consequences. Addressing rockfall risks effectively is essential for sustainable infrastructure planning and environmental protection. This review examines traditional and innovative approaches for assessing and managing rockfall hazards, drawing on advancements in geology, civil engineering, remote sensing, and artificial intelligence. Techniques such as terrestrial laser scanning (TLS), 3D modeling, geographic information systems (GIS), LiDAR, and machine learning algorithms have significantly enhanced the ability to detect, monitor, and evaluate these events. The review highlights the progress in understanding rockfall dynamics and developing effective strategies for risk prevention and mitigation. By integrating diverse methodologies, it underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in addressing the complex challenges posed by rockfall hazards.

title: From Legal Databases to AI-Assisted Justice: A Risk-Sensitive Framework for the Application of Information Technologies in Law
abstract: This paper analyzes information technologies in law and proposes a risk-sensitive framework for responsible digital legal practice. Using EU regulatory developments as the main legal lens, while also referring to international standards and policy materials, the study reviews legal databases, case-management systems, artificial intelligence and natural language processing, electronic identification and signatures, digital evidence, online dispute resolution and electronic courts. The paper's contribution is to connect general principles of transparency, human oversight, source verification and accountability to concrete stages of legal work: intake, research, drafting, identity assurance, signing, archiving and audit. Brief examples of AI-assisted drafting, online dispute resolution and electronic signature verification illustrate the practical use of the framework. The analysis concludes that digital legal systems create value when they remain traceable, proportionate and subject to professional responsibility rather than replacing legal judgment.

title: Regulating the Frontier: Model-Level Evidence from the EU AI Act
abstract: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act creates a binding, economy-wide transparency regime directed specifically at providers of general-purpose AI models. Whether such rules alter model-development practice, rather than merely producing legal documentation outside public view, is an empirical question. This article offers an early model-level assessment using a daily updated public database of 3,571 machine-learning models. The main analysis compares 604 language-based models that satisfy a transparent general-purpose-AI proxy with 401 narrow-task models released during an approximately two-year window from 2 August 2024 to 21 July 2026, when the Act's general-purpose-model obligations began to apply to newly marketed models. A seven-component Structured Disclosure Index records whether public sources report parameter count, training compute, training-data scale, training time, training hardware, training-code status, and model-access status. Organization and calendar-month fixed-effects estimates associate the post-application period with an 8.7 percentage-point increase in structured disclosure for the general-purpose group. The change is concentrated in training-compute reporting. The estimate remains positive in several within-provider specifications, although it becomes small and statistically indistinguishable from zero when organization fixed effects are replaced by country and organization-category controls. No corresponding change is detected in open-weight release, model parameter scale, or disclosed training compute. Only two post-application observations with disclosed compute exceed the Act's $10^{25}$ floating-point-operation presumption, making a threshold design premature. These findings are best read as pre-enforcement evidence of selective documentation adaptation, not a definitive causal estimate. The article contributes a reproducible measurement framework, identifies the distinction between structured and substantive transparency, and provides code for extending the analysis to versioned Hugging Face model cards, safety reports, and copyright disclosures.

title: A Study on the Mechanism and Ways to Improve New-Quality Productivity of Enterprises Driven by AI and the Digital Economy
abstract: With the deep development of the digital economy and the accelerated iteration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, the formation and development of enterprise new quality productive forces have attracted increasing attention from academia and practice. Based on enterprises as the micro-subject, this paper constructs a theoretical analysis framework for the "dual-wheel drive of AI and the digital economy" and explores the formation mechanism and the path to enhancing the synergistic empowerment of enterprise these forces. The research finds that AI and the digital economy are not simply parallel drivers, but form a synergistic empowerment effect through a triple interactive mechanism of "technology-factor-organization." AI technology reshapes the technological boundary of the production function, while the digital economy reconstructs the allocation logic of production factors. The deep integration of the two drives a fundamental transformation of enterprise production modes from "factor-input-driven" to "innovation-driven". On this basis, this paper reveals the formation mechanism of these advanced productive capabilities across three dimensions: technological innovation, data element allocation, and organizational change, and proposes corresponding enhancement paths. This study has significant theoretical and practical value for understanding the micro-formation mechanism of enterprise new-quality productive forces and for guiding enterprise digital transformation and intelligent upgrading.

title: From Prediction to Action: Translational Readiness of Artificial Intelligence in Perioperative Pain Care
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied in perioperative pain care to estimate nociception, predict acute postoperative pain, and forecast opioid-related outcomes. However, improvements in technical performance have outpaced evidence demonstrating meaningful patient benefit. This review examines the gap between predictive performance and clinical translation and outlines the evidence required to bridge that gap. Methods: We conducted a focused translational narrative review. Recent reviews were first used to map the field and identify key studies, followed by targeted PubMed searches through 31 July 2026, supplemented by reference screening and forward citation tracking. Additional searches identified methodological guidance and implementation precedents. Evidence was synthesized according to clinical task and stage of translation and evaluated across five domains: technical validity, decision relevance, pathway actionability, implementation fidelity, and clinical impact. Results: Model performance varied substantially across clinical tasks and evaluation settings. The strongest reported discrimination was observed for contemporaneous pain-state assessment in awake postoperative patients, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) around 0.93, whereas intraoperative models showed more modest and label-dependent performance. Models predicting future postoperative pain reported heterogeneous discrimination, with the highest estimates arising from restricted cohorts evaluated using internal or temporal data splits; prospective evaluation of a multicenter-developed model demonstrated more modest discrimination together with deterioration in calibration, highlighting the challenges of model transportability. External validation of opioid-related prediction remained rare. Translation from prediction to clinical implementation remained limited. No reviewed study linked a validated postoperative pain prediction to a prespecified analgesic pathway. Clinician-mediated nociception-index protocols did not reduce their primary opioid-consumption outcomes, while automated titration altered opioid exposure without improving postoperative pain or analgesic requirements. Evidence supporting AI-assisted regional anesthesia and procedural safety remains preliminary. Conclusion: Artificial intelligence has demonstrated potential for perioperative pain and nociception assessment and for prediction of postoperative outcomes, but the evidence remains insufficient to conclude that acting on these predictions improves patient-centered outcomes. The principal gaps are not limited to discrimination; they include calibration, external and prospective validation, availability at clinically relevant decision points, reproducible workflow integration, adherence to linked interventions, and evidence of benefit and safety. The next translational step is a prospective impact study in which a calibrated and transportable prediction is delivered before a modifiable clinical decision, linked to a prespecified care pathway, and compared with usual care. Such a study should evaluate both implementation fidelity and patient-centered outcomes. Until such evidence is available, AI-based perioperative pain prediction should be regarded as a promising decision-support capability rather than an established intervention.
