title: Entrepreneurship, Innovation Ecosystems, and Post-Pandemic Economic Recovery Strategies
abstract: The post-pandemic period has fundamentally reshaped the global economic landscape, compelling governments, businesses, and local communities to develop more adaptive and innovation-oriented recovery strategies. Within this context, entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystems have emerged as critical drivers of economic resilience, business sustainability, and inclusive development. This study aims to analyze the interrelationship between entrepreneurial activities, innovation ecosystems, and post-pandemic economic recovery strategies, while identifying the institutional, technological, and collaborative factors that strengthen sustainable economic revitalization. The research employs a qualitative field research design, collecting primary data through semi-structured interviews, direct observations, and focus group discussions involving entrepreneurs, business incubator managers, government officials, financial institutions, and innovation ecosystem stakeholders. The data are analyzed using thematic analysis through data reduction, categorization, interpretation, and triangulation to ensure the credibility and trustworthiness of the findings. The results demonstrate that successful post-pandemic economic recovery depends not only on entrepreneurial capabilities but also on the maturity of innovation ecosystems characterized by effective collaboration among government, universities, industry, financial institutions, and digital technology providers. The findings further reveal that digital transformation, access to entrepreneurial financing, policy support, innovation-oriented business networks, and institutional capacity building significantly enhance business adaptability, accelerate innovation diffusion, and improve the resilience of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises. Nevertheless, disparities in digital infrastructure, limited innovation capabilities, and uneven stakeholder coordination remain major obstacles to achieving sustainable recovery. This study contributes to the entrepreneurship and innovation literature by proposing an integrated recovery framework that combines entrepreneurial resilience, collaborative innovation ecosystems, and adaptive governance as complementary pillars for sustainable post-pandemic economic development. The findings also provide practical policy implications for strengthening innovation-driven entrepreneurship and designing more resilient, inclusive, and long-term economic recovery strategies.

title: SHAP-based Feature Stability Analysis for High-dimensional IoT Intrusion Detection Using Deep Neural Network
abstract: In today's world, the Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a vital network infrastructure in the process of digitalization.However, existing works struggle with high-dimensional and redundant features that increase computation and reduce efficiency.Furthermore, they fail to distinguish critical features for specific attack types, making their security decisions difficult to interpret.This manuscript presents a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based Feature Stability Analysis Network (SFSA-Net) for an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) in IoT.The proposed SFSA-Net uses SHAP to extract consistent stable features from a baseline Deep Neural Network (DNN), which then optimizes the final network for all attack types.To evaluate feature consistency, a stability-weighted feature ranking index, the Refined Explainable Index (REI), is established by conducting a three-stage stability analysis.The proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 98.75%±0.23%on UNSW-NB15 and 98.85%±0.28%on CICIoT-2023 datasets, respectively.Moreover, the proposed SFSA-Net achieves an optimal feature reduction of 78.7% on UNSW-NB15 and 97.4% on CICIoT-2023, minimizes memory consumption by 83.63% on UNSW-NB15 and 89.03% on CICIoT-2023, while simultaneously improving the detection of minority classes, specifically increasing the recall for worm attacks by 39.25 percentage points.

title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

title: An Inventory Model for Non-Instantaneously Reasoned, Continuously Deteriorating Items under a Linear Demand Rate
abstract: This paper develops a deterministic economic order quantity (EOQ) model for a single deteriorating item under a linear, time-dependent demand rate D(t) = a+bt, where deterioration proceeds at a constant instantaneous rate θ applied to the on-hand inventory. Shortages are not permitted. The governing first-order linear differential equation describing inventory depletion is solved in closed form, and the order quantity, holding cost integral, and deterioration cost expression are derived analytically and verified symbolically. The average total cost per unit time, TCU(T), is shown via a rigorous second-order condition together with numerical evidence to be strictly convex in the cycle length T, guaranteeing a unique global minimizer T∗. The model is further validated by showing that it reduces exactly to the classical no-deterioration linear-trend model as θ →0, to the constant-demand Ghare–Schrader deteriorating inventory model as b→0, and to the textbook economic order quantity formula as both θ →0 and b→0 simultaneously. A solution algorithm is proposed, and a numerical example, together with an extended six-scenario numerical study spanning low, base, and high deterioration rates and growing, flat, and declining demand trends, and a comprehensive sensitivity analysis with respect to the deterioration rate, demand trend, holding cost, deterioration cost, and ordering cost, illustrates the practical behaviour of the optimal policy across realistic operating regimes. Managerial insights and limitations relevant to perishable goods and fast-moving consumer goods supply chains are discussed in detail.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on human safety and data protection in smart logistics: opportunities, risks and governance challenges
abstract: Aim: This article examines the dual role of artificial intelligence (AI) in smart logistics, focusing on its capacity to strengthen human and operational safety while simultaneously creating new risks for data protection, cybersecurity and automated decision-making. Methods: The study applies a structured literature review covering publications from 2018–2025 in Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar, supplemented by comparative analysis of AI-enabled and conventional security approaches and a case-based synthesis of cyber-physical disruptions relevant to logistics. Results: The review indicates that AI can improve anomaly detection, video surveillance, network monitoring, predictive maintenance, routing and incident response. At the same time, the same dependence on data-intensive models creates vulnerabilities related to adversarial inputs, data poisoning, model theft, privacy leakage, algorithmic bias, model drift and service disruption. These risks can propagate from digital systems to physical logistics operations and therefore affect both data subjects and personnel. Conclusions: AI can provide reliable proactive support for smart-logistics security only when it is embedded in lifecycle governance that combines secure data management, continuous model validation, human oversight, resilient fallback procedures and compliance with relevant cybersecurity, data-protection and AI-governance requirements. The most appropriate approach is therefore not full automation, but risk-based human-in-the-loop deployment supported by auditable technical and organizational controls.

title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
abstract: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Human Communication: From Machine-Mediated Human Communication to Human and Machine Communication
abstract: This systematic review assessed the ever-changing role of artificial intelligence and intelligent machines in human communication in the current globalized world. The findings reported in the current manuscript are from a systematic review of 17 papers published from 2002 to 2023. An online search using Web of Science (WoS) and SCOPUS databases was done to record the related works. A total of 58 works were recorded through an online search, and of all 58 items 17 works published from 2002 to 2023 in 15 different journals were selected and thoroughly reviewed. The reviewed works' results support the ever-growing and inevitable role of AI and intelligent machines in human communication. Based on the results, the influence of AI and intelligent machines on human communication is a modern opportunity. The results indicate that based on its fast growth, an intelligent machine powered by AI can conduct intra-machine communication and act as an autonomous communicator in active human interactions. Based on the results, people must adequately update their technical skills to deal with ever-growing communication technologies.

title: AI-Driven Motion Capture for Health-Oriented Performance Analysis and Training Optimization in Boxing
abstract: Boxing is a high-intensity combat sport with asymmetric motions, explosive actions, and a high danger of overtraining and injury. This means that rigorous monitoring is necessary for athlete heath. This research presents an AI-driven framework that amalgamates wearable inertial measurement sensors (Neuron32), machine learning models, and a multi-objective recommender system to oversee performance, forecast fatigue, assess training load, and avert injuries in both professional and amateur boxers. We kept an eye on 15 seasoned athletes and 97 amateur athletes, looking at things like exhaustion, training load, and injuries. We created predictive models for classifying fatigue and estimating load, and we used their results to build a recommender system that finds a compromise between improving performance and lowering risk. The results showed that the models were quite good at predicting outcomes. The fatigue classification had an AUC of 0.91, and the load prediction had a R² of 0.89. The recommender system also cut down on fatigue-related overload episodes by 21.3% and injuries by 13.8%. These results indicate that AI can provide objective, tailored insights for boxing training, facilitating both performance improvement and healthfocused approaches. In conclusion, this architecture shows how AI-enabled monitoring systems could improve precision sports medicine in boxing and be used as a paradigm for other combat and endurance sports.

title: Areca-CEDNet: Arecanut Plant Disease Classification Using Convolutional Encoder–decoder Network
abstract: Plant disease classification is crucial in agriculture for ensuring food security and sustainability.Traditional methods require expert knowledge, are time-consuming, and does not appropriate for large-scale analysis.Deep Learning (DL)-assisted image classification techniques offer effective performance in identifying plant diseases.This research proposes the arecanut leaf disease classification approach called Areca-Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network (Areca-CEDNet) architecture, which builds on and extends the concepts of the CED-Net and the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN).The study uses two datasets: a private Arecanut and the publicly available PlantVillage dataset, for implementing the proposed approach.A Visual Geometric Group-16 (VGG16) architecture extracts both low-and high-level features.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Areca-CEDNet method achieves an impressive accuracy of 99.93% on Arecanut dataset and 99.65% on PlantVillage dataset.This approach makes a significant contribution to sustainable Artificial Intelligence (AI) for plant disease detection by improving model generalization and allowing precise classification over diverse classes with smaller image sizes in DL-based agricultural applications.

title: AI in higher education: the role of students’ value orientations, effort perceptions, and academic ethics
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has led to its widespread adoption in highereducation. A growing body of research has examined its educational implications, includingeffects on learning and academic integrity. Building on this literature, this paper investigateshow students’ orientations toward learning, effort, and ethics relate to their use of AI inacademic contexts. The study was conducted on a sample of 115 undergraduate and graduatebusiness students using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Chi-squaretests and Cramer’s V coefficients. The results reveal significant relationships betweenstudents’ orientations and AI use. Students who prioritize efficiency, minimal effort, and finaloutcomes are more likely to use AI frequently, trust its outputs without verification, and rely onit for assignments. Likewise, students with more tolerant attitudes toward unethical academicbehavior are more likely to use AI as a shortcut in academic tasks. In contrast, students whovalue the learning process, theoretical knowledge, and academic integrity are more likely tocritically evaluate AI-generated content and consult additional sources. The findings suggestthat AI acts primarily as an amplifying tool rather than an independent driver of academicbehavior, reflecting pre-existing attitudes toward learning and ethics.

title: Digital Transformation Strategies for UAE Startups in the AI Era: A Critical Literature Review and Qualitative Research Framework
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive examination of digital transformation strategies for UAE startups navigating the artificial intelligence era, synthesizing insights from 163 scholarly sources and proposing a qualitative research framework based on 15 senior leadership interviews. The critical literature review reveals that successful digital transformation in UAE startups requires the strategic integration of three interdependent pillars: digital leadership capabilities, AI adoption practices, and organizational readiness. Key findings indicate that UAE startups face distinct challenges including skills shortages, ethical governance concerns, and resource constraints, while benefiting from supportive government initiatives aligned with national smart transformation agendas. The proposed qualitative methodology employs semi-structured interviews with 15 senior leaders across UAE startup ecosystems to capture nuanced insights into strategic decision-making, implementation challenges, and success factors. This research contributes to both academic understanding and practical guidance for startup leaders, policymakers, and ecosystem stakeholders seeking to accelerate digital transformation in the UAE's dynamic entrepreneurial landscape.

title: From Rubble to Resource: AI-Enhanced Biorecycling in Sustainable Construction Waste Management
abstract: Construction waste, accounting for up to one-third of global solid waste, presents substantial environmental and resource challenges. Rapid urbanization, intensive building activities, and heterogeneous waste streams exacerbate the problem, including hazardous materials such as asbestos and lead-based products. This paper evaluates the environmental impact of construction waste and examines reduction methods, highlighting biorecycling as the most effective and sustainable approach. Construction waste is categorized into inert, non-inert, and hazardous types to enable targeted management. The analysis reviews reduction techniques including design optimization, material efficiency, conventional recycling, and AI-enhanced biorecycling. Biorecycling methods, such as composting, anaerobic digestion, and vermicomposting, are optimized through Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive control of microbial activity, and improved waste segregation. The paper advocates for a combined strategy integrating traditional recycling with AI-driven biorecycling to maximize waste reduction, promote circular economy principles, and enhance sustainability in the construction sector.

title: Ecosystem Banking: Redefining Banking Services in an Interconnected World
abstract: Research background: The rapid digital transformation of the banking industry is accelerating the emergence of ecosystem banking as a new strategic paradigm in global finance. Technologies such as fintech, artificial intelligence (AI), open banking, and application programming interfaces (APIs) have transformed traditional banks into interconnected digital platforms. Furthermore, growing customer demand for fast, personalised, and integrated mobile banking services, together with evolving regulatory policies, is further increasing the importance of the ecosystem banking model. Purpose of the article: This study aims to identify the main drivers of banking ecosystem development and assess their effects on competitiveness, operational efficiency, profitability, innovation, and customer satisfaction in the banking sector. It also analyses differences among banking ecosystem models in Europe, Asia, and North America. Methods: The study adopts a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative and qualitative methods. Descriptive statistics and multiple regression models are used to analyse the relationship between ecosystem integration and bank performance indicators. The empirical analysis is based on data from 25 international banks and fintech companies operating between 2018 and 2025. The variables examined include API integration, AI adoption, fintech partnerships, profitability, customer loyalty, and customer satisfaction. Strategic ecosystem management and regional differences are further explored through a comparative analysis of Ant Group, BBVA, ING, DBS Bank, Revolut, and Goldman Sachs. Findings & Value added: The results show that ecosystem-based banking significantly improves operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, innovation capacity, and digital revenue growth compared with traditional banking models. API integration, Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS), AI adoption, and collaboration with fintech companies are identified as key drivers of improved banking performance. The Asian market exhibits the highest level of platform integration, whereas European banks benefit from a robust open banking regulatory framework. The study extends the existing literature by examining the technological, strategic, organisational, and regulatory dimensions of integrated banking ecosystem models. The findings provide relevant implications for financial regulation, cybersecurity, and digital governance and contribute to the literature on emerging global economic trends and digital transformation.

title: Student Perceptions of Innovative Educational Approaches in the Era of Generative AI
abstract: Research background: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and ongoing digital transformation are reshaping higher education and increasing demand for more flexible and competence-oriented educational approaches. Recent studies indicate that students tend to associate educational innovation less with technological novelty itself and more with flexibility, practical learning outcomes, and career relevance. Purpose of the article: This article aims to identify the key educational and digital factors that positively influence students’ perceptions of innovative educational approaches that support critical thinking and personal development in higher education. Methods: The quantitative research was conducted using a sample of 925 students from a partner university participating in a V4 research project. Students’ attitudes were collected through an online questionnaire administered in October 2025. The research hypotheses were tested using correlation analysis and linear regression modelling. The data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Findings & Value added: The findings indicate that students place greater value on educational approaches that support practical skills development, flexibility, and preparation for future careers than on technological novelty itself. The strongest positive effects were identified for approaches supporting the development of future career skills and flexible educational systems. By contrast, several variables related to AI and digital resources exhibited weaker or statistically non-significant effects. This may indicate that students increasingly perceive digital technologies as a standard component of higher education rather than as a distinct indicator of educational innovation. The study contributes to current debates on AI and educational innovation by demonstrating that students associate innovation more strongly with competence development and flexibility than with technological novelty alone.

title: Agentic Commerce and SME Competitiveness: An Integrative Review and Theory-Informed Research Framework
abstract: Research background: Artificial intelligence is shifting online shopping from recommendation-based assistance towards delegated search, comparison, configuration, and, in emerging cases, transaction execution. For SMEs, this transition may expand market access while simultaneously creating new forms of algorithmic gatekeeping and platform dependence. Purpose of the article: This integrative review develops a theory-informed explanation of how agentic commerce may affect SME competitiveness. Competitiveness is conceptualised as the joint ability to capture agent-mediated demand while preserving strategic option value, customer access, and bargaining autonomy over time. Methods: Seventeen documented OpenAlex title-and-abstract queries were used to identify English-language journal articles published between 2015 and July 2026. Following deduplication and eligibility screening, 117 Scopus- and/or Web of Science-indexed articles were reviewed in full, comprising 82 consumer-agent studies and 35 SME-platform studies. A concept-centric synthesis was conducted using dynamic capabilities and resource dependence as the principal theoretical lenses. The review does not claim exhaustive coverage or pooled causal effects, as the discovery process relied on a single source and only one record was identified through direct merchant-bridge queries. Claims were therefore calibrated according to evidential directness, convergence across research designs, and proximity to the outcome of interest. Findings & Value added: The synthesis identifies five core themes: assistance-to-delegation, machine legibility, trust transfer, empowerment–dependence, and offering/governance contingency. The proposed framework distinguishes foundational capabilities—product-data legibility, interface and transaction readiness, and verifiable trust evidence—from higher-order sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring capabilities. These mechanisms operate through eligibility and visibility, trust transfer, delegation depth, and dependency exposure. The evidence is moderate for consumer trust mechanisms and established forms of platform dependence, but remains limited for execution-capable agents, direct SME outcomes, and comparative boundary effects. Six propositions are developed to provide a testable rather than validated causal framework. The findings are relevant to SME managers, platform and AI-agent designers, policymakers, and researchers seeking to understand how firms can capture agent-mediated demand without surrendering strategic option value.

title: Are we thinking green? Determinants of green purchasing intention among the elderly towards green vehicles in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Research background: Despite growing environmental concerns and active government promotion, electric vehicle (EV) uptake in sub-Saharan Africa remains notably low, representing a significant gap in the region’s transition towards sustainable mobility. Furthermore, while the global shift towards green transportation continues to accelerate, the specific socio-demographic factors influencing EV adoption among older adults in the region remain substantially under-researched. Purpose of the article: This study aims to investigate the determinants of EV adoption intentions among older adults in sub-Saharan Africa, where EV uptake remains limited despite increasing environmental concerns and government support. Methods: Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the study analyses empirical data collected from a sample of 312 registered vehicle owners aged 55 years and older. By examining this specific cohort across three major metropolitan areas in Ghana, the study provides detailed demographic and behavioural insights into a population segment whose perspectives are important for understanding the region’s transition towards green mobility. The research hypotheses were tested using confirmatory factor analysis and covariance-based structural equation modelling. The data were analysed using IBM SPSS Amos. Findings & Value added: The findings identify four key factors that significantly and positively influence behavioural intentions to purchase environmentally friendly vehicles: attitudes and beliefs towards EVs, financial incentives, environmental concern, and uncertainty avoidance. Furthermore, uncertainty avoidance was found to positively moderate the relationships between these factors and behavioural intention, thereby strengthening the effects of attitudes, financial incentives, and environmental concern on purchase decisions. The study highlights the need for targeted and multifaceted strategies to encourage EV adoption among older consumers. Practical implications include fostering positive attitudes towards EVs, designing effective financial incentive programmes, promoting environmental awareness, and developing communication strategies that address risk-related concerns. By focusing on an under-researched demographic in a developing African context, the study provides valuable insights for policymakers and marketers seeking to advance sustainable transportation and reduce the environmental impacts of conventional vehicles in the region.

title: AI-driven optimisation of drug delivery systems for therapeutic enhanced efficacy
abstract: By guaranteeing that medicinal materials reach the intended spot in the body with maximum efficacy and few side effects, drug delivery systems (DDS) are essential to modern medicine. However, time-consuming and expensive trial-and-error methods are frequently used in traditional drug delivery systems. Predictive modelling, formulation optimisation, and tailored therapy have all been made possible by the development of artificial intelligence (AI), especially machine learning and deep learning, which have drastically changed pharmaceutical research. This study examines how AI-assisted optimisation affects therapeutic results in drug delivery systems. Advanced drug carrier design, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic behaviour prediction, and real-time drug release monitoring are all made possible by AI technologies. Additionally, specialized delivery methods like nanoparticle-based carriers, which increase drug bioavailability and lower toxicity, are made possible by AI-driven models. AI has a lot of promise, but there are still issues with data quality, regulations, and model interpretability. Future medication delivery is anticipated to be revolutionized by the integration of AI with digital health platforms, nanotechnology, and precision medicine. This study highlights important technologies, applications, difficulties, and opportunities while examining the function of AI-assisted optimization in drug delivery systems and assessing its potential to enhance therapeutic outcomes.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SPORTS PERFORMANCE AND COACHING: CURRENT APPLICATIONS AND EMERGING CHALLENGES
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to transform athlete data into predictions, classifications, and decision-support outputs for coaches and sport scientists. This review examines current applications of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and generative artificial intelligence in sports performance and coaching. A structured narrative approach was used to synthesize peer-reviewed research published mainly between 2018 and 2026, with emphasis on athlete monitoring, training individualization, technical and tactical analysis, injury-risk estimation, talent identification, and coach learning. The evidence shows that artificial intelligence can automate movement recognition, combine high-frequency wearable and tracking data, identify non-linear performance patterns, and improve the speed of video and match analysis. However, predictive accuracy reported in experimental studies does not automatically translate into effective coaching decisions. Small samples, class imbalance, inconsistent outcome definitions, limited external validation, data leakage, poor calibration, and low model explainability remain frequent problems. Generative tools can support planning, report preparation, and reflective practice, but their outputs require verification because they may omit context or generate inaccurate recommendations. The most appropriate role of artificial intelligence is therefore decision support rather than autonomous decision-making. Practical implementation should begin with a clear coaching question, validated data, interpretable outputs, and continuous human oversight. Future research should prioritize multicenter validation, female and youth athlete representation, sport-specific benchmarks, transparent reporting, and prospective studies that measure whether AI-supported decisions improve performance, health, and coaching efficiency.

title: Enriched Proximal Gradient Descent Deep Unfolding Framework for Rice Leaf Disease Classification
abstract: Rice leaf diseases create a critical threat to global food security, which requires rapid and effective diagnostic solutions.Existing Deep Learning (DL) frameworks, such as Residual Network (ResNet) and Visual Geometry Group Network (VGGNet) struggle to handle variations in lighting, background canopy clutter, and visual metamerism, which reduces the detection performance under various environmental conditions.To address these challenges, this research introduces the Enriched Proximal Gradient Descent Deep Unfolding Framework (EPGD-DUF) to develop an environmentally robust model to reduce sensitivity towards domain-specific illumination and background variations for rice-leaf disease detection.EPGD-DUF architecture employs the Proximal Gradient Descent (PGD) algorithm across four parameter-shared stages to mathematically model software-synthesized pseudo-spectral latent reconstruction.This integrates a Cross-Channel Latent Fusion Module (CCLFM) to suppress soil-line vectors and applies a Hyperspherical ArcFace classification head to strictly separate angular classes.The detection performance of the EPGD-DUF is evaluated on two standard datasets, achieving 99.83% accuracy on the laboratorycontrolled Mendeley rice leaf disease dataset and 98.89% accuracy on the highly cluttered Paddy Doctor field dataset.The proposed EPGD-DUF achieves higher accuracy than other baseline models, such as ResNet50, VGG16, ConvNeXt, and Vanilla PINN baselines under the corresponding dataset specific evaluation protocols.Under an explicit laboratory-to-field transfer protocol over the four classes common to both repositories, the framework retains 96.2% accuracy on the held-out target-domain test set, while target-domain labels were not used during adaptation or model selection, corresponding to a domain gap of 3.6 percentage points, compared with 6.0 percentage points for the strongest convolutional baseline.

title: The Evolution of the Music Industry in Light of Information and Communication Technologies
abstract: This paper examines the transformative role of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) in shaping contemporary music industry structures, practices and economies. Drawing on a systematic literature review, the study maps how digital tools, from digital audio workstations, streaming platforms, recommendation algorithms to technologies such as AI and Virtual Reality, have changed the creative agency, altered revenue streams and reconfigured audience engagement. Findings indicate a double-sided transformation, as ICTs have made music production more participatory and lowered market entry barriers, enabling diverse voices, while concentrating attention and value through platform-mediated algorithms that favor scale and discoverability. Monetization has shifted from ownership to access, creating new micro-revenue models, also raising concerns about artist remuneration, copyright enforcement and market oversaturation. Using a dataset of 5300 scientific sources published between 2015 and 2025, the analysis conducted in the VOSviewer program shows the thematic architecture of the field and reveals how scholars, institutions, countries and conceptual domains interact. The results offer a structural overview and validate the relevance of this topic as a rapidly expanding research frontier. The paper reviews current trends in the literature and outlines future research agendas on AI authorship, immersive live experiences and data governance, aiming to guide academics, industry stakeholders, specialists in the field of Computer Sciences and policymakers navigating the digital music ecosystem. Finally, it discusses regulatory, ethical and business-model implications, emphasizing the need for policy interventions that balance innovation with fair compensation and cultural diversity.

title: TRANSFORMING KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATOR (KPI) TRACKING IN HIGHER EDUCATION THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING: THE APPLICATION OF THE PREMIER SCORE INDEX (PSI) IN HIGHER EDUCATION
abstract: The rapid digital transformation in higher education has exposed a critical flaw in institutional governance: traditional Key Performance Indicator (KPI) tracking methods that reliant on manual data entry, siloed systems, and static reports are increasingly obsolete and lack the precision, adaptability, and responsiveness needed in today's data-intensive environments. To address this pressing need for data-driven evaluation tools, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are fundamentally transforming performance management by introducing real-time analytics, strategic alignment, and Data-informed decision-making. This study explores the development and application of the Premier Score Index (PSI), a novel, weighted composite metric assessing institutional performance across five strategic domains: Teaching, Research, Community Service, Professional Service, and Academic Reputation. Through a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis from 2010 to 2024, the paper identifies how AI/MLenhance KPI tracking across its lifecycle: development, monitoring, and reporting. Findings reveal the potential of AI-driven KPI systems, such as the PSI, to revolutionize institutional planning and accountability, positioning academic institutions to thrive in a rapidly evolving digitallandscape.

title: A LITERATURE REVIEW OF RADIAL BASIS FUNCTION NEURAL NETWORKS FOR BLAST EXPLOSIVE PREDICTION
abstract: This review paper examines the development and application of Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) for predicting blast explosive effects. Addressing the complexities of nonlinear and multi-physics blast phenomena, it highlights the advantages of data-driven approaches over traditional analytical methods. The paper presents the fundamentals of RBF networks, including their architecture, training techniques, and optimization strategies, emphasizing their capacity for universal function approximation and adaptability. A broad range of application domains such as mechanical control systems, energy and environmental modelling, medical diagnostics, and materials science underscore the versatility of RBF models. Performance evaluations demonstrate their robustness and accuracy in handling nonlinearities and uncertainties, although challenges related to computational complexity and data limitations persist. The review discusses hybrid modelling approaches and emerging methodologies like quantum kernels and interpretable artificial intelligence to address existing gaps. Ultimately, this synthesis underscores the significant potential of RBF neural networks in advancing blast effect prediction and suggests pathways for future research integrating novel computational techniques to further enhance prediction accuracy and reliability.

title: GENERATION Z’S ATTITUDES AND SOFT SKILLS SET TO GREEN HOTELS AND SUSTAINABILITY ON THE BASIS OF A HUNGARIAN EMPIRICAL STUDY
abstract: Generation Z, encompassing individuals born between the mid-1990s and early 2010s, is emerging in shaping the future of sustainable tourism. Characterized by their digital fluency, social consciousness, and environmental awareness, Generation Z's preferences and behaviours are influencing various sectors, notably tourism and hospitality. This paper delves into three interconnected aspects: Gen Z's perceptions of sustainability in tourism, their criteria for selecting green hotels, and the skills and competencies they deem essential to foster receptivity towards sustainable practices. In 2024, research on green tourism was started to analyse the factors that play a role in choosing green accommodation. For the study, a questionnaire survey was conducted, which consisted of 26 questions and resulted in 246 responses. Based on the definitions of green hotels and green tourism students gave, it can be seen that they unanimously agree on the green content of hotels and tourism. Although they are committed to green ideas, this is not always reflected in their willingness to pay more for these services. The most important contextual skills for generating this commitment include respect for the environment, efficiency, adaptability and resilience. As the research has proved their strong commitment to environmental principles, we can confirm that Gen Z has emerged as a dominating force in the tourist business today, and their preferences and actions are changing th e face of the travel and hospitality sector, particularly with regard to sustainability challenges. It is important to note, however, that one important finding of the research is that openness and receptivity to green hotels does not necessarily correlate with the willingness or intention to pay more for this option.

title: Effect of Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbots on the 21st Century Skills Development of Undergraduate Students
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) learning tools such as chatbots have the potential to enhance the learning experience of students and develop their 21st Century skills. In this study, we investigate how the use of AI chatbots affects the development of undergraduate students’ communication, collaboration, creativity and critical thinking which are essential 21st century skills. Using a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data was collected from a stratified sample of 382 undergraduate students from four public universities in Ghana. The findings of the study show that, there is high prevalence of AI chatbot usage among students with ChatGPT and Meta AI being the most utilized tools. The students mainly use AI chatbots for researching information and assisting them in their assignments. It was also found that the frequent use of AI chatbots significantly relates to the development of communication, creativity and critical thinking skills among students, but not their collaboration skills. Moreover, the frequency of AI chatbot usage among students is significantly affected by their age and level of study, whereas their gender, field of study and institution had no significant effect. The findings of the study underscore the importance of targeted interventions in guiding students to ethically use AI chatbots to develop essential 21st century skills.

title: The Architecture of the Intuition Ecosystem Model (IEM): Multidimensional Validation and Decision Engineering in Complex Governance
abstract: This article consolidates the validation of the Intuition Ecosystem Model (IEM) as a disruptive governance infrastructure. Grounded in the integration of human neurophysiology and complex systems theory (Balloni, 2022), the IEM Model optimizes decision-making under extreme uncertainty. The validation of this Model is presented through a multidimensional lens: (i) structural, via Self-Organizing Holarchic Open Systems (SOHO); (ii) biological, through the 'somatic congruence' metric; and (iii) ethical, grounded in the concept of Ecoism. This work culminates in the Balloni Protocol, an auditable procedural flow that harmonizes algorithmic precision with biological wisdom. By synthesizing these structural, biological, and ethical dimensions, the study provides a robust technical blueprint for contemporary governance, ensuring that technological integration enhances human sovereign intelligence and effectively mitigates the systemic risks of cognitive atrophy in automated governance.

title: Critical Issues in Building Information Modeling (BIM) Workflows: A Multi-Case Study Review
abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) is increasingly used in structural and infrastructure engineering as a digital environment supporting design, construction, and asset management processes. However, the application of BIM to complex infrastructures still presents several critical issues, particularly when dealing with non-standard geometries, existing structures, and heterogeneous information flows. This paper presents a technical synthesis based on six case studies developed by the authors through BIM-based approaches applied to different structural and infrastructural fields, including bridges, road infrastructures, underground utility networks, and complex structural systems. The study analyzes the main issues encountered during the modeling, coordination, and data exchange phases, highlighting the strategies adopted to address them. The identified challenges mainly concern the geometric modeling of irregular or existing structures, interoperability issues between BIM software and structural analysis software, the management of point clouds and survey-derived data, as well as the definition of appropriate Levels of Development and Information. The paper provides a technical overview of recurring issues and offers useful indications for improving BIM workflows applied to structural and infrastructure engineering.

title: PERCEIVED CULTURAL PERFORMANCE AND BEHAVIORAL INTENTIONS IN GASTRONOMY FESTIVALS: A FUZZY-SET QUALITATIVE COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF LOCAL IDENTITY AND HERITAGE AWARENESS
abstract: The study aims to understand the concept of perceived cultural performance at gastronomy festivals, along with its coupling with local identity and cultural heritage to influence the behavioral intentions of visitors. For data collection purposes, a structured survey instrument was employed to obtain data from 544 domestic and foreign visitors who visited the two major gastronomy festivals, namely GastroANTEP in Gaziantep, Türkiye, and the Budapest Wine and Gourmet Festival in Hungary. In other words, the settings used here provide a cross-cultural foundation to examine the issue of gastronomic heritage in different kinds of festivals. Configurational design approach is used to avoid assuming a specific path towards the accomplishment of each outcome. Data have been analyzed using fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), which is an asymmetric approach for finding alternative combinations of conditions resulting in the same outcome. High behavioral intention and high perceived cultural performance are both considered to be focal outcomes of the configurational analysis. Six sufficient configurations have been found for behavioral intention; among them, the top three configurations show consistencies ranging from 0.962 to 0.969 and coverages ranging from 0.844 to 0.874, implying that there are alternative combinations of conditions that lead to high behavioral intention through the interplay of perceptions about cultural performance, local identity, and cultural heritage. Five configurations have been found in case of high perceived cultural performance, where the overall solution shows coverage value of 0.975 and consistency value of 0.905. Equifinality has thus been demonstrated, and none of the individual condition has been found to explain visitors' responses. The study adds to the literature in the domain of gastronomy and tourism by operationalizing the theory of cultural performance.

title: AI-Facilitated Formative Feedback and Students’ Classroom Engagement: A Review of Pedagogical Integration, Learning Outcomes, and Teacher-Student Interaction Dynamics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) supported formative feedback has emerged as ostensibly transformative pedagogical tool, however, its influence within traditional (physical) classroom settings are still insufficiently synthesized. The present review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, examined 21 empirical studies published from 2014 till 2026 to examine how AI-supported formative feedback effect student’s engagement and redefines teacher-student interaction patterns in traditional classrooms informed by a multi-perspectival conceptual framework incorporating formative feedback theory, the tripartite engagement model, and classroom orchestration theory, thematic synthesis indicated that AI feedback effects on behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement are conditional rather than universal, moderated by feedback elaboration level, temporal granularity, cognitive load, and learner prior knowledge. A directional shift in teacher function from primary feedback provider to orchestrator of AI-generated analytics was the most consistent finding across studies. Three structural tensions were identified: scalability versus relational quality, personalization versus cognitive overload, and AI reliability versus contextual responsiveness. These findings substantiate a conditional engagement model and emphasises that teacher orchestration is a non-negotiable precondition for the effectiveness of AI feedback in classroom ecologies.

title: Professional Development Needs of Physics Teachers in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming educational practice, creating new opportunities and challenges for teachers. This study explored the professional development needs of secondary school physics teachers for effective AI integration in Kampala, Uganda. A qualitative descriptive research design was adopted, involving 22 purposively selected physics teachers with experience in digital technologies and awareness of AI applications. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Six themes emerged: awareness and understanding of AI, current use of AI in physics teaching, barriers to AI adoption, required AI competencies, professional development priorities, and institutional support needs. The findings revealed that although teachers recognized the potential of AI to enhance lesson preparation, assessment, and conceptual understanding, they lacked adequate knowledge, practical skills, and institutional support for effective classroom implementation. Participants emphasized the need for continuous, practical, subject-specific professional development focusing on AI literacy, pedagogical integration, ethical considerations, and prompt engineering. The study concludes that effective AI integration requires coordinated investments in teacher capacity building, supportive institutional policies, technological infrastructure, and sustained professional learning opportunities.

title: From Design to Discovery: A Systematic Review of Canva AI as a Pedagogical Tool in Education
abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has drawn attention to digital learning tools that support creativity and effective teaching. Canva is originally a graphic design platform that evolved into an AI-assisted education tool. This study conducted a systematic review following the PRISMA guidelines and the SPIDER framework to explore Canva’s role in secondary education, focusing on its uses, benefits and challenges. From 1,725 initial records, 15 peer-reviewed studies ,lastly from Indonesia and a few from Malaysia met the inclusion criteria. Findings show that Canva is widely used for visual learning and content creation in language, social studies and science subjects. It enhances student motivation, comprehension, creativity, improves writing and digital literacy. However, its classroom use remains short-term and teacher-centered , with limited focus on science and higher-order thinking. Reported challenges include low digital literacy, poor infrastructure and insufficient teacher training. Overall, Canva is a flexible platform that supports 21st-century learning, but equitable access and teacher readiness are essential for its effective technology integration.

title: PREFERENCES OF DIGITAL NOMADS: ANALYZING POPULAR DESTINATIONS AND DECISION-MAKING FACTORS THROUGH INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS USING PUBLIC ACCESS DATABASES
abstract: Digital nomadism is a rapidly spreading form of location-independent work that is fundamentally transforming the global labour market, economy, and tourism. The aim of this study is to quantitatively explore and model the destination preferences of digital nomads and to present an innovative, interactive data visualization framework. Our research analyses the structural changes of the period 2021-2024 following the logic of the PEST model (Political, Economical, Social, Technological). The study is based on a longitudinal database collected by a proprietary Python-based web scraping method from the nomads.com platform, which was analyzed using Spearman's rank correlation and multiple linear regression (OLS). The methodological innovation of the research is an interactive visualization dashboard based on the PEST framework, created with Tableau software, which enables the real-time exploration of complex decision factors and their trade-offs. Our results indicate significant restructuring of preferences. In the post-pandemic period, the social dimension, especially the quality of community life and safety, has become the most decisive attraction. The correlation coefficient between the Community factor and popularity increased from 0.58 to 0.65, and its explanatory power in our regression models nearly doubled relative to 2021. In parallel, technological infrastructure (internet speed) and healthcare have become critical, significant factors, indicating the professionalization of lifestyle. The relative importance of the cost factor has decreased. Geographically, Bangkok (Thailand) leads the global ranking, and Europe (Spain, Portugal) is making significant progress with the introduction of digital nomad visas. The higher coefficient of determination (R² = 0.455) for the 2024 decision models indicates that nomadic choices are becoming more rational and can be better described by objective indicators. Our study demonstrates how the integrated application of modern data science and infocommunication tools can support conscious decision-making for both digital nomads and host tourism destinations in this dynamically changing market environment.

title: THE IMPACT OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT COSTS ON THE OPERATIONAL PROFITS OF JORDANIAN COMPANIES
abstract: Research and development drive competitive advantage but requires substantial investments that can constrain profitability. This study examines the impact of R&D costs on the operating profits of Jordanian pharmaceutical companies listed in ASE from 2015-2022. Financial data across five major players is analysed using multiple regression techniques using EViews. The results reveal a statistically significant positive relationship whereby a 1% increase in R&D spending as a proportion of revenue enhances the profit margin by 0.17%. However, when controlled for company size, the R&D impact becomes insignificant, indicating scale-based barriers. But incorporating age and sales growth factors restores significance, suggesting life cycle contingent effects. However, R&D displays a contingent profitable influence depending on organizational context. Thus, for further research can support optimal resource allocation towards differentiated research initiatives across market segments. Quantifying input-output mechanisms and delineating cost thresholds promises to nurture the pharmaceutical innovation ecosystem. This paper offers specific insights for pharmaceutical leaders to optimize innovation planning based on companyspecific factors to elevate financial sustainability. This paper highlights the need for evidence-based allocation decisions catering to life cycle stage, growth objectives and market positioning. Based on the study's findings, companies should create collaborative partnerships with universities and research institutions. The collaborative partnerships will help them cover service gaps, reduce costs, and, most importantly, reduce the uncertainties that come with innovation. Managers should consider the size, age, and growth levels of the firm while developing research and development strategies. On the other hand , policymakers should pay special attention to innovative strategies, especially in the pharmaceutical industry. This should be done by introducing appropriate rewards, financing, and initiatives to support R&D.

title: FROM IMAGES TO UNDERSTANDING: INFOGRAPHICS AS AN EFFECTIVE TOOL FOR SHAPING CHILDREN’S SPATIAL THINKING IN GEOGRAPHY
abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of infographic-based learning in developing spatial thinking skills among primary students and examined the sustainability of these skills over time in geography learning environments. A quasiexperimental design was employed with an experimental group (n = 50) and a control group (n = 50) from private schools in the Al-Ahsa region of Saudi Arabia. Spatial thinking skills were assessed using a structured test, with pre-test scores serving as a covariate to control for initial differences between groups. Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) was conducted to determine the immediate impact of the intervention, while a paired samples t-test evaluated skill retention three months post-intervention. The results revealed that students in the experimental group, who received geography learning using infographics, achieved significantly higher adjusted post-test scores across all spatial thinking domains compared to their peers in control group, with large effect sizes (η² ranging from 0.64 to 0.95). These findings indicate that integrating visual and textual information through infographics facilitates meaningful learning, enhances students’ ability to construct mental representations of spatial concepts, reduces cognitive load, and promotes higher-order thinking skills. The delayed post-test results further demonstrated stable or slightly improved performance, confirming that infographic-based learning supports the long-term retention and sustainability of spatial thinking skills. Pedagogically, the study contributes by demonstrating how infographic-based instruction can integrate foundational and complex spatial skills, strengthen cognitive processing, and provide teachers with an effective tool for enhancing students’ spatial reasoning and problem-solving abilities. Based on these findings, it is recommended to incorporate infographic-based approaches into primary education curricula, train teachers in effective infographic usage, and adopt diverse assessment strategies, including observational and qualitative methods, to complement traditional tests. Overall, the study provides compelling evidence that infographic-based learning is an effective and sustainable pedagogical approach in geography teaching and learning, offering practical implications for curriculum design, instructional strategies, and educational innovation.

title: SACRED PLACES IN A SHADOW AS A RESOURCE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF RELIGIOUS TOURISM: A CASE STUDY IN SOUTHWESTERN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to analyze less familiar Orthodox sites in Blagoevgrad District of Southwestern Bulgaria, defined here as “sacred places in a shadow” as a factor for religious tourism development, specifically through community-led charitable activities for their renovation. Observations and visual data serve as the starting point of the analysis. Next, the study applies the mixed-methods approach, integrating field observation and visual documentation of six selected sites with 34 in-depth interviews. These were conducted with adult Bulgarian citizens residing in the territory of Blagoevgrad district. The interviewees included persons directly involved in local church activities (e.g. priests, church members, lay officials (klisari)), which made it possible to outline the different aspects of the research problem.The results are contextualized through an analysis of a national representative survey (n =1283) to evaluate broader trends in religion and socialization. The findings suggest that the “sacred places in shadow” can function as vital tools for social cohesion, evidenced by localized efforts and volunteer-led renovations. These activities demonstrate that besides the scope of tourism, these sites are a tool for collective philanthropy and community spirit. The data indicate that these “sacred places in a shadow" contribute to the local society spirit and the are factor for the development of religious tourism in the region. The study concludes that their integration into the tourism product profile can strengthen regional identity and better align with the principles of community social value. This approach offers a replicable framework for peripheral regions seeking to balance cultural heritage preservation with sustainable economic growth. By repositioning overlooked spiritual landmarks for civic engagement, the research underscores the profound interconectedness of faith and regional development.

title: Sustainable Agriculture and Food Security
abstract: Agriculture and food security are central to sustainable development in Bangladesh and South Asia, where millions of smallholder farmers depend on agriculture for their livelihoods and where food systems face increasing pressures from climate change, natural resource degradation, population growth, market volatility, and changing dietary needs. Ensuring long-term food and nutrition security requires a transition towards agricultural systems that are productive, resource-efficient, climate-resilient, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable. Sustainable Agriculture and Food Security examines the interconnected dimensions of sustainable agriculture and resilient food systems, with particular emphasis on Bangladesh and relevant experiences across South Asia. The book explores climate-smart agriculture, agroecological approaches, soil health, sustainable water management, efficient irrigation, biodiversity conservation, circular agriculture, and environmentally responsible farming practices. It also investigates the potential of precision agriculture, digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT) to improve agricultural productivity, resource-use efficiency, and climate adaptation. Particular attention is given to the opportunities and challenges associated with adopting these innovations among smallholder farmers, women, and young people. Beyond farm-level production, the book examines agricultural finance, agribusiness development, market access, value-chain integration, sustainable food supply chains, and the policy and institutional frameworks needed to strengthen food security. Drawing on empirical research, regional experiences, case studies, and policy-oriented analysis, it highlights practical pathways for improving agricultural livelihoods, reducing environmental pressures, and building more inclusive and resilient food systems. The book aims to serve as a useful resource for researchers, students, development practitioners, agricultural professionals, and policymakers working towards sustainable agriculture and food security in Bangladesh and South Asia.

title: Decision-Making: A Narrative Review
abstract: The risks that have been presented in this current literature on decision-making include elevated arousal, COVID-19, independent medical decisions, gaming disorder, and gambling addiction. Several predictors of decision-making have appeared in this current literature including reversible decisions, experiential information, social media use, and ChatGPT advice. Only two potential underlying biological mechanisms have appeared in this literature on decision-making including the influence of dopamine and activation of the temporoparietal junction. Several methodological limitations can be noted for this literature including issues regarding sampling, variable selection and missing topics like interventions.

title: Contemporary Business Management: Concepts, Strategies, and Applications
abstract: The changing global business environment, technological advancements, and evolving stakeholder expectations have transformed the principles and practices of contemporary business management. Organizations increasingly require effective managerial strategies, informed decision-making, innovative business models, and sustainable practices to remain competitive and achieve long-term success. However, students and aspiring professionals often encounter challenges in understanding fundamental management concepts, applying theoretical frameworks to practical business situations, and responding effectively to emerging organizational and market challenges. This book, Contemporary Business Management: Concepts, Strategies, and Applications, provides a comprehensive yet accessible introduction to the fundamental principles, theories, strategies, and practices of modern business management. Designed primarily for early-career researchers, academicians, and practitioners, along with undergraduate and postgraduate students, the book integrates foundational management knowledge with practical business applications and contemporary organizational perspectives. The book begins with the fundamental concepts of management, the evolution of management thought, organizational structures, and the business environment. It subsequently explores core managerial functions and business disciplines, including planning, decision-making, strategic management, leadership, organizational behavior, human resource management, marketing, financial management, and operations and supply chain management. Building on these foundations, the book examines contemporary developments in entrepreneurship, innovation, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, business analytics, corporate governance, business ethics, and sustainable management. Particular emphasis is placed on the practical application of management theories, strategic decision-making, organizational effectiveness, and responsible business practices in dynamic and competitive environments. Drawing on real-world business examples and case studies from international markets and emerging economies, with particular attention to Bangladesh, the book demonstrates how management concepts and strategic frameworks can be applied to address contemporary business challenges. Accessible explanations, practical illustrations, managerial tools, review questions, and problem-solving exercises are incorporated to strengthen conceptual understanding, analytical thinking, and decision-making skills. By bridging established management principles with emerging business practices, this book aims to equip students and aspiring professionals with the knowledge, competencies, and practical insights necessary to understand modern organizations, respond to changing business environments, and contribute to effective, innovative, and sustainable business management.

title: AI-ENABLED COMMUNICATION EFFICIENCY AS A MEDIATOR BETWEEN REGULATORY ADAPTATION, INTERCULTURAL TRAINING, AND PROJECT PERFORMANCE IN GEOSITE TOURISM DEVELOPMENT: A CASE OF YUNNAN CONSTRUCTION AND INVESTMENT HOLDING GROUP
abstract: This study develops and tests a mediation model in which AI-enabled communication efficiency (AICE) transmits the effects of regulatory adaptation (RA) and intercultural training (ICT) to project performance (PP) in geosite tourism development projects associated with Yunnan Construction and Investment Holding Group (YCIH). A sequential quantitative design is specified and analyzed data from 320 respondents that represents stakeholder responses in a provincial state-owned enterprise project context. Quantitative analysis follows the structure: indicator loadings, reliability (ρA, ρc, α), convergent validity (AVE), discriminant validity (Fornell–Larcker and HTMT), structural paths with bootstrapped standard errors, effect sizes (f²), and predictive diagnostics (R², Q²predict, RMSE, MAE). Regulatory adaptation and intercultural training both improve AI-enabled communication efficiency (β = 0.430 and 0.370, p < 0.001). AI-enabled communication efficiency improves project performance (β = 0.410, p < 0.001) and partially mediates the effects of regulatory adaptation and intercultural training on performance (indirect effects β = 0.176 and 0.152, p < 0.001). The model explains 38.2% of the variance in AICE and 45.3% in PP, with acceptable predictive relevance (Q²predict = 0.369 for AICE; 0.436 for PP). For geosite tourism development, where projects must satisfy geopark governance expectations for visibility, conservation, and community participation. This study positions AICE as a managerial lever that makes regulatory and intercultural capabilities “actionable.” It suggests that horizon scanning and cross-cultural capability building yield stronger performance benefits when project teams adopt AIsupported translation, summarisation, and knowledge-routing routines consistent with responsible AI governance.

title: EXPERIENCE ECONOMY AS A CATALYST FOR SUSTAINABLE GEOSITE TOURISM: SERVICE DESIGN MECHANISMS IN THE DUNHUANG DESTINATION SYSTEM, CHINA
abstract: This study examines how experience economy perceptions are associated with sustainable geosite tourism intention in Dunhuang, China, through service design mechanisms and place engagement. A cross-sectional visitor survey yielded 452 valid responses for PLS-SEM analysis, and semi-structured interviews with visitors and frontline staff were completed as contextual support for understanding destination touchpoints. The measurement model demonstrates satisfactory reliability and convergent validity, while discriminant validity is supported, with the EE-SDM HTMT value (0.8925) remaining below 0.90. The structural results show positive relationships for EE→SDM (β=0.824), SDM→SGTI (β=0.385), and EE→SGTI (β=0.457). The indirect association EE→SDM→SGTI is significant (β=0.319, 95% CI [0.241, 0.398]), and place engagement positively moderates the SDM→SGTI relationship (β=0.184, p<.01). The model therefore indicates that memorable destination experiences are linked to sustainable tourism intentions partly through visitors' perceptions of coherent, interpretable, and participation-oriented service design, with the strength of this relationship varying by place engagement. The study contributes a destination-system perspective that connects experience staging, service design, and sustainability-oriented intention across heritage, landscape, transport, and digital touchpoints. Managerially, the findings support touchpoint mapping, interpretive micro-experiences, coordinated digital-physical services, and context-sensitive stewardship cues across the Dunhuang destination network.

title: FACTORS INFLUENCING THE PURCHASE CONTINUANCE USAGE OF DIGITAL TOURISM PLATFORMS: AN INTEGRATED MODEL
abstract: The main objective of the current study is to investigate antecedent factors influencing the continuance usage of digital tourism platforms in emerging markets (e.g., Jordan). This objective reflects the growing importance of digital platforms in shaping tourists’ travel planning and destination selection processes. An online survey was used to collect data from 519 social networking users who rely on digital tourism platforms to select their tourist destinations. These users actively depend on online platforms to obtain tourism information, explore destinations, and review travel experiences shared by others. Partial least squares-structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used for data analysis. This method was selected because it is suitable for analysing complex models and examining relationships between multiple constructs. The results confirmed that all direct hypotheses were accepted except the first hypothesis (H1), and hence the related hypothesis was rejected. This indicates that most of the proposed relationships in the research model were statistically supported. Regarding the indirect hypothesis (the moderating effect of e-WOM), the results show that e-WOM has moderated the relationship between purchase usage and continuation usage. In other words, the presence of electronic word-of-mouth strengthens the relationship between users’ purchase-related activities and their intention to continue using the platforms. This study provides valuable and actionable insights to tourism marketers, digital strategists, and managers of social networking platforms about how to further engage, satisfy and retain their users in the long term. These insights may assist practitioners in improving user experience and enhancing platform engagement strategies. Knowing digital tourist behavioural patterns, especially in the Jordanian context, helps programs achieve more targeted and more effective marketing strategies. Such understanding is particularly important for developing digital marketing initiatives that better respond to the needs and expectations of tourism platform users.

title: Generative AI-supported problem-based learning for enhancing computational thinking and chemistry achievement in engineering chemistry
abstract: The increasing adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created new opportunities to enhance active learning; however, empirical evidence regarding its integration with Problem-Based Learning (PBL) in Engineering Chemistry remains limited, particularly for simultaneously fostering Computational Thinking (CT) and chemistry achievement. This study investigates the effectiveness of integrating GenAI with PBL in an undergraduate Engineering Chemistry course within a Mechanical Engineering Education program. In the intervention, GPT-4 was embedded as an AI learning scaffold that guided students through Socratic questioning, provided formative feedback, and supported problem decomposition and analysis during collaborative PBL activities rather than supplying direct answers. Employing a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design, the study involved 68 undergraduate students (n = 34 experimental; n = 34 control) selected through cluster random sampling. Data were collected using three validated instruments: a Computational Thinking Test (CTT, 30 items, ? = .87), a Chemistry Achievement Test (CAT, 35 items, ? = .84), and a Learning Observation Sheet (LOS, 20 items, ICC = .91). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Shapiro-Wilk normality tests, Levene's homogeneity tests, independent-samples t-tests, ANCOVA, and Cohen's d effect size analysis. The results revealed significant improvements in both CT skills (t(66) = 8.47, p .001) and chemistry achievement (t(66) = 9.12, p .001) in the experimental group compared with the control group. ANCOVA controlling for pretest scores confirmed significant treatment effects for CT (F(1,65) = 127.84, p .001) and chemistry achievement (F(1,65) = 109.07, p .001), with large practical effects (Cohen's d = 2.14 and 2.06, respectively). These findings provide empirical support for integrating AI-supported scaffolding within structured PBL environments to strengthen computational thinking and conceptual understanding in Engineering Chemistry, while extending the pedagogical application of AI-enhanced constructivist learning in engineering education.

title: Massive open online courses: Trends shaping online education
abstract: The development of digital technology has enabled the emergence and expansion of Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), which are transforming education through global accessibility, flexibility, and interactivity. This paper analyzes several platforms, their structure, the role of mentors, and the application of learning analytics. By searching citation databases and using generative artificial intelligence tools, relevant studies in the field were identified as the foundation of the analysis. An analysis of the most prominent MOOC platforms was conducted, with a more detailed comparison between the international platforms Coursera, edX, Future Learn, and the Croatian national platforms Srce and CARNET. The research shows that platforms differ in their use of technology, target groups, and approaches to mentorship, but they share a common goal: to provide accessible and personalized education. Personalized education is maintained through the role of mentors, reflected in communication on forums, AI assistants, and peer interaction. Learning analytics also play an equally important role, enabling precise monitoring of progress and adapting content to the specific needs of individuals. Alongside many advantages, the paper also discusses challenges such as privacy protection and data accuracy, which influence the development of MOOCs.
